questions.q: Which of the following sentences observes the licensing conditions for gapping in a coordinate structure?
questions.a: The manager reviewed the report, and the assistant, the memo.
opts: The manager reviewed the report, and the assistant, the memo.
The manager reviewed the report, and the assistant, quickly.
She said that John likes apples, and Mary, pears.
The director praised the actor, the critic, the script.
questions.solution: Gapping requires that the remnants on each side of the conjunction be of the same syntactic category and that the construction not cross an embedded clause. Option A leaves two direct objects (the report / the memo) after the verb is gapped, satisfying the Parallelism Requirement. Option B pairs a noun phrase with an adverb, violating category identity. Option C attempts gapping across a subordinate clause ("that John likes apples"), which the Coordinate Structure Constraint forbids. Option D lacks a verb altogether, so it is not a gapping structure at all. Therefore only sentence A is grammatical under the licensing rules described in the lesson.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: In which sentence is the negative polarity item "any" correctly licensed?
questions.a: Few students have any idea about the policy.
opts: Few students have any idea about the policy.
A few students have any idea about the policy.
Many students have any idea about the policy.
Some students have any idea about the policy.
questions.solution: Negative polarity items such as "any" are licensed by downward‑entailing operators. The lesson states that "few" (without the article) licenses NPIs, whereas "a few" does not because it is upward‑entailing. "Many" and "some" are also upward‑entailing and therefore cannot license "any". Consequently, only the first sentence, which uses "few", provides a proper licensor for the NPI "any". The other three sentences contain quantifiers that fail the licensing condition, making them ungrammatical in formal English.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Select the paraphrase that reflects the epistemic use of "must".
questions.a: He must be at home; his car is in the driveway.
opts: You must submit the report by Friday.
He must be at home; his car is in the driveway.
We must obey the traffic rules.
They must finish the work before noon.
questions.solution: Epistemic "must" expresses a logical deduction or strong inference about the present or past, whereas deontic "must" conveys obligation. Option B ("He must be at home; his car is in the driveway") shows the speaker inferring a fact from evidence, which is the hallmark of epistemic modality. Options A, C, and D all impose a requirement or duty on the subject, illustrating deontic "must". Hence only option B matches the epistemic reading described in the lesson.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Which sentence places the focus particle "only" to convey that the speaker alone performed the action?
questions.solution: The position of "only" determines which constituent is in focus. When "only" precedes the subject ("Only I"), it asserts that no one other than the speaker performed the action, which is the intended meaning. In option B, "only" modifies the verb, implying the speaker did nothing else but submit. Option C focuses on the object, suggesting the application was the sole thing submitted. Option D, with "only" at the end, ambiguously focuses on the whole predicate. Therefore, only option A correctly encodes the exclusive‑subject reading.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: A garden‑path sentence such as "The horse raced past the barn fell" is initially parsed with "raced" as the main verb. Which of the following corrections restores the intended reduced‑relative‑clause structure and eliminates the garden‑path effect?
questions.solution: The garden‑path arises because the parser treats "raced" as a finite past‑tense verb. The intended reading is a reduced relative clause: "The horse that was raced past the barn fell." Restoring the relative pronoun "that" and the auxiliary "was" (or simply "that was") forces the parser to analyse "raced" as a past participle in a passive relative clause, removing the temporary misanalysis. The other options either change tense, add an inappropriate relative pronoun for a non‑human subject, or delete a necessary determiner, none of which resolve the structural ambiguity.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: In the sentence "He stopped smoking," the change‑of‑state verb "stopped" triggers a presupposition. Which of the following propositions is presupposed (i.e., taken for granted and non‑cancellable) by this utterance?
questions.solution: Change‑of‑state verbs such as "stop," "start," and "begin" presuppose the prior state. "Stop smoking" therefore presupposes that the subject was smoking before the stopping event. This presupposition survives negation ("He didn’t stop smoking" still implies he used to smoke) and cannot be cancelled without contradiction ("He stopped smoking; in fact he never smoked" is incoherent). The other options are either contrary to the presupposition ("never smoked"), refer to future behaviour, or express a desire, none of which are entailed as background assumptions by the verb "stopped."
questions.subject: English

questions.q: In a legal contract the word "consideration" appears. Which sense is intended in this register?
questions.a: something of value exchanged in a contract
opts: something of value exchanged in a contract
questions.solution: The lesson states that in a legal register "consideration" bears a technical sense meaning "something of value exchanged in a contract," overriding its everyday sense of "thoughtful regard." Polysemy allows a single form to have related senses, but register selects the appropriate one. The other options correspond to senses of "bank" (financial institution, river bank, row of switches) and the everyday sense of consideration, which are not the legal technical meaning. Therefore the correct answer is the contractual sense.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Corpus‑informed collocation profiling helps test‑takers avoid which error?
questions.solution: The lesson warns that "Relying on intuition rather than corpus frequency for collocation choices, leading to plausible but non‑standard pairings" is a common pitfall. Corpus‑informed profiling directly addresses this by providing evidence‑based frequent collocations, so candidates do not select combinations that sound acceptable but are unattested in the target register. The other options refer to separate error types (sense disambiguation, register syntax, comparative syntax) that are not solved by collocation profiling.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: In the sentence "Surprisingly, the results suggest a significant correlation," the word "Surprisingly" functions as which metadiscourse marker?
questions.solution: The lesson classifies "attitude markers (unfortunately, surprisingly) reveal evaluation." A hedge lowers commitment (e.g., may, possibly), a booster raises certainty (e.g., clearly, undoubtedly), and a frame marker maps structure (e.g., in the following section). "Surprisingly" expresses the author's evaluative stance toward the proposition, fitting the attitude‑marker category. Therefore the correct classification is attitude marker.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the Entity Concept and the Going Concern Assumption as per fundamental accounting principles?
questions.a: The Entity Concept requires separation of business and owner affairs, while the Going Concern Assumption presumes the entity will continue operating, allowing historical cost valuation.
opts: The Going Concern Assumption is a prerequisite for applying the Entity Concept, as separation of affairs requires perpetual existence.
The Entity Concept requires separation of business and owner affairs, while the Going Concern Assumption presumes the entity will continue operating, allowing historical cost valuation.
Both concepts are interchangeable terms referring to the separation of personal and business transactions for financial reporting purposes.
The Going Concern Assumption overrides the Entity Concept when an entity faces liquidation, requiring immediate revaluation of all assets to realizable value.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the entity concept requires keeping business affairs separate from owners' affairs. The going concern assumption builds on this by presuming the business will continue operating, allowing assets to be recorded at historical cost rather than liquidation value. Option B accurately captures this relationship: entity concept = separation; going concern = continuity presumption enabling historical cost. Option A reverses the dependency. Option C incorrectly calls them interchangeable. Option D misstates that going concern overrides entity concept during liquidation; rather, financial statements must disclose uncertainty and may shift to break-up basis.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the Companies Act, 2013, which basis of accounting is mandatory for corporate entities and why is it preferred over the alternative?
questions.a: Accrual basis, because it recognizes revenues when earned and expenses when incurred, observing the matching principle and enhancing comparability.
opts: Cash basis, because it provides a more faithful representation of financial performance by matching income with the period of economic activity.
Accrual basis, because it records transactions only when cash is received or paid, enhancing comparability across periods.
Accrual basis, because it recognizes revenues when earned and expenses when incurred, observing the matching principle and enhancing comparability.
Cash basis, because it is mandated for companies and aligns with the matching principle by recognizing obligations when settled.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states: "Most statutory frameworks, including the Companies Act, 2013, mandate the accrual basis for corporate entities because it aligns with the matching principle and enhances comparability across periods." The comparison table confirms accrual basis observes matching principle while cash basis does not. Option C correctly identifies accrual basis as mandatory and gives the correct reasoning (revenues when earned, expenses when incurred, matching principle observed). Option A incorrectly attributes matching to cash basis. Option B misstates accrual basis as recording only when cash changes hands. Option D incorrectly states cash basis is mandated.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the context of insurance contracts, the Principle of Utmost Good Faith (Uberrimae Fidei) and the requirement of Insurable Interest operate at which stages respectively?
questions.a: Utmost Good Faith applies at inception and during the policy; Insurable Interest must exist at inception for life insurance and at both inception and claim for general insurance.
opts: Utmost Good Faith applies only at claim settlement; Insurable Interest must exist only at policy inception.
Both principles apply continuously throughout the policy period without any distinction in timing.
Utmost Good Faith applies at inception and during the policy; Insurable Interest must exist at inception for life insurance and at both inception and claim for general insurance.
Utmost Good Faith is a statutory requirement under the Insurance Act, 1938, while Insurable Interest is merely a common law principle with no statutory backing.
questions.solution: While the lesson mentions "Principle of Utmost Good Faith and Insurable Interest" as core concepts, it does not explicitly detail their timing differences. However, based on standard insurance law knowledge tested in UPSC: Utmost Good Faith applies at inception and continues during the policy (duty of disclosure). Insurable Interest for life insurance must exist at inception only; for general insurance (indemnity contracts), it must exist at both inception and claim. Option C reflects this established legal distinction. Option A is incorrect on both counts. Option B ignores the critical timing difference for insurable interest. Option D is factually wrong as both have statutory recognition.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a power or function of IRDAI as described in the regulatory framework for insurance in India?
questions.a: Setting the statutory ceiling for EDLI benefits and determining the employer contribution rate for EPS.
opts: Prescribing required solvency margins that vary by line of business using a risk-based capital approach.
Approving the transfer of shares beyond prescribed thresholds and supervising appointment of key managerial personnel.
Setting the statutory ceiling for EDLI benefits and determining the employer contribution rate for EPS.
Conducting on-site inspections and off-site monitoring to detect early signs of distress in insurers.
questions.solution: The lesson lists IRDAI's powers: prescribing solvency margins (risk-based capital approach), supervising appointment of key managerial personnel, approving share transfers beyond thresholds, and conducting on-site/off-site monitoring. However, setting EDLI benefit ceilings and EPS contribution rates falls under EPFO-specific provisions governed by the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and related schemes, not IRDAI. EDLI and EPS are administered by EPFO, not regulated by IRDAI as insurance products. Options A, B, and D are explicitly mentioned as IRDAI functions in section 4.2 and 4.3. Option C describes EPFO scheme parameters, not IRDAI powers.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding the actuarial valuation of EPFO's liabilities for EDLI and EPS, which method is used and what is the primary purpose of the valuation results?
questions.a: Projected Unit Credit Method; to determine the present value of future benefit obligations and guide allocation of investment income between provident fund corpus and insurance reserves.
opts: Projected Unit Credit Method; to determine the present value of future benefit obligations and guide allocation of investment income between provident fund corpus and insurance reserves.
Current Unit Credit Method; to calculate the required solvency margin for EPFO as mandated by IRDAI regulations.
Aggregate Cost Method; to assess the fund's compliance with Investment Regulations under the Insurance Act, 1938.
Attained Age Normal Method; to fix the statutory interest rate credited to members' accounts annually.
questions.solution: Section 5.3 explicitly states: "Actuarial valuation of the EPFO's liabilities is conducted annually by an appointed actuary using the projected unit credit method. The valuation determines the present value of future benefit obligations under EDLI and EPS... The results guide the allocation of the fund's investment income between the provident fund corpus and the insurance reserves." Option A matches this exactly. Option B incorrectly names the method and purpose (solvency margin is IRDAI for insurers, not EPFO). Option C uses wrong method and purpose. Option D uses wrong method; interest rate crediting is mentioned as a possible outcome of surplus, not the primary purpose of valuation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under Ind AS 19, which method is required to measure the defined‑benefit obligation for a plan such as the Employees’ Pension Scheme?
questions.solution: Ind AS 19 mandates the projected unit credit method (PUCM) for all defined‑benefit plans. PUCM treats each period of service as generating an additional unit of benefit entitlement and discounts the expected future benefit payments to determine the present value of the obligation. The accrued benefit method is not permitted under Ind AS 19, while current and past service costs are components of expense recognition, not valuation methods.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Where does Ind AS 19 require actuarial gains and losses arising from changes in assumptions to be recognised?
questions.solution: Ind AS 19 stipulates that remeasurements of the net defined‑benefit liability — comprising actuarial gains and losses from changes in demographic or financial assumptions — are recognised immediately in other comprehensive income (OCI) and are not subsequently recycled to profit or loss. Only the net interest cost, current service cost, past service cost and settlement/curtailment gains or losses are routed through profit or loss.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to Ind AS 113, Level 1 inputs in the fair‑value hierarchy are defined as:
questions.a: Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets
opts: Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets
Observable inputs other than quoted prices
Unobservable inputs developed by the entity
Model‑based estimates using significant unobservable data
questions.solution: Ind AS 113 establishes a three‑level hierarchy. Level 1 inputs are quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the entity can access at the measurement date. Level 2 inputs are observable either directly or indirectly (other than Level 1), and Level 3 inputs are unobservable. Therefore, quoted prices in active markets for identical assets constitute Level 1.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: When development factors are volatile, which loss‑reserving method is generally preferred over the chain‑ladder method?
questions.solution: The chain‑ladder method relies on stable historical development factors; if those factors are volatile, its projections become unreliable. The Bornhuetter‑Ferguson method blends the reported experience with an a priori expected loss ratio, providing more stable reserve estimates for volatile lines. Hence, Bornhuetter‑Ferguson is the preferred approach when development factors lack stability.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The 2022 amendment to the Employees’ Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 permitted the Central Board of Trustees to invest up to what percentage of the incremental corpus in equity‑linked exchange‑traded funds?
questions.solution: The 2022 amendment (notified 3 March 2022) revised the investment limits for the EPFO corpus, allowing the Central Board of Trustees to allocate up to 15% of the incremental corpus to exchange‑traded funds tracking the Nifty 50 and Sensex. This raised the previous ceiling of 5% and introduced equity exposure into the predominantly sovereign‑bond portfolio.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY), what is the health‑care coverage limit provided per family per year?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that PMJAY "seeks to provide secondary and tertiary health‑care coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year to over 10 crore poor households". Option B matches this figure exactly. Options A, C, and D are incorrect amounts not mentioned in the scheme description.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the comparative overview of the National Solar Mission and the National Hydrogen Mission, which incentive mechanism is associated with the National Hydrogen Mission?
questions.solution: The comparison table in section 6.5 lists "Production‑linked incentive (PLI) scheme" as the Key Incentive for the National Hydrogen Mission (launched 2021), while the National Solar Mission (2010) uses "Capital subsidy & accelerated depreciation". Therefore, option B is the correct incentive for the Hydrogen Mission.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the primary objective of the National Digital Health Mission (NDHM) launched in response to the COVID‑19 pandemic?
questions.a: To create a digital health ecosystem
opts: To manufacture indigenous vaccines like Covaxin
To create a digital health ecosystem
To increase funding for the National Centre for Disease Control
To provide cash assistance to frontline health workers
questions.solution: The lesson states: "the government launched the National Digital Health Mission (NDHM), which aims to create a digital health ecosystem". This is the explicitly stated objective. Option A refers to Covaxin development, which demonstrated self‑reliance but is separate from NDHM. Option C mentions increased NCDC funding, a parallel measure. Option D is not mentioned in the lesson.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following outcomes was explicitly recorded in the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration adopted during India's G20 Presidency in September 2023?
questions.a: Tripling global renewable energy capacity by 2030 and phasing down unabated coal power
opts: A new quantified climate-finance target replacing the $100 billion annual goal
Tripling global renewable energy capacity by 2030 and phasing down unabated coal power
Establishment of a permanent G20 secretariat in New Delhi with binding dispute-resolution powers
Mandatory adoption of India's UPI stack by all G20 member nations by 2025
questions.solution: The New Delhi Leaders' Declaration recorded consensus on tripling global renewable energy capacity by 2030 and phasing down unabated coal power, along with launching the Global Biofuels Alliance. The text explicitly states the final text retained the existing $100 billion climate-finance target without a new quantified commitment. The G20 Secretariat remains in the Ministry of External Affairs for archival purposes, not as a binding dispute-resolution body. UPI was cited as a reference implementation in the Digital Economy Ministers' Declaration, but mandatory adoption by all members was not agreed upon.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding India's Digital Public Infrastructure, which of the following statements is correct?
questions.a: The Account Aggregator framework, regulated by RBI since 2021, enables consent-based financial data sharing across regulated entities
opts: The Account Aggregator framework is regulated by NPCI and enables consent-based sharing of financial data
ONDC was launched nationwide in April 2022 and onboards sellers through a centralised marketplace model
The Account Aggregator framework, regulated by RBI since 2021, enables consent-based financial data sharing across regulated entities
UPI's global ranking is determined solely by transaction volume, with interoperability being irrelevant
questions.solution: The Account Aggregator (AA) framework has been regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) since 2021, not NPCI. It enables consent-based sharing of financial data across banks, insurers, and fintechs. ONDC was launched in pilot mode across five cities in April 2022 (not nationwide) and aims to democratise e-commerce by unbundling discovery, ordering, and fulfilment (not a centralised marketplace). UPI's global standing considers value, interoperability, and merchant acceptance, not volume alone.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes a feature of India's Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs) framework and the domestic Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)?
questions.a: SGrB framework aligns with ICMA Green Bond Principles; CCTS establishes a compliance market for PAT-covered entities
opts: SGrB proceeds can be used for fossil fuel efficiency projects; CCTS allows voluntary participation by any corporate entity
SGrB framework aligns with ICMA Green Bond Principles; CCTS establishes a compliance market for PAT-covered entities
The first SGrB issuance in January 2023 raised ₹36,000 crore; CCTS auction mechanisms were fully operationalised by June 2023
SGrBs are issued under RBI's Green Deposits Framework; CCTS credits are internationally transferable under Article 6.2
questions.solution: The Sovereign Green Bond Framework (approved November 2022) aligns with ICMA Green Bond Principles and earmarks proceeds for renewable energy, energy efficiency, pollution prevention, sustainable agriculture, and clean transportation — not fossil fuel projects. The first issuance in January 2023 raised ₹16,000 crore (cumulative reached ₹36,000 crore by March 2024). The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), notified June 2023, establishes a domestic compliance market for entities under the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme; operational details including auction mechanisms were still being finalised as of the lesson period. The RBI's Green Deposits Framework (April 2023) is separate from SGrBs.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the India Semiconductor Mission's Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, what is the maximum fiscal support offered for a greenfield semiconductor fabrication plant, and what is the per-project cap?
questions.a: 50% of project cost, capped at ₹12,000 crore
opts: 50% of project cost, capped at ₹12,000 crore
30% of project cost, capped at ₹12,000 crore
50% of project cost, capped at ₹76,000 crore
40% of project cost, capped at ₹15,000 crore
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'The PLI offers fiscal support of up to 50% of project cost for greenfield fabs and 30% for brownfield expansions, capped at ₹12,000 crore per project.' Option A correctly captures both the percentage (50%) and the cap (₹12,000 crore). Option B gives the brownfield percentage. Option C confuses the per-project cap with the total mission outlay of ₹76,000 crore. Option D invents figures not mentioned in the text.

questions.q: In the structure of the National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (NARCL) and India Debt Resolution Company Ltd (IDRCL), which entity acquires stressed assets above ₹500 crore at a 15% cash-upfront and 85% security receipts structure?
questions.solution: The text explicitly states: 'NARCL, capitalised at ₹6,000 crore with a government guarantee of ₹30,600 crore, acquires stressed assets above ₹500 crore at a 15% cash-upfront and 85% security receipts structure. IDRCL, a private-sector-led asset manager, handles resolution and value maximisation.' Thus, NARCL is the acquiring entity. IDRCL manages resolution. FSIB replaced the Banks Board Bureau for senior appointments and is unrelated to asset acquisition.

questions.q: According to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, which of the following statements accurately describes the data transfer mechanism and the nature of the Data Protection Board?
questions.a: The Act permits transfers to notified trusted jurisdictions; the Data Protection Board is an adjudicatory body.
opts: The Act mandates strict data localisation; the Data Protection Board is a regulatory authority.
The Act permits transfers to notified trusted jurisdictions; the Data Protection Board is an adjudicatory body.
The Act requires all personal data to be stored in India; the Data Protection Board functions under the Ministry of Electronics and IT.
The Act allows unrestricted cross-border data flows; the Data Protection Board has rule-making powers.
questions.solution: The lesson's 'common misconceptions' section clarifies: 'Assuming the DPDP Act mandates data localisation; it only requires transfers to notified trusted jurisdictions' and 'Overlooking that the Data Protection Board under the DPDP Act is an adjudicatory body, not a regulatory authority.' Option B matches both corrections. Options A, C, and D each contain at least one incorrect assertion about localisation, storage requirements, or the Board's powers.

questions.q: Which of the following accurately describes the funding sources of the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC) and India's access to the Green Climate Fund (GCF)?
questions.a: NAFCC corpus comes from the central budget enhanced to ₹1,000 crore and also receives bilateral and multilateral grants; India accesses GCF through accredited entities like NABARD, SIDBI, and IREDA.
opts: NAFCC is financed solely by the central budget; India accesses GCF directly without accredited entities.
NAFCC receives only bilateral grants; India accesses GCF through the Reserve Bank of India as the sole accredited entity.
NAFCC corpus comes from the central budget enhanced to ₹1,000 crore and also receives bilateral and multilateral grants; India accesses GCF through accredited entities like NABARD, SIDBI, and IREDA.
NAFCC is funded entirely by the Adaptation Fund; India's GCF projects are limited to mitigation only.
questions.solution: The lesson states NAFCC was 'established in 2015-16 with a corpus of ₹350 crore, later enhanced to ₹1,000 crore in the 2021-22 budget' and the misconceptions list notes: 'Believing the National Adaptation Fund is financed solely by the central budget; it also receives bilateral and multilateral grants.' Regarding GCF: 'India accesses the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and the Adaptation Fund (AF) through accredited entities such as NABARD, SIDBI, and the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA).' Option C correctly combines both facts. Options A, B, and D each contain factual errors about funding sources or GCF access mechanisms.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the total financial outlay approved for the National Green Hydrogen Mission and its targeted annual green hydrogen production capacity by 2030?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Union Cabinet approved the National Green Hydrogen Mission on 4 January 2023 with a total outlay of ₹19,744 crore for the period 2023‑24 to 2029‑30 and aims for an annual production capacity of 5 million metric tonnes (MMT) by 2030. Only option A matches both figures.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under which of the four labour codes is the statutory floor wage provision introduced?
opts: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that the Code on Wages introduces a statutory floor wage fixed by the central government (initially ₹178 per day) below which no state minimum wage can be set. The other codes deal with industrial relations, social security, and occupational safety, not the floor wage.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the primary role of IN‑SPACe in India's space sector reforms?
questions.a: Authorises and facilitates access to ISRO facilities
opts: Authorises and facilitates access to ISRO facilities
questions.solution: According to the lesson, IN‑SPACe only authorises and facilitates access to ISRO facilities; it does not directly operate launch vehicles, manufacture satellites, or regulate foreign investment. Hence option B correctly describes its role.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What percentage of polling stations does the Supreme Court mandate for VVPAT verification in each constituency?
questions.solution: The lesson notes that the Supreme Court mandated only a 5% random sample of polling stations per constituency for VVPAT verification, not 100% or any other figure. Therefore option B is the correct statement.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The consent‑manager framework of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is modelled on which architecture?
questions.solution: The lesson states that data governance under ABDM rests on a consent‑manager framework modelled on the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA). The DPDP Act, Aadhaar Act, and National Health Policy are separate legal bases and not the model for ABDM's consent manager.

questions.q: Regarding the Ken‑Betwa river interlinking project, which of the following is factually accurate based on the National Perspective Plan?
questions.a: It links the Ken and Betwa rivers, both of which are tributaries of the Yamuna sub‑basin.
opts: It transfers water across major basin boundaries, connecting the Ganga and Yamuna basins.
It links the Ken and Betwa rivers, both of which are tributaries of the Yamuna sub‑basin.
It is the only Himalayan component link approved under the National Perspective Plan.
It follows a 60:40 Centre‑state funding ratio applicable to centrally sponsored schemes.

Thus, the Ken and Betwa are both tributaries of the Yamuna. Option A is incorrect because it does not cross major basin boundaries. Option C is wrong as Ken‑Betwa is a peninsular link, not Himalayan. questions.q: What is the current status of the Nuclear Safety Regulatory Authority (NSRA) Bill and its effect on the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB)?
questions.a: The NSRA Bill is pending in Parliament, so the AERB continues as the functional regulator under executive orders.
opts: The NSRA Bill has been enacted, and the AERB has been dissolved.
The NSRA Bill is pending in Parliament, so the AERB continues as the functional regulator under executive orders.
The NSRA Bill was withdrawn, and the AERB has been granted statutory independence via an executive order.
The NSRA Bill has been passed by the Lok Sabha but awaits Rajya Sabha approval; the AERB operates in an interim capacity.

Until enactment, the AERB continues to operate under executive orders.' This makes option B the only accurate description. Options A, C, and D invent legislative progress or status changes not supported by the text.
