questions.q: Which of the following is included in the domestic territory of India as per national income accounting conventions?
opts: Foreign embassies located in New Delhi
Territorial waters of a neighbouring country
questions.solution: The domestic territory of India includes political frontiers, territorial waters, airspace, and Indian embassies, consulates, and military establishments located abroad. It explicitly excludes foreign embassies and international organisations located within India. Therefore, Indian military establishments abroad are part of the domestic territory, while foreign embassies and international organisations in India are not.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the GDP deflator and the Consumer Price Index (CPI): 1. The GDP deflator uses a fixed basket of goods and services. 2. The CPI automatically adjusts its basket every year to reflect the changing composition of output. 3. The GDP deflator covers all domestically produced goods and services. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: The GDP deflator is the ratio of Nominal GDP to Real GDP multiplied by 100. Unlike the CPI, which uses a fixed basket of consumption items, the GDP deflator automatically adjusts its basket every year to reflect the changing composition of output. It covers all domestically produced goods and services, making it a broader measure. Thus, statement 1 is false (it describes CPI), statement 2 is false (it describes the GDP deflator), and statement 3 is true.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Profits earned by a foreign-owned factory operating in Gujarat are included in India's GDP but not in its GNP. Wages earned by an Indian engineer working in Dubai are included in India's GNP but not in its GDP. Which concept explains this difference?
questions.solution: Gross National Product (GNP) equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad (factor income earned by residents from overseas minus factor income paid to non-residents domestically). The foreign-owned factory's profits are factor income paid to non-residents within the domestic territory, so they are in GDP but excluded from GNP via negative net factor income from abroad. The Indian engineer's wages are factor income earned by a resident from abroad, added to GDP to arrive at GNP. This difference is precisely captured by net factor income from abroad.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to poverty estimation methodologies in India, consider the following statements: 1. The Tendulkar Committee (2009) adopted a uniform poverty line basket across rural and urban areas. 2. The Rangarajan Committee (2014) recommended lower expenditure thresholds than the Tendulkar Committee. 3. The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) introduced by NITI Aayog in 2021 uses twelve indicators across health, education, and living standards. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: The Tendulkar Committee shifted to a mixed basket of food, education, health, and transport and used a uniform poverty line basket across rural and urban areas (statement 1 correct). The Rangarajan Committee recommended higher expenditure thresholds, not lower, and separate rural-urban baskets (statement 2 incorrect). The NITI Aayog introduced the MPI in 2021 aligned with the global MPI, measuring deprivations across health, education, and living standards using twelve indicators (statement 3 correct). Thus, statements 1 and 3 are correct.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the Fifteenth Finance Commission (2020-25), consider the following statements: 1. It recommended a vertical devolution share of 42 per cent for States, same as the Fourteenth Finance Commission. 2. Its horizontal devolution formula assigned the highest weight to income distance at 45 per cent. 3. It introduced performance-based incentives for health, education, and local-body grants. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is incorrect. The 15th Finance Commission reduced the vertical devolution share to 41 per cent from the 42 per cent recommended by the 14th Commission, primarily because the GST compensation cess altered the revenue base. Statement 2 is correct. The horizontal formula weights were: 45 per cent to income distance, 15 per cent to population (2011 Census), 15 per cent to area, 10 per cent to forest and ecology, 12.5 per cent to demographic performance, and 2.5 per cent to tax effort. Statement 3 is correct. The Commission introduced performance-based incentives for health, education, and local-body grants, and recommended a debt-relief framework for States with high debt-to-GSDP ratios. Therefore, statements 2 and 3 are correct.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) and its pre-packaged insolvency resolution process, which of the following statements is correct?
questions.a: It applies only to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and not to large corporates.
opts: It applies to all corporate debtors irrespective of size, including large corporates.
It was introduced in 2019 as part of the original IBC framework.
It applies only to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and not to large corporates.
It allows creditors to initiate resolution without any threshold of default amount.
questions.solution: The lesson text explicitly states under 'Common Mistakes': 'Overlooking that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code's pre-packaged process applies only to MSMEs, not to large corporates.' This is a specific design feature to provide a faster, less disruptive resolution mechanism for smaller enterprises. The pre-packaged framework was introduced later (in 2021 via ordinance), not in the original 2016 IBC. It also has specific thresholds and procedural requirements distinct from the general Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP). Therefore, the correct statement is that it applies only to MSMEs.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Consider the following statements about agricultural price policy in India: 1. Since 2018-19, the Minimum Support Price (MSP) is fixed at 1.5 times the A2+FL cost of production. 2. The Price Support Scheme (PSS) under PM-AASHA covers procurement of oilseeds, pulses, and copra at MSP. 3. The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020 and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020 are currently in force. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct. The lesson states: 'Since 2018-19, MSP = A2+FL cost plus 50 per cent margin,' which equals 1.5 times the A2+FL cost. Statement 2 is correct. PM-AASHA comprises the Price Support Scheme (PSS) for physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds, and copra at MSP through central nodal agencies. Statement 3 is incorrect. The lesson explicitly mentions: 'Recent legislative changes — the Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act 2020 and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act 2020 — were repealed in 2021 after widespread farmer protests.' Thus, only statements 1 and 2 are correct.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) launched in August 2021, which of the following statements is correct?
questions.a: It targets asset monetisation of ₹6 lakh crore over FY2022-25 through leasing revenue rights via InvITs and REITs.
opts: It involves transfer of ownership of core public assets like roads and railways to private entities.
It targets asset monetisation of ₹6 lakh crore over FY2022-25 through leasing revenue rights via InvITs and REITs.
It is limited to the roads and railways sectors only.
It replaces the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for infrastructure projects.
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'The National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP), unveiled in August 2021, targets asset monetisation of ₹6 lakh crore over FY2022-25 across roads, railways, power, telecom, and warehousing. Core assets remain under public ownership; revenue rights are leased to private operators through InvITs (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) and REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts).' Option 1 is incorrect because ownership is not transferred. Option 3 is incorrect as NMP covers multiple sectors beyond roads and railways. Option 4 is incorrect; NMP complements but does not replace VGF, which supports commercially unviable but socially essential projects. Budget 2024-25 further expanded NMP scope to include gas pipelines and stadiums.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) established under the Finance Act 2016, consider the following statements: 1. The MPC consists of six members, including three external members appointed by the government for a four‑year term. 2. Decisions are taken by consensus; the Governor does not have a casting vote. 3. The committee is required to meet at least four times a year and publish its resolution after a 14‑day lag. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct: the MPC has six members — the Governor (chair), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer nominated by the Central Board, and three external members appointed by the government for a four‑year term. Statement 2 is incorrect because decisions are taken by majority vote and the Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie. Statement 3 is correct: the MPC meets at least four times a year and its resolution, including the policy repo rate, is published with the minutes after a 14‑day lag. Therefore, only statements 1 and 3 are correct.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The 15th Finance Commission (Chair: N. K. Singh) recommended a vertical devolution of net proceeds of Union taxes to states for the award period 2021‑26. What was the percentage fixed for vertical devolution?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 15th Finance Commission, constituted in 2017, submitted its report for the award period 2021‑26 and fixed vertical devolution at 41 percent of the divisible pool, unchanged from the previous commission. Hence the correct figure is 41 percent.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Debt Management Office (DMO) was established in 2022 to centralise cash management, issuance calendar coordination, and investor relations for the Centre and willing states. On whose recommendation was the DMO set up?
questions.a: FRBM Review Committee (2017, Chair: N. K. Singh)
opts: FRBM Review Committee (2017, Chair: N. K. Singh)
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Review Committee (2017, Chair: N. K. Singh) recommended the establishment of an independent Debt Management Office. The DMO was subsequently set up in 2022 under the Department of Economic Affairs. It was not created by any Finance Commission.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the Fifteenth Finance Commission (2020‑25), consider the following statements: 1. It retained the States' share in the divisible pool at 41 per cent. 2. It assigned a 1 per cent weight to demographic performance to reward States that have controlled population growth. 3. It recommended a combined debt‑to‑GDP target of 60 per cent by 2025‑26 for the Centre and States together. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct: the Fifteenth Finance Commission kept the vertical devolution at 41 % (adjusted for the new Union Territories). Statement 2 is correct: the Commission introduced a 1 % weight for demographic performance to incentivise population control. Statement 3 is correct: the Commission’s fiscal consolidation roadmap targets a combined debt‑to‑GDP ratio of 60 % by 2025‑26. All three statements are supported by the lesson text.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Regarding the horizontal devolution formula used by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, consider the following statements: 1. The income distance criterion accounts for roughly 45 per cent of the weight. 2. Forest cover and ecology receive a 10 per cent weight. 3. The Commission continued to use the 1971 Census population base for horizontal devolution. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct: income distance remains the dominant equalising factor with about 45 % weight. Statement 2 is correct: forest cover and ecology are assigned a 10 % weight. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Fifteenth Commission shifted to the 2011 Census base, abandoning the 1971 population base used until the Fourteenth Commission. Hence only statements 1 and 2 are correct.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the implementation of Finance Commission recommendations and the GST Council: 1. The recommendations of the Finance Commission become effective automatically upon submission. 2. The Union government accepts the recommendations through a presidential order. 3. The GST Council is a constitutional body that decides GST rates and compensation. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is false: Finance Commission recommendations require acceptance by the Union government via a presidential order; they are not automatic. Statement 2 is true: the President’s order gives effect to the recommendations. Statement 3 is true: the GST Council, a constitutional body under Article 279A, determines GST rates, exemptions and the compensation mechanism. Therefore, statements 2 and 3 are correct.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commissions, consider the following statements: 1. The Fourteenth Finance Commission introduced a performance‑based grant component for local bodies. 2. The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended a separate grant for health, education, and disaster relief. 3. The Fifteenth Finance Commission set a fiscal consolidation roadmap targeting a combined debt‑to‑GDP ratio of 60 per cent by 2025‑26. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct: the Fourteenth Commission added a performance‑based grant for local bodies. Statement 2 is correct: the Fifteenth Commission earmarked a distinct grant for health, education and disaster relief. Statement 3 is correct: the Fifteenth Commission’s fiscal consolidation roadmap aims at a combined debt‑to‑GDP of 60 % by 2025‑26. All three statements are supported by the lesson.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What specific measure did the RBI introduce to accelerate the transmission of the policy repo rate to bank lending rates?
questions.a: External benchmark linking of floating‑rate loans such as the repo‑linked lending rate (RLLR).
opts: Introduction of the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) in 2022.
External benchmark linking of floating‑rate loans such as the repo‑linked lending rate (RLLR).
Conduct of variable rate reverse repo auctions (VRRR) for fine‑tuning liquidity.
Open Market Operations termed "Operation Twist" involving purchases of short‑dated securities.
questions.solution: The lesson notes that transmission in India has been incomplete, with lending rates adjusting with a lag. To address this, the RBI introduced external benchmark linking of floating‑rate loans (e.g., repo‑linked lending rate, RLLR) to accelerate transmission. The SDF, VRRR auctions, and Operation Twist are liquidity management tools; Operation Twist specifically targeted long‑dated securities to compress the term premium, not to speed up lending‑rate pass‑through. Hence, the correct measure is the external benchmark linking described in option B.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In India, the inflation target under the flexible inflation‑targeting framework is set by which authority?
questions.a: The Government of India in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India.
opts: The Reserve Bank of India acting alone.
The Government of India in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India.
The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) by majority vote.
The Finance Commission during its five‑year review.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that the inflation target is set by the Government in consultation with the RBI, not by the RBI alone, the MPC, or the Finance Commission. The MPC is responsible for achieving the target through policy rate decisions, while the Finance Commission deals with fiscal devolution. Hence, option B correctly identifies the authority that sets the inflation target.

questions.q: Which entity operates the central switch that settles Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions?

It further clarifies that NPCI acts as the settlement layer (central switch) for UPI transactions, enabling instant, 24×7, interoperable fund transfers. The RBI regulates the payments system, the Indian Banks' Association is an industry body, and the Ministry of Finance handles fiscal policy. Therefore, option B correctly identifies NPCI as the operator of the UPI central switch.

questions.q: When was the first sovereign green bond issued by the Government of India?

questions.q: If a³ - b³ = 56 and a - b = 2, find ab.
questions.solution: a³-b³ = (a-b)(a²+ab+b²) = 2(a²+ab+b²) = 56 => a²+ab+b² = 28. Also (a-b)² = a²-2ab+b² = 4. Subtracting: (a²+ab+b²)-(a²-2ab+b²)=28-4 => 3ab=24 => ab=8.

questions.q: A sphere of radius 10 cm is cut by a plane at a distance of 6 cm from its centre. What is the volume of the resulting spherical cap?
questions.solution: The cap height H = r − h = 10 − 6 = 4 cm. The volume formula for a spherical cap is V = π H² (r − H/3). Substituting H = 4 and r = 10 gives r − H/3 = 10 − 4/3 = 26/3. Then V = π × 16 × (26/3) = (416/3)π cm³. This matches option A.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A right circular cylinder is inscribed in a sphere of radius 7 cm. What is the ratio of the total surface area of the cylinder to the surface area of the sphere?
questions.solution: For an inscribed cylinder, height = 2r = 14 cm and radius = r = 7 cm. Cylinder total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2π(49) + 2π(7)(14) = 98π + 196π = 294π. Sphere surface area = 4πr² = 4π(49) = 196π. Ratio = 294π / 196π = 3/2. Hence option A is correct.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A closed cylindrical can must have a fixed total surface area of 300π cm². What radius maximizes its volume?
questions.solution: Surface area S = 2πr² + 2πrh = 300π ⇒ h = (300π − 2πr²)/(2πr) = (150 − r²)/r. Volume V = πr²h = πr(150 − r²) = 150πr − πr³. dV/dr = 150π − 3πr² = 0 ⇒ r² = 50 ⇒ r = √50 = 5√2 cm. This gives maximum volume. Option A is correct.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A point is chosen uniformly at random inside a sphere of radius 6 cm. What is the probability that the point lies within a concentric sphere of radius 2 cm?
questions.solution: Probability = volume of inner sphere / volume of outer sphere = (4/3 π (2)³) / (4/3 π (6)³) = 8 / 216 = 1/27. Option A is correct.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: Four collinear points A, B, C, D have directed distances AB = 2, BC = 3, CD = 4. The cross ratio (AC/BC) ÷ (AD/BD) equals:
questions.solution: AC = AB + BC = 5, BC = 3, AD = AB + BC + CD = 9, BD = BC + CD = 7. Cross ratio = (AC/BC) / (AD/BD) = (5/3) / (9/7) = (5/3) * (7/9) = 35/27. The invariance of cross ratio under projection makes this value unchanged if the four points are projected from a pencil of lines.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: In triangle ABC, the side lengths are a = 13, b = 14, c = 15. The incenter I has barycentric coordinates proportional to (a, b, c). What are the normalized barycentric coordinates of I (i.e., α+β+γ = 1)?
questions.solution: The barycentric coordinates of the incenter are proportional to the side lengths a, b, c. Here a=13, b=14, c=15. The sum is 13+14+15 = 42. Normalizing so that α+β+γ = 1 gives α = 13/42, β = 14/42, γ = 15/42. This matches the first option. The other options use incorrect sums (40, 39, 41) and therefore do not satisfy the normalization condition.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A needle of length 4 cm is dropped on a floor ruled with parallel lines 7 cm apart. Assuming the needle length is less than the line spacing, the probability that the needle crosses a line is given by 2ℓ/(πd). What is this probability?
questions.solution: Buffon's needle formula for ℓ ≤ d is P = 2ℓ/(πd). Substituting ℓ = 4 cm and d = 7 cm gives P = 2×4/(π×7) = 8/(7π). This matches the third option. The first option omits the factor 2, the second uses d=1, and the fourth inverts the fraction incorrectly.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: Using Cavalieri's principle, the volume of a hemisphere of radius R is 2/3 πR³. What is the volume of a hemisphere with radius 6 cm?
questions.solution: The volume formula for a hemisphere is V = (2/3)πR³. For R = 6 cm, R³ = 216. Then V = (2/3)π × 216 = 144π cm³. This corresponds to the fourth option. The first option is (1/3)πR³, the second is (4/3)πR³ (full sphere), and the third is πR³.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A company's profit margin rises from 15% to 18%. By what percent did the profit margin increase?
questions.solution: The increase in percentage points is 18% - 15% = 3 percentage points. Percent increase is calculated relative to the original margin: ((18 - 15) / 15) * 100 = (3/15)*100 = 20%. The phrase "by what percent" asks for the relative change, not the point difference. Hence the correct answer is 20%.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: After a 25% increase, the price of an article becomes Rs 250. What was its original price?
questions.solution: Let the original price be x. A 25% increase means the final price = x * (1 + 25/100) = 1.25x. Given 1.25x = 250, so x = 250 / 1.25 = 200. Therefore the original price was Rs 200.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A shopkeeper sells 900 grams of goods as 1 kilogram at the cost price. What is his profit percent?
questions.solution: The shopkeeper gives 900 g but charges for 1000 g. Cost price of 900 g = CP of 900 g. Selling price = CP of 1000 g. Profit = CP of (1000 - 900) = CP of 100 g. Profit percent = (Profit / CP of 900 g) * 100 = (100/900)*100 = 100/9 ≈ 11.11%.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A factory operates two shifts. Shift A has 120 workers with an average daily output of 85 units. Shift B has 80 workers with an average daily output of 92 units. What is the overall average daily output per worker for the factory?
questions.solution: The combined mean is the weighted average of the two shifts. Total output = (120 × 85) + (80 × 92) = 10200 + 7360 = 17560 units. Total workers = 120 + 80 = 200. Overall average = 17560 / 200 = 87.8 units per worker.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: The mean height of a group of students is 165 cm with a standard deviation of 9 cm. Their mean weight is 55 kg with a standard deviation of 6 kg. Which statement about relative variability is correct?
opts: Both have the same relative variability.
questions.solution: Coefficient of variation (CV) = (σ/μ)×100%. For heights: CV = (9/165)×100 ≈ 5.45%. For weights: CV = (6/55)×100 ≈ 10.91%. Since 10.91% > 5.45%, weights exhibit greater relative variability than heights.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A machine produces 5% defective items. If a random sample of 20 items is inspected, what is the probability that exactly 2 items are defective?
questions.solution: This is a binomial experiment with n = 20, p = 0.05. P(X = 2) = C(20,2) × (0.05)² × (0.95)¹⁸ = 190 × 0.0025 × 0.95¹⁸. 0.95¹⁸ ≈ 0.397. Product = 190 × 0.0009925 ≈ 0.1886, which rounds to 0.188.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: The lifetime of an electronic component follows an exponential distribution with a mean of 50 hours. Given that the component has already operated for 20 hours, what is the probability that it will operate for at least 50 additional hours?
questions.solution: The exponential distribution has the memoryless property: P(T > s + t | T > s) = P(T > t). Here, s = 20 hours and additional time t = 50 hours. The required probability is P(T > 50). For an exponential distribution with mean 50, rate λ = 1/50. P(T > 50) = e^(-λ * 50) = e^(-50/50) = e^(-1) ≈ 0.3679. Option A is correct. Option B (0.6321) is P(T ≤ 50), the complement.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: Two independent samples are drawn from normal populations with equal variances. Sample 1: n₁ = 10, mean = 15, s₁ = 3. Sample 2: n₂ = 10, mean = 12, s₂ = 3. What is the value of the pooled t-test statistic for testing equality of means?
questions.solution: First, compute the pooled variance: sₚ² = [(n₁-1)s₁² + (n₂-1)s₂²] / (n₁+n₂-2) = [9(9) + 9(9)] / 18 = 162/18 = 9. So sₚ = 3. The standard error of the difference is sₚ × √(1/n₁ + 1/n₂) = 3 × √(0.1 + 0.1) = 3 × √0.2 ≈ 3 × 0.4472 = 1.3416. The t-statistic = (15 - 12) / 1.3416 ≈ 2.236. Rounding to two decimal places gives 2.24, matching option A.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: In a random sample of 400 voters, 220 support a candidate. What is the margin of error for a 95% confidence interval for the population proportion? (Use z₀.₀₂₅ = 1.96)
questions.solution: Sample proportion p̂ = 220/400 = 0.55. Standard error = √[p̂(1-p̂)/n] = √[(0.55 × 0.45)/400] = √[0.2475/400] = √0.00061875 ≈ 0.02487. Margin of error = z × SE = 1.96 × 0.02487 ≈ 0.04875. Rounding to three decimal places gives 0.049. Option A is correct. Option B would result from using z=1.8 or a calculation error; Option C from using p=0.5; Option D from using n=500.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A die is rolled 120 times with observed frequencies: 1→22, 2→18, 3→20, 4→25, 5→17, 6→18. Testing fairness at 5% significance, the correct conclusion is:
questions.solution: Expected frequency per face = 120/6 = 20. χ² = Σ(O-E)²/E = (22-20)²/20 + (18-20)²/20 + (20-20)²/20 + (25-20)²/20 + (17-20)²/20 + (18-20)²/20 = 0.2+0.2+0+1.25+0.45+0.2 = 2.30. Degrees of freedom = 6-1 = 5. Critical χ²₀.₀₅,₅ = 11.07. Since 2.30 < 11.07, we fail to reject the null hypothesis that the die is fair.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: The time to failure of a component follows an exponential distribution with failure rate λ = 0.02 per hour. What is the probability that the component lasts more than 50 hours?
questions.solution: For an exponential distribution, P(X > x) = e^(−λx). Here λ = 0.02 and x = 50, so λx = 1. Hence P(X > 50) = e^(−1) ≈ 0.3679, which rounds to 0.368.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A manufacturer claims the mean life of a bulb is 1000 hours. A sample of 25 bulbs gives a mean of 980 hours with sample standard deviation 50 hours. Test H₀: μ = 1000 against H₁: μ ≠ 1000 at the 5% significance level. What is the correct decision?
questions.solution: Test statistic t = (980 − 1000) / (50/√25) = −20 / 10 = −2.0. Degrees of freedom = 24. Two‑tailed critical value at α = 0.05 is approximately ±2.064. Since |t| = 2.0 < 2.064, we do not reject H₀.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: In a survey of 400 voters, 230 support a policy. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the true proportion of supporters using the normal approximation.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: The average number of customers arriving at a service counter is 6 per hour. The inter‑arrival time follows an exponential distribution. What is the probability that the waiting time until the next customer exceeds 15 minutes?
questions.solution: The arrival rate λ = 6 per hour. The waiting time T (in hours) is exponential with mean 1/λ = 1/6 hour = 10 minutes. For an exponential distribution, P(T > t) = e^(−λt). Here t = 15 minutes = 0.25 hour. So P(T > 0.25) = e^(−6 × 0.25) = e^(−1.5) ≈ 0.2231. The other options correspond to e^(−1) ≈ 0.368, e^(−2) ≈ 0.135, and 0.5 (the median). Thus the correct probability is 0.223.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: Component lifetimes are exponentially distributed with mean 1000 hours. A random sample of 36 components is taken. Using the Central Limit Theorem, what is the approximate probability that the sample mean lifetime exceeds 1050 hours?
questions.solution: For an exponential distribution with mean μ = 1000, the variance is μ² = 1,000,000. The sample mean of n = 36 components is approximately normal with mean 1000 and standard error σ/√n = 1000/√36 = 1000/6 ≈ 166.67. The z‑score for 1050 is (1050 − 1000) / 166.67 = 50 / 166.67 ≈ 0.30. The upper‑tail probability P(Z > 0.30) = 1 − Φ(0.30) ≈ 1 − 0.6179 = 0.3821. The other options are the lower tail (0.618), the median (0.500), and a value for z ≈ 0.60 (0.274). Hence the required probability is 0.382.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: A study measures the effect of a training program on 8 employees. The differences (after − before) in performance scores are: 5, −2, 8, 3, −1, 6, 4, −3. Using the Wilcoxon signed‑rank test, what is the value of the test statistic W⁺ (sum of positive signed ranks)?
questions.solution: First, discard zero differences (none). Take absolute values: 5, 2, 8, 3, 1, 6, 4, 3. Rank them from smallest to largest, assigning average ranks for ties: 1→1, 2→2, 3→3.5 (two 3s), 4→5, 5→6, 6→7, 8→8. Attach the original signs: +5 (rank 6), −2 (rank 2), +8 (rank 8), +3 (rank 3.5), −1 (rank 1), +6 (rank 7), +4 (rank 5), −3 (rank 3.5). Sum the ranks with positive signs: 6 + 8 + 3.5 + 7 + 5 = 29.5. Thus W⁺ = 29.5. The other options result from incorrect ranking (e.g., ignoring ties gives 31.0), omitting a positive difference (25.5), or mis‑assigning signs (27.0).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: If sinθ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find cosθ.
questions.solution: sin²θ+cos²θ=1 → cos²θ = 1-9/25 = 16/25 → cosθ = ±4/5. Since θ is acute (0<θ<90°), cosθ is positive, so cosθ = 4/5.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: Find the value of sin 75°.
questions.solution: sin75° = sin(45°+30°) = sin45°cos30°+cos45°sin30° = (1/√2)(√3/2)+(1/√2)(1/2) = (√3+1)/(2√2) = (√6+√2)/4. Both a and c are equivalent. Option a is the simplified form.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: The general solution of sinθ = 1/2 is:
questions.solution: sinθ = 1/2 → θ = π/6 (principal value). General solution: θ = nπ + (-1)ⁿ·π/6.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: If tanθ = 1, then secθ + cosecθ = ?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: The maximum value of 3 sinθ + 4 cosθ is:
questions.solution: Max of a sinθ + b cosθ = √(a²+b²) = √(9+16) = √25 = 5.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.q: Convert to passive voice: 'The committee is considering several proposals.'
questions.a: Several proposals are being considered by the committee.
opts: Several proposals are being considered by the committee.
Several proposals are considered by the committee.
Several proposals were being considered by the committee.
Several proposals have been considered by the committee.
questions.solution: Present Continuous (is considering) → is/am/are being + V3. 'Several proposals are being considered by the committee.'

questions.q: Convert to active voice: 'The report had been submitted by the manager before the deadline.'
questions.a: The manager had submitted the report before the deadline.
opts: The manager submitted the report before the deadline.
The manager has submitted the report before the deadline.
The manager had submitted the report before the deadline.
The manager was submitting the report before the deadline.
questions.solution: Passive (Past Perfect: had been submitted) → Active Past Perfect: had submitted.

questions.q: Convert to passive voice: 'Someone stole my wallet while I was shopping.'
questions.a: My wallet was stolen while I was shopping.
opts: My wallet is stolen while I was shopping.
My wallet was stolen while I was shopping.
My wallet had been stolen while I was shopping.
My wallet was being stolen while I was shopping.
questions.solution: Simple Past (stole) → was/were + V3 (was stolen). The agent 'by someone' is omitted when it is unknown/unimportant.

questions.q: Convert to passive voice: 'The students must submit their assignments by Friday.'
questions.a: Their assignments must be submitted by the students by Friday.
opts: Their assignments must submit by the students by Friday.
Their assignments must be submit by the students by Friday.
Their assignments must be submitted by the students by Friday.
Their assignments must have been submitted by the students by Friday.

questions.subject: English

questions.q: Convert to passive voice: 'Who broke the window?'
questions.a: By whom was the window broken?
opts: By whom the window was broken?
By whom was the window broken?
Who was the window broken by?
questions.solution: Active (Who broke) → Passive (By whom + was + window + broken). 'By whom was the window broken?'
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Convert to indirect speech: 'He said, "I am learning French these days."'
questions.a: He said that he was learning French those days.
opts: He said that he is learning French these days.
He said that he was learning French those days.
He said that I am learning French these days.
He said that he was learning French these days.
questions.solution: Present Continuous (am learning) → Past Continuous (was learning). 'these days' → 'those days'. 'I' → 'he'.

questions.q: Convert to indirect speech: 'She said to me, "What do you want?"'
questions.a: She asked me what I wanted.
opts: She asked me what I wanted.
She asked me what did I want.
She asked me what do you want.
She asked me that what I wanted.
questions.solution: WH-question → WH-word retained + statement order (subject + verb). 'What do you want?' → 'what I wanted'. 'She said to me' → 'She asked me'.

questions.q: Convert to indirect speech: 'The doctor said, "Take this medicine twice a day."'
questions.a: The doctor advised to take that medicine twice a day.
opts: The doctor said to take this medicine twice a day.
The doctor advised to take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor advised taking this medicine twice a day.
The doctor said take that medicine twice a day.
questions.solution: Imperative (advice) → advised + to + V1. 'this' → 'that'. 'Take' → 'to take'.

questions.q: Convert to direct speech: 'He exclaimed with joy that his team had won the championship.'
questions.a: He said, "Hurrah! My team has won the championship!"
opts: He said, "Hurrah! My team won the championship!"
He said, "Hurrah! My team has won the championship!"
He said, "Hurrah! My team had won the championship!"
He said, "My team won the championship."
questions.solution: Indirect (Past Perfect: had won) → Direct (Present Perfect: has won). Exclamation → 'Hurrah!'. 'his team' → 'my team'.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Identify the error: 'He told that he will come the next day.'
questions.solution: Two errors: (1)'told' needs an object → 'He told me that...' or use 'He said that...'. (2)'will come' should be 'would come' (backshift after past reporting verb).

questions.a: The teacher said that the Earth moves around the Sun.
opts: The teacher said that the Earth moved around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth moves around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth had moved around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth is moving around the Sun.

questions.q: Passage: 'The Right to Information (RTI) Act, passed in 2005, empowered Indian citizens to demand information from public authorities. It was hailed as a landmark legislation for transparency. However, recent amendments have raised concerns about the weakening of the RTI Act, with critics arguing that the changes undermine the very purpose of the law.' What is the main idea of the passage?
questions.a: The RTI Act, once a landmark for transparency, now faces concerns due to amendments that may weaken its purpose
opts: The RTI Act was passed in 2005
The RTI Act, once a landmark for transparency, now faces concerns due to amendments that may weaken its purpose
Citizens can demand information from public authorities
All amendments to laws are harmful
questions.solution: The passage traces the RTI Act from its original purpose (transparency) to the current concerns about amendments weakening it. Option b captures this journey. Options a and c are details, not main ideas. Option d is an extreme overgeneralisation.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Passage: 'Despite significant progress in electrification under the Saubhagya scheme, rural India still faces frequent power cuts. The quality of power supply — voltage fluctuations, unscheduled outages — remains a major impediment to small-scale industries in villages.' What can be inferred about the Saubhagya scheme?
questions.a: It successfully connected households but did not fully address power quality issues
opts: It successfully connected households but did not fully address power quality issues
It focused only on urban areas
It solved all rural power problems
questions.solution: The passage says 'despite significant progress in electrification' (success in connection) but 'the quality of power supply... remains a major impediment' (quality issues persist). This implies the scheme addressed quantity but not quality fully.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Passage: 'The ancient city of Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage site, was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Its magnificent temples and intricate carvings reflect the prosperity and artistic achievement of that era. However, decades of neglect and unregulated tourism have taken a toll on its structural integrity.' The word 'integrity' in this context most nearly means:
questions.solution: 'Structural integrity' refers to the soundness and wholeness of the physical structures. 'Toll on its integrity' means the structures have been damaged or weakened.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Passage: 'India's export sector has shown remarkable resilience despite global trade disruptions. Engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, and IT services have been the top contributors. The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme has boosted manufacturing exports significantly.' According to the passage, which sectors have contributed most to India's export resilience?
questions.a: Engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, and IT services
opts: Engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, and IT services
questions.solution: The passage explicitly lists 'engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, and IT services' as the top contributors. This is a direct detail question — the answer is stated verbatim.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Passage: 'The Bengal tiger, India's national animal, is classified as endangered. Conservation efforts under Project Tiger have led to an increase in tiger population from 1,411 in 2006 to 3,167 in 2022. However, habitat fragmentation and poaching remain persistent threats, particularly in corridors connecting tiger reserves.' The tone of the passage can best be described as:
questions.solution: The author presents positive data (population increase from Project Tiger) but also notes ongoing threats. This balanced, data-driven tone is 'analytical with cautious optimism.' It is not purely celebratory (a) because threats remain, nor critical (c) because progress is acknowledged.
questions.subject: English

questions.q: Passage: 'The phenomenon of 'brain drain' — the emigration of highly skilled workers — has historically been viewed as a loss for developing countries. Recent research, however, suggests that diaspora networks can facilitate trade, investment, and knowledge transfer back to the home country, turning 'brain drain' into 'brain gain'.' It can potentially benefit the home country through diaspora networks
Brain gain is the same as brain drain
questions.solution: The passage contrasts the old view (brain drain = loss) with new research showing benefits through diaspora networks. Option b captures this shift. Option a reflects only the old view. Option c is factually wrong. Option d conflates two distinct concepts.

questions.q: Passage: 'India has the third-largest startup ecosystem in the world. While GST has improved tax compliance and revenue collection, businesses initially faced challenges with the complex filing system and frequent rate changes.' The mission will study深海 biodiversity and mineral resources. This places India among a select group of nations with deep-sea manned mission capability.' Only Russian astronauts will fly on Gaganyaan

questions.q: According to Newton's third law of motion, when a rocket expels hot gases downward, the rocket gains upward thrust. Which of the following correctly describes the action-reaction pair in this scenario?
questions.a: Action: Rocket pushes gases down; Reaction: Gases push rocket up
opts: Action: Rocket pushes gases down; Reaction: Gases push rocket up
Action: Gases push rocket up; Reaction: Rocket pushes gases down
Action: Rocket's engine ignites fuel; Reaction: Rocket moves upward
Action: Gravitational pull on rocket; Reaction: Rocket's thrust opposes gravity
questions.solution: Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The text explicitly gives the example: 'when a rocket expels hot gases downward to gain upward thrust.' The action force is the rocket pushing the exhaust gases downward. The reaction force is the gases pushing the rocket upward with equal magnitude. Option A correctly identifies this pair. Option B reverses the labels. Option C describes cause and effect, not an action-reaction pair. Option D describes gravity and thrust, which are two separate forces acting on the rocket, not an action-reaction pair (which must act on two different bodies).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes pellagra, characterized by dermatitis, diarrhoea, and dementia?
questions.solution: The lesson lists B-complex vitamins and their deficiency diseases: 'B₃ (niacin) for NAD⁺ (pellagra — dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia)'. Vitamin B₁ deficiency causes beriberi. Vitamin B₉ and B₁₂ deficiencies cause megaloblastic anaemia. Therefore, niacin (Vitamin B₃) deficiency is the cause of pellagra.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at 600 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K. What is its maximum theoretical efficiency?
questions.solution: The Carnot efficiency is given by η = 1 − Tc/Th, where temperatures are in kelvin. Substituting Th = 600 K and Tc = 300 K gives η = 1 − 300/600 = 1 − 0.5 = 0.5, i.e. 50%. This matches option C.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A radioactive isotope has a half‑life of 10 years. What fraction of the original sample remains after 30 years?
questions.solution: Radioactive decay follows N = N₀(1/2)^(t/t½). Here t = 30 years and t½ = 10 years, so the exponent is 30/10 = 3. The remaining fraction is (1/2)³ = 1/8. This corresponds to option C.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Trisomy of chromosome 21 leads to which genetic disorder?
questions.solution: The lesson notes that aneuploidy such as trisomy 21 results in Down syndrome. Turner syndrome is 45,X, Klinefelter is 47,XXY, and Edwards syndrome is trisomy 18. Hence the correct answer is option C.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the CRISPR‑Cas9 system, what protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) sequence is required for Cas9 cleavage?
questions.solution: The lesson specifies that the guide RNA directs Cas9 to a target DNA sequence adjacent to a PAM of NGG. This NGG motif is essential for Cas9 binding and cleavage. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a series RLC circuit, the resonant angular frequency ω₀ is given by which expression?
questions.solution: Resonance occurs when inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance: X_L = X_C → ωL = 1/(ωC). Solving gives ω² = 1/(LC), so ω = 1/√(LC). This matches option A.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In Young's double‑slit experiment the fringe width β = λD/d. If the wavelength is doubled and the slit separation is halved, the new fringe width becomes:
questions.solution: Original β = λD/d. New wavelength = 2λ, new slit separation = d/2. New β' = (2λ)D/(d/2) = 4λD/d = 4β. Hence the fringe width increases by a factor of 4, corresponding to option B.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For a galvanic cell at 298 K, the cell potential E is related to the reaction quotient Q by the Nernst equation as:
questions.solution: The Nernst equation at 298 K uses base‑10 logarithm: E = E° − (0.0591/n) log₁₀ Q. The negative sign indicates that an increase in Q (more products) lowers the cell potential. This is exactly option B.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Lindeman’s 10 % rule applies to the transfer of which ecological parameter between trophic levels?
questions.solution: Lindeman’s 10 % rule states that only about 10 % of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next. It does not hold for biomass, numbers, or nutrient mass. Therefore the correct parameter is energy, option B.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In an ideal transformer, the ratio of secondary voltage to primary voltage equals the ratio of:
questions.solution: For an ideal transformer V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p = I_p/I_s. Thus the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio of secondary to primary. This corresponds to option B.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a silicon p-n junction under forward bias, what happens to the width of the depletion region compared to its equilibrium state?
questions.a: It narrows as the applied voltage opposes the built-in potential
opts: It widens due to increased uncovered ionised dopants
It narrows as the applied voltage opposes the built-in potential
It remains unchanged because only current flow is affected
It disappears completely allowing unrestricted carrier flow
questions.solution: Under forward bias, the positive terminal is connected to the p-side and negative to the n-side. The applied voltage opposes the built-in potential (V_bi), reducing the barrier height. This reduction in the electric field across the junction allows majority carriers to diffuse across, which neutralises some of the fixed ionised dopants at the edges of the depletion region. Consequently, the depletion region narrows. Under reverse bias, the applied voltage adds to the built-in potential, pulling majority carriers away from the junction and widening the depletion region. The text explicitly states: 'forward bias narrows the depletion region, reverse bias widens it'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the protective effect of many modern vaccines such as those for influenza and COVID-19?
questions.a: They primarily reduce disease severity and transmission without necessarily preventing infection
opts: They induce sterilising immunity that completely blocks pathogen entry and replication
They primarily reduce disease severity and transmission without necessarily preventing infection
They provide lifelong immunity after a single dose due to strong memory B-cell activation
They rely solely on innate immune activation through adjuvant stimulation of TLRs
questions.solution: The lesson highlights a common examiner trap: 'Assuming all vaccines induce sterilising immunity; many (e.g., influenza, COVID‑19) primarily reduce severity and transmission rather than block infection completely.' Sterilising immunity implies complete prevention of infection and replication. However, many respiratory virus vaccines generate robust systemic IgG and T-cell responses that limit viral load and pathogenesis but may not generate sufficient mucosal IgA to block initial infection entirely. Therefore, the primary measured efficacy is against severe disease, hospitalisation, and transmission reduction, not absolute infection blockade.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the relationship between Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) and Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) for a given wastewater sample?
questions.a: COD is always greater than or equal to BOD as it oxidises non-biodegradable organics
opts: BOD is always greater than COD because biological oxidation is more complete
COD is always greater than or equal to BOD as it oxidises non-biodegradable organics
BOD and COD are numerically identical for domestic sewage but differ for industrial waste
COD measures only the carbonaceous demand while BOD includes nitrogenous demand
questions.solution: COD uses a strong chemical oxidant (potassium dichromate in acidic medium) that oxidises virtually all organic compounds, including those that are non-biodegradable or toxic to microorganisms. BOD relies on microbial metabolism over 5 days at 20°C, which only degrades biodegradable organics. Since the set of substances oxidised chemically includes the set oxidised biologically plus additional refractory organics, COD ≥ BOD always. The lesson explicitly flags the error of 'Treating BOD and COD as interchangeable; COD includes non‑biodegradable organics and is always ≥ BOD'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which process consumes oxygen and releases carbon dioxide in the presence of light without producing ATP, and is essentially a wasteful competition with carbon fixation?
questions.solution: Photorespiration occurs when RuBisCO oxygenates RuBP instead of carboxylating it, which happens at high O2/CO2 ratios and temperatures. This process consumes O2 and releases CO2 in the light but does not generate ATP or NADPH; instead, it consumes energy (ATP and reducing power) to recycle the product phosphoglycolate. The lesson identifies the trap: 'Overlooking that photorespiration consumes O2 and releases CO2 without ATP production'. C4 plants minimise this by spatially separating initial CO2 fixation (mesophyll) from the Calvin cycle (bundle sheath). Dark respiration occurs in mitochondria day and night. Cyclic photophosphorylation produces ATP without NADPH or O2 evolution.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: How does the photoluminescence emission wavelength of a quantum dot change as its particle size increases?
questions.a: It increases (red shift) because quantum confinement energy decreases
opts: It decreases (blue shift) due to increased quantum confinement energy
It increases (red shift) because quantum confinement energy decreases
It remains constant as emission depends only on material composition
It becomes unpredictable due to surface defect dominance
questions.solution: Quantum dots exhibit quantum confinement: the band gap energy increases as particle size decreases because the electron and hole wavefunctions are more restricted. A larger band gap corresponds to higher energy (shorter wavelength) emission. Conversely, as particle size increases, the confinement energy decreases, the band gap narrows, and the emitted photon energy decreases, resulting in a longer wavelength (red shift). The lesson corrects the misconception in the 'Confusing' section: 'Believing quantum‑dot emission wavelength increases with particle size; in fact, larger dots emit at longer wavelengths (red shift) because confinement energy decreases.' Note: The formula λ ∝ 1/√(size) in the Optical properties section appears inconsistent with this established physics and the explicit trap correction; the trap correction reflects the correct physical principle.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a p-n junction at thermal equilibrium, the built-in potential (V_bi) is:
questions.a: Positive on the n-side relative to the p-side
opts: Positive on the p-side relative to the n-side
Positive on the n-side relative to the p-side
Negative on both sides relative to the intrinsic region
questions.solution: The built-in potential arises due to diffusion of majority carriers across the junction. Electrons diffuse from the n-side to the p-side, leaving behind positively charged donor ions on the n-side. Holes diffuse from the p-side to the n-side, leaving behind negatively charged acceptor ions on the p-side. This creates an electric field directed from the n-side to the p-side, making the n-side at a higher potential relative to the p-side. Thus, V_bi is positive on the n-side relative to the p-side.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a nuclear reactor, if the neutron multiplication factor k is exactly 1, the reactor is said to be:
questions.solution: The neutron multiplication factor k is defined as the ratio of neutrons produced in one generation to the number of neutrons lost (absorbed plus leakage) in the preceding generation. When k = 1, the neutron population remains constant over time, meaning the chain reaction is self-sustaining at a steady power level. This condition is defined as the critical state. If k 1, it is supercritical (power increases).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following statements about step-growth polymerisation is correct?
questions.a: Some step-growth polymerisations, such as polyurethane formation, do not release a small molecule
opts: All step-growth polymerisations are condensation reactions releasing a small molecule
Polyurethane formation is a step-growth polymerisation that releases water as a by-product
Some step-growth polymerisations, such as polyurethane formation, do not release a small molecule
The Carothers equation applies equally to both step-growth and chain-growth polymerisations
questions.solution: Step-growth polymerisation proceeds by stepwise reaction between functional groups of monomers. While many step-growth reactions are condensation type (e.g., polyesterification releasing water), polyurethane formation from diisocyanates and diols occurs via addition reaction without elimination of any small molecule. The Carothers equation (X_n = 1/(1-p)) relates the degree of polymerisation to the extent of reaction p and is strictly valid only for step-growth (condensation or addition) systems, not for chain-growth (free radical, ionic) polymerisation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes MHC restriction in T cell recognition?
questions.a: CD4+ T cells recognise antigens presented by MHC Class II molecules
opts: CD4+ T cells recognise antigens presented by MHC Class I molecules
CD8+ T cells recognise antigens presented by MHC Class II molecules
CD4+ T cells recognise antigens presented by MHC Class II molecules
Both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells recognise antigens presented by MHC Class I molecules
questions.solution: MHC restriction is a fundamental principle of T cell recognition. CD4+ T helper cells express the CD4 co-receptor which binds to non-polymorphic regions of MHC Class II molecules (expressed on professional antigen-presenting cells). CD8+ cytotoxic T cells express the CD8 co-receptor which binds to MHC Class I molecules (expressed on almost all nucleated cells). This co-receptor binding stabilises the interaction between the T cell receptor and the peptide-MHC complex and ensures appropriate immune response activation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding photorespiration in C4 plants, which statement is accurate?
questions.a: C4 plants strongly suppress photorespiration by concentrating CO2 in bundle-sheath cells, but do not eradicate it entirely
opts: C4 plants lack the enzyme Rubisco, thereby avoiding photorespiration
C4 plants strongly suppress photorespiration by concentrating CO2 in bundle-sheath cells, but do not eradicate it entirely
Photorespiration in C4 plants occurs at a higher rate than in C3 plants due to the C4 cycle
questions.solution: C4 plants (e.g., maize, sugarcane) possess a CO2 concentrating mechanism. PEP carboxylase in mesophyll cells fixes HCO3- into a 4-carbon acid (oxaloacetate/malate), which is transported to bundle-sheath cells. Decarboxylation releases CO2 at high concentration around Rubisco, suppressing its oxygenase activity and thus strongly reducing photorespiration. However, the mechanism is not perfectly efficient; some CO2 leaks back and oxygenase activity still occurs at a low level, so photorespiration is suppressed but not completely eliminated.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which semiconductor material has an energy band gap of approximately 1.12 eV at 300 K?
questions.solution: The lesson lists typical semiconductor parameters at 300 K. For Silicon the band gap Eg is given as 1.12 eV, while Germanium is 0.66 eV and GaAs is 1.42 eV. Diamond is an insulator with a much larger gap (>5 eV). Therefore the material matching 1.12 eV is Silicon.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The nucleus with the maximum binding energy per nucleon (≈ 8.8 MeV) is:
questions.solution: According to the nuclear physics section, Iron‑56 (⁵⁶Fe) has the highest binding energy per nucleon, about 8.8 MeV, making it the most stable nucleus. Uranium‑235, Helium‑4 and Carbon‑12 have lower values per nucleon.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Humoral immunity is primarily mediated by which type of lymphocyte?
questions.solution: The immunology part states that adaptive immunity has two arms: humoral (antibody‑mediated) and cell‑mediated. Humoral immunity is carried out by B lymphocytes which differentiate into plasma cells secreting antibodies. Cytotoxic T cells, NK cells and macrophages are involved in cell‑mediated or innate responses.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which class of chemical reactions typically exhibits 100 % atom economy according to the green chemistry principles?
questions.solution: The twelve principles of green chemistry include atom economy, defined as (MW of desired product / Σ MW of all reactants) × 100 %. The lesson explicitly gives addition reactions as an example of 100 % atom economy, whereas substitution and elimination reactions have lower atom economy.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: As per the WHO 2021 air‑quality guidelines, the annual mean concentration limit for PM₂.₅ is:
questions.solution: The lesson provides a table of WHO 2021 guideline values. For PM₂.₅ the annual averaging time guideline is listed as 5 µg/m³. The older 10 µg/m³ value is outdated, and 15 µg/m³ and 25 µg/m³ correspond to other pollutants or averaging periods.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the System of National Accounts followed by the Central Statistics Office, which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Gross National Product (GNP) from Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
questions.a: GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad, which covers wages, rent, interest, and profits earned by residents overseas minus payments to non-residents in India.
opts: GNP includes the value of illegal activities and voluntary household work, while GDP excludes them.
GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad, which covers wages, rent, interest, and profits earned by residents overseas minus payments to non-residents in India.
GNP measures output produced by Indian-owned firms globally, whereas GDP measures output produced by all firms within India's borders regardless of ownership.
GNP is calculated using the expenditure approach only, while GDP uses the production, income, and expenditure approaches.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states: "Gross national product extends this concept by adding net factor income from abroad, which consists of wages, rent, interest and profits earned by Indian residents from overseas investments minus similar payments made to foreign residents inside India." Option B matches this definition verbatim. Option A is incorrect because both GDP and GNP exclude illegal activities and voluntary household work per the production boundary convention. Option C confuses ownership with residency; GNP is based on residency of income earners, not firm ownership. Option D is false because both aggregates can be measured by all three approaches.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Central Statistics Office publishes a "statistical discrepancy" item in the national accounts. What is the primary reason for this discrepancy?
questions.a: Timing differences, data source gaps, and the treatment of the informal sector cause the three measurement approaches to produce different empirical results.
opts: The production, income, and expenditure approaches use different base years, making their totals incomparable.
The three theoretical approaches yield identical results only in a closed economy; in an open economy they diverge due to net exports.
Timing differences, data source gaps, and the treatment of the informal sector cause the three measurement approaches to produce different empirical results.
The discrepancy arises because the value-added method double-counts intermediate goods while the income approach omits mixed income.
questions.solution: The lesson states: "In theory all three approaches yield identical GDP figures; in practice statistical discrepancies arise from timing differences, data source gaps and the treatment of the informal sector, and the Central Statistics Office publishes a statistical discrepancy item to reconcile them." Option C directly reflects this explanation. Option A is incorrect because the base year (2011-12) is common across approaches. Option B is wrong; the identity holds for open economies as well (net exports are part of the expenditure approach). Option D misstates the value-added method, which avoids double counting by design.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which institutional reform introduced a time-bound resolution process for distressed assets to address the twin-balance-sheet problem of over-leveraged corporates and stressed banks?
questions.a: The enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code in 2016.
opts: The replacement of the Planning Commission by NITI Aayog in 2015.
The launch of the Goods and Services Tax in July 2017.
The enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code in 2016.
The adoption of the FRBM Act amendment targeting a 3% fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio.
questions.solution: The lesson states: "The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, introduced a time‑bound resolution process for distressed assets, strengthening creditor rights and addressing the twin‑balance‑sheet problem of over‑leveraged corporates and stressed banks." Option C matches this description exactly. Option A refers to cooperative federalism and policy design. Option B refers to indirect tax unification. Option D refers to fiscal consolidation rules, not asset resolution.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which facility, introduced in April 2022, completed the symmetric interest‑rate corridor by offering a non‑collateralised deposit window at a rate 25 basis points below the repo rate?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) was launched in April 2022 at a rate 25 basis points below the repo rate and that it is non‑collateralised from inception, thereby completing the symmetric corridor (repo rate at the centre, MSF at repo + 100 bps as the ceiling, SDF at repo − 25 bps as the floor). The MSF was introduced earlier in 2011, the reverse repo window existed from the start of LAF, and LAF itself is the overarching framework, not the new facility.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The 15th Finance Commission (2020‑25) retained the vertical devolution share at 41 % of the divisible pool and introduced a performance‑based incentive for States. Which of the following is NOT a criterion for that incentive?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, the 15th Finance Commission added a performance‑based incentive for States that achieve targets in three areas: GST collection, ease of doing business, and demographic performance. Fiscal deficit reduction target is not listed among these criteria. Hence option D is the correct choice as it is not a criterion for the incentive.

questions.q: Regarding the agricultural marketing reforms, which statement correctly reflects the status of the three farm Acts enacted in September 2020?
questions.a: They were repealed in November 2021, leaving the APMC framework largely intact.
opts: They remain in force and have replaced the APMC framework nationwide.
They were repealed in November 2021, leaving the APMC framework largely intact.
They were amended in 2022 to make APMC participation mandatory for all traders.
They were upheld by the Supreme Court and are being implemented through the model APMC Act.
questions.solution: The lesson clearly states that the three farm Acts enacted in September 2020 were repealed in November 2021 following sustained protests, and that the repeal left the APMC framework largely intact. The Centre is now pursuing a model APMC Act for voluntary adoption by States. Therefore option B accurately describes the current status, while the other options contradict the lesson’s timeline and outcome.

questions.q: As per the 2023-24 Budget Estimates and the FRBM framework, what is the approximate combined Centre-State debt-to-GDP ratio and its compliance status with the FRBM anchor?
questions.a: Centre ~58%, States ~30%, combined >85% — well above the FRBM anchor of 60%.
opts: Centre ~40%, States ~20%, combined ~60% — compliant with the FRBM anchor of 60%.
Centre ~58%, States ~30%, combined >85% — well above the FRBM anchor of 60%.
Centre ~45%, States ~25%, combined ~70% — marginally above the FRBM anchor.
Centre ~60%, States ~20%, combined ~80% — within the revised FRBM glide path.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states: "As of the 2023-24 Budget Estimates, the Centre's gross fiscal deficit stands at 5.9 per cent of GDP, and the debt-to-GDP ratio is approximately 58 per cent (including off-budget borrowings). States collectively hold a debt-to-GDP ratio near 30 per cent, pushing the combined ratio above 85 per cent — well above the FRBM anchor." The FRBM Act's 2018 amendment set a combined Centre-State debt ceiling of 60 per cent. Therefore, the combined ratio exceeding 85 per cent is non-compliant. Option B reflects these exact figures and the compliance assessment. Options A, C, and D present incorrect debt ratios and compliance statuses.

questions.q: Regarding the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework for banks, which statement correctly describes the exit criteria?
questions.a: A bank exits PCA once it meets all three threshold parameters for four consecutive quarters.
opts: A bank exits PCA immediately upon meeting any one of the three threshold parameters (capital, asset quality, profitability).
A bank exits PCA after meeting all three threshold parameters for two consecutive quarters.
A bank exits PCA once it meets all three threshold parameters for four consecutive quarters.
A bank can exit PCA only through amalgamation with a bank not under PCA.
questions.solution: The lesson includes a specific "Exam-relevant nuance": "Treating PCA as a permanent label; banks exit once they meet all three thresholds for four consecutive quarters." This directly confirms Option C. Option A is incorrect because meeting a single threshold is insufficient. Option B is incorrect because the required period is four quarters, not two. Option D is incorrect as amalgamation is not the prescribed exit route; the framework allows exit based on sustained financial improvement.

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately describes the nature and operation of the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme?
questions.a: The PLI scheme is a supply-side intervention that pays incentives on incremental sales over a defined base year and does not alter bound tariff rates under the WTO.
opts: The PLI scheme reduces bound tariff rates under WTO commitments for the targeted manufacturing sectors.
The PLI scheme provides financial incentives based on the absolute production volume achieved from the first year of operation.
The PLI scheme is a supply-side intervention that pays incentives on incremental sales over a defined base year and does not alter bound tariff rates under the WTO.
The PLI scheme replaces the requirement for 'rules of origin' certification under Free Trade Agreements.
questions.solution: The lesson states two key facts about the PLI scheme: (1) "The PLI scheme is a supply-side intervention; it does not directly alter bound tariff rates under the WTO." (2) Under "Exam-relevant nuances": "Thinking PLI incentives are granted on absolute production; they are paid on incremental sales over a defined base year." Option C combines both accurate points. Option A is false because PLI does not change bound tariffs. Option B is false because incentives are on incremental, not absolute, production. Option D is false because PLI is unrelated to FTA rules of origin, which determine preferential tariff eligibility.

questions.q: Which statement correctly reflects the fiscal and legal nature of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)?
questions.a: MGNREGA is a demand-driven legal entitlement; its expenditure cannot be capped by the annual budget without amending the Act.
opts: MGNREGA expenditure is strictly capped by the annual budget allocation; the government is not legally obligated to spend beyond the budgeted amount.
MGNREGA is a demand-driven legal entitlement; its expenditure cannot be capped by the annual budget without amending the Act.
MGNREGA is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with a 60:40 Centre-State funding share, similar to Ayushman Bharat.
The annual allocation for MGNREGA is determined by the recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states under "Exam-relevant nuances": "MGNREGA is a legal entitlement; its expenditure cannot be capped by the budget without amending the Act" and "Assuming MGNREGA spending is capped by the annual budget allocation; the Act mandates demand-driven funding." Option B matches this exactly. Option A contradicts the statutory guarantee. Option C is incorrect because MGNREGA is a Central sector scheme (fully funded by the Centre), not a 60:40 Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Option D is incorrect because the 15th Finance Commission provides sectoral grants for health and education, not MGNREGA allocations.

questions.q: The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate currently stands at how many basis points above the policy repo rate, and what does it represent in the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor?
questions.a: 25 basis points; upper bound of the LAF corridor
opts: 25 basis points; upper bound of the LAF corridor
50 basis points; upper bound of the LAF corridor
25 basis points; lower bound of the LAF corridor
100 basis points; midpoint of the LAF corridor
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'The Marginal Standing Facility, introduced in May 2011, provides a safety valve for banks to borrow overnight from the RBI at a rate penalised above the repo rate (currently 25 basis points higher).' Option A correctly captures both the current spread (25 bps) and the MSF's role as the corridor ceiling. questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes India's Green Finance Taxonomy applicability and the nature of Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs)?
questions.a: The Taxonomy is mandatory for sovereign green bond allocation but voluntary for private issuers; SGrBs are use-of-proceeds bonds
opts: The Taxonomy is legally binding for all private issuers; SGrBs are sustainability-linked bonds with coupon step-ups
The Taxonomy is mandatory for sovereign green bond allocation but voluntary for private issuers; SGrBs are use-of-proceeds bonds
The Taxonomy applies only to corporate green bonds; SGrBs follow the EU Taxonomy exclusively
The Taxonomy is mandatory for all financial institutions; SGrBs are identical to sustainability-linked bonds
questions.solution: The lesson states two key facts: (1) 'India's taxonomy is voluntary for private issuers but mandatory for sovereign green bond allocation.' Option B correctly combines both facts. Option A reverses the taxonomy applicability and misclassifies SGrBs. Option C incorrectly limits taxonomy scope and SGrB framework. Option D makes both claims false.

questions.q: Under the revised liquidity management framework introduced by the RBI in April 2022, which of the following statements correctly describes the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)?
questions.a: The SDF rate is set 25 basis points below the policy repo rate, creating a symmetric 50-bps corridor with the MSF rate fixed 25 bps above the repo rate.
opts: The SDF requires eligible government securities as collateral, similar to the erstwhile fixed-rate reverse repo window.
The SDF rate is set 25 basis points below the policy repo rate, creating a symmetric 50-bps corridor with the MSF rate fixed 25 bps above the repo rate.
The width of the LAF corridor changes automatically with every monetary policy review depending on liquidity conditions.
The SDF has replaced Open Market Operations (OMOs) and the Market Stabilisation Scheme (MSS) as the primary tool for structural liquidity management.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the SDF is a collateral-free absorption tool (unlike the reverse repo which required collateral), the SDF rate is set at repo minus 25 bps while MSF remains at repo plus 25 bps, creating a fixed symmetric 50-bps corridor. The corridor width is fixed unless the RBI explicitly changes the spreads. OMOs and MSS continue to be used for structural liquidity and capital flow sterilisation respectively, and are not replaced by the SDF.

questions.q: Regarding the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), which of the following combinations of threshold and voting requirement is correct as per the current framework?
questions.a: Default threshold of ₹1 crore; Resolution plan approved by 66% of CoC voting share; Maximum timeline of 180 days extendable by 90 days.
opts: Default threshold of ₹1 lakh; Resolution plan approved by simple majority (51%) of Committee of Creditors (CoC) voting share.
Default threshold of ₹1 crore; Resolution plan approved by 66% of CoC voting share; Maximum timeline of 180 days extendable by 90 days.
Default threshold of ₹1 crore; Resolution plan approved by 75% of CoC voting share; Fixed timeline of 270 days with no extension.
Default threshold of ₹10 lakh; Resolution plan approved by 66% of CoC voting share; Maximum timeline of 330 days including all extensions.
questions.solution: The lesson specifies that CIRP is initiated upon default of ₹1 crore (raised from ₹1 lakh in 2020), must be completed within 180 days extendable by 90 days with CoC approval, and a resolution plan requires approval by 66% of the CoC's voting share. The other options incorrectly state the default threshold, voting threshold, or timeline structure.

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately reflects the current status of the GST compensation cess and the associated Centre-State fiscal arrangement?
questions.a: The GST compensation cess has been extended until March 2026, and the Centre continues to service the back-to-back loans taken to fund the compensation shortfall during the transition period.
opts: The GST compensation cess expired in June 2022 and no further collections are being made; States must now absorb all revenue shortfalls independently.
The GST compensation cess has been extended until March 2026, and the Centre continues to service the back-to-back loans taken to fund the compensation shortfall during the transition period.
The GST compensation cess has been extended until March 2028, but the responsibility of servicing the back-to-back loans has been transferred to the State governments.
The GST compensation cess was subsumed into the general GST rates in 2023, eliminating the need for separate cess collections and back-to-back loan servicing.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that the GST compensation cess has been extended to March 2026 and the Centre continues to service the back-to-back loans. The common mistake highlighted is believing the cess expired in 2022. The other options incorrectly state the extension period, loan servicing responsibility, or claim the cess was subsumed.

questions.q: Up to which date has the GST compensation cess period been extended to amortise the Centre’s borrowing on behalf of states?
questions.solution: The original five‑year compensation guarantee (2017‑22) was extended because the Centre borrowed ₹1.1 lakh crore in 2020‑21 and ₹1.59 lakh crore in 2021‑22 to meet shortfalls. The cess period was prolonged to March 2026 to allow future cess collections to repay this borrowing.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the current status of India’s capital account liberalisation?
questions.a: Capital account liberalisation has proceeded in stages and the rupee remains partially convertible on the capital account.
opts: India has achieved full capital account convertibility.
The Fully Accessible Route for government securities implies full capital account convertibility.
Capital account liberalisation has proceeded in stages and the rupee remains partially convertible on the capital account.
External commercial borrowings are prohibited for Indian corporates.
questions.solution: India follows a “managed openness” approach. Liberalisation occurred in stages — FII entry (1992), ECB framework (1995), ADR/GDR (1996), gradual FDI limit increases — but the capital account is not fully convertible. The Fully Accessible Route for certain government securities is a limited channel and does not equate to full convertibility.
