questions.q: The External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) framework introduced by the RBI in October 2019 applies to which category of loans?
questions.a: Only new floating rate loans sanctioned after the effective date.
opts: All outstanding loans including legacy MCLR‑linked credit.
Only new floating rate loans sanctioned after the effective date.
Only loans to micro and small enterprises.
questions.solution: The EBLR mandate covers all new floating rate personal or retail loans and floating rate loans to micro and small enterprises sanctioned from 1 October 2019. Existing MCLR‑linked loans continue under the old regime unless the borrower opts to switch; the framework does not automatically apply to legacy credit.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of the Retail Digital Rupee (e₹‑R) as described in the pilot phases?
questions.a: It is a non‑interest‑bearing token issued by the RBI.
opts: It pays interest at the prevailing savings deposit rate.
It is a non‑interest‑bearing token issued by the RBI.
It can be held only by commercial banks.
It is based on a permissionless blockchain open to the public.
questions.solution: The digital rupee (e₹) is a sovereign digital currency issued by the RBI. In both wholesale (e₹‑W) and retail (e₹‑R) pilots it is designed as a non‑interest‑bearing token, equivalent to physical cash. It is not restricted to banks, nor does it use a public permissionless blockchain; the RBI controls the ledger.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the three parallel ranges of the Himalayan Mountain System from north to south and the location of duns?
questions.a: A. Himadri, Himachal, Shiwaliks; duns lie between Himachal and Shiwaliks
opts: A. Himadri, Himachal, Shiwaliks; duns lie between Himachal and Shiwaliks
B. Himadri, Shiwaliks, Himachal; duns lie between Himadri and Himachal
C. Himachal, Himadri, Shiwaliks; duns lie between Himadri and Shiwaliks
D. Shiwaliks, Himachal, Himadri; duns lie between Shiwaliks and Himadri
questions.solution: The Himalayas comprise three parallel ranges: the northernmost Great Himalayas (Himadri), the middle Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), and the outermost Shiwaliks. Longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal) and the Shiwaliks are called duns, with Dehra Dun as the prominent example. Option A matches this north-to-south sequence and dun location. Options B, C, and D either reverse the order or misplace the duns.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding the alluvium of the Northern Plains, which statement accurately distinguishes Khadar from Bhangar?
questions.a: B. Khadar is newer alluvium in floodplains, light and sandy; Bhangar is older alluvium above flood level with kankar
opts: A. Khadar is older alluvium containing kankar; Bhangar is newer alluvium annually renewed
B. Khadar is newer alluvium in floodplains, light and sandy; Bhangar is older alluvium above flood level with kankar
C. Both Khadar and Bhangar are newer alluvium but Khadar has kankar
D. Both are older alluvium but Bhangar is annually renewed
questions.solution: The Northern Plains' alluvium is divided into Khadar (newer alluvium) found in active floodplains — light, sandy, and renewed annually by floods — and Bhangar (older alluvium) lying above flood level, characterized by calcareous concretions called kankar. Option B correctly states this distinction. Option A reverses the attributes, while C and D incorrectly describe both as same-age alluvium.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The major rivers of the Deccan Plateau — Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri — flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal. What geological feature causes this drainage pattern?
questions.a: B. The Deccan Plateau slopes gently eastward
opts: A. The Western Ghats block westward flow
B. The Deccan Plateau slopes gently eastward
C. The Eastern Ghats are higher than Western Ghats
D. The Narmada rift valley diverts rivers east
questions.solution: The Deccan Plateau, formed by Cretaceous basaltic lava flows, tilts gently eastward. This regional slope directs the major peninsular rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) toward the Bay of Bengal. The Western Ghats form the western escarpment but the eastward slope is the primary control. Option A describes a barrier, not the slope cause; Option C is factually incorrect (Western Ghats are higher); Option D refers to the Narmada rift which separates Central Highlands from Deccan, not the Deccan's internal slope.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement about Indian coal reserves is correct?
questions.a: C. Gondwana coal is Permian age, constitutes 98% of reserves, found in Damodar, Son, Godavari, Mahanadi valleys
opts: A. Gondwana coal is Eocene age, high in sulphur, found in Assam and Meghalaya
B. Tertiary coal is Permian age, constitutes 98% of reserves, found in Damodar valley
C. Gondwana coal is Permian age, constitutes 98% of reserves, found in Damodar, Son, Godavari, Mahanadi valleys
D. Both Gondwana and Tertiary coal are Permian age but Gondwana has higher sulphur
questions.solution: Gondwana coal (Permian period, 250–300 million years old) accounts for 98% of India's coal reserves and occurs in the Damodar valley (Jharia, Bokaro, Raniganj), Son valley (Singrauli, Korba), Godavari valley (Ramagundam), and Mahanadi valley (Talcher). Tertiary coal (Eocene, 50–60 million years old) is found in northeastern states (Assam, Arunachal, Meghalaya, Nagaland) and is high in sulphur. Option C matches these facts. Options A and B swap the age, sulphur content, and locations of the two coal types. Option D incorrectly assigns Permian age to both.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: India holds the world's largest reserves of thorium (about 25%). Where do these reserves occur and what is their role in India's nuclear programme?
questions.a: B. Thorium reserves are largest in monazite sands of Kerala and Odisha coasts; central to three-stage programme (PHWR → FBR → Thorium reactors)
opts: A. Thorium reserves are largest in Jharkhand's Singhbhum belt; used in first stage PHWR
B. Thorium reserves are largest in monazite sands of Kerala and Odisha coasts; central to three-stage programme (PHWR → FBR → Thorium reactors)
C. Uranium reserves are largest in monazite sands; Thorium is in Cuddapah basin
D. Thorium reserves are largest in Rajasthan; used directly in first stage reactors
questions.solution: Thorium reserves, constituting about 25% of global reserves, occur in monazite sands along the Kerala and Odisha coasts. They are pivotal to India's three-stage nuclear power programme: Stage 1 uses Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR) fuelled by natural uranium; Stage 2 uses Fast Breeder Reactors (FBR) to breed plutonium; Stage 3 will use thorium-based reactors to utilise the vast thorium reserves. Option B correctly identifies the location (monazite sands of Kerala and Odisha) and the strategic role in the three-stage sequence. Option A misplaces thorium in Singhbhum (uranium belt) and assigns it to Stage 1. Option C confuses uranium with thorium locations. Option D mislocates reserves in Rajasthan and suggests direct first-stage use.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What key change did the 2019 amendment to the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 introduce to address delays in adjudication?
questions.a: It established a single standing tribunal with multiple benches and a strict three‑year timeline
opts: It allowed states to directly approach the Supreme Court without tribunal intervention
It established a single standing tribunal with multiple benches and a strict three‑year timeline
It made tribunal awards advisory rather than binding on riparian states
It transferred all water dispute resolution to the Central Water Commission
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 2019 amendment introduced a single standing tribunal with multiple benches and a strict three‑year timeline for adjudication, aiming to reduce the decades‑long delays that characterised earlier tribunals. Option A is incorrect because Article 262 and the Act still require tribunal adjudication before Supreme Court review. Option C is wrong because awards remain final and binding. Option D is not mentioned; the Central Water Commission is not given dispute resolution authority.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which climatic phenomenon offset a weak El Niño signal to produce above‑normal monsoon rainfall in India during 2019?
questions.solution: The text explicitly mentions that a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) in 2019 contributed to above‑normal rainfall despite a weak El Niño signal. It also notes that the IOD can offset ENSO, citing 1997 and 2019 as examples. The Madden‑Julian Oscillation, Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and Southern Annular Mode are not referenced in the lesson as factors for the 2019 monsoon.

questions.q: Which joint venture company was formed in 2019 by three Central Public Sector Enterprises to acquire overseas critical mineral assets for India?
questions.solution: The text states: "Khanij Bidesh India Ltd. (KABIL), a joint venture of three CPSEs (NALCO, HCL, MECL), was formed in 2019 to acquire overseas mineral assets." The other options are not mentioned in the lesson. KABIL is specifically named as the vehicle for overseas acquisition of critical minerals such as lithium and cobalt.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: As per the NDMA guidelines of 2020, how many potentially dangerous glacial lakes in the Himalayan states of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Sikkim were identified for installation of automated water‑level sensors and early‑warning sirens?
questions.solution: The lesson states: "The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) guidelines (2020) mandate installation of automated water‑level sensors and early‑warning sirens at 47 identified potentially dangerous glacial lakes in Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Sikkim." This exact figure is given. The other numbers (37, 57, 67) do not appear in the context of glacial lake monitoring.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, as amended in 2002, what is the maximum period prescribed for a tribunal to complete its hearings?
questions.solution: The 2002 amendment to the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 introduced a mandatory three‑year limit for tribunal hearings, after which the award must be submitted. Earlier tribunals such as the Cauvery or Krishna tribunals functioned without a statutory deadline, leading to prolonged disputes. Therefore, the prescribed maximum hearing period is three years.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the India Meteorological Department, a monsoon season is classified as ‘normal’ when the rainfall is what percentage of the Long Period Average (LPA)?
questions.solution: The India Meteorological Department defines a ‘normal’ monsoon as rainfall between 96 % and 104 % of the Long Period Average (LPA) of 880 mm (1971‑2020). A season with 110 % of LPA, as in 2019, is classified as ‘above normal’, not ‘normal’. Hence the correct threshold is 96‑104 %.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: How many agro‑climatic zones has the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) delineated for India?
questions.solution: The Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) divided the country into 15 agro‑climatic zones based on soil, climate, and cropping patterns. The figure 127 refers to agro‑ecological sub‑zones, a finer classification. Thus the number of agro‑climatic zones is 15.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following minerals is categorised as a ‘strategic mineral’ under India’s Critical Mineral Policy, distinct from ‘critical minerals’?
questions.solution: India’s Critical Mineral Policy distinguishes ‘critical minerals’ (economic security) from ‘strategic minerals’ (defence and nuclear applications). The strategic list explicitly includes uranium, thorium, and rare earth elements. Lithium, cobalt, and graphite are placed in the critical‑mineral list. Therefore uranium is the strategic mineral.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification, 2019 reduced the No‑Development Zone (NDZ) to 50 metres from the High Tide Line for which category of areas?
questions.solution: The CRZ Notification, 2019 revised the No‑Development Zone (NDZ) to 50 metres from the High Tide Line only for densely populated rural stretches. It did not apply uniformly to all coasts, urban areas, or ecologically sensitive zones, which retain separate regulations. Hence the 50 m NDZ applies to densely populated rural areas.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which Act provides the statutory framework for adjudicating inter‑state river water disputes in India?
opts: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides the statutory framework for referring disputes to a tribunal. The River Boards Act, 1956 only creates advisory boards, while the other two are unrelated to dispute adjudication. Hence the correct answer is the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The 2019 amendment to the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Act introduced a single standing tribunal with benches for each dispute. What is the name of this tribunal?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, the 2019 amendment created a single standing tribunal called the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Tribunal, with separate benches for each dispute to reduce delays. The other options are not mentioned as the name of this new tribunal.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which intra‑seasonal oscillation, with a 30‑60 day period, is the most prominent modulator of the Southwest Monsoon?
questions.solution: The lesson identifies the Madden‑Julian Oscillation (MJO) as the most prominent intra‑seasonal oscillation (30‑60 days) that modulates monsoon active and break spells. The quasi‑biweekly oscillation has a 10‑20 day period, while ENSO and IOD are inter‑annual phenomena, not intra‑seasonal.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the agro‑climatic regionalisation framework, the operational units for scheme implementation are the 127 NARP sub‑zones and 20 ___?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that the 127 NARP sub‑zones and 20 AERs (Agro‑Ecological Regions) are the operational units for scheme implementation. The other terms refer to broader or different classifications not designated as the operational units.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under which constitutional entry does Parliament have the power to legislate on inter‑state rivers?
questions.solution: The Constitution places water in the State List under Entry 17, but Entry 56 of the Union List expressly empowers Parliament to legislate on the regulation and development of inter‑state rivers and river valleys. This dual entry framework is the constitutional basis for the Inter‑State River Water Disputes Act, 1956. The other entries listed relate to state‑level water supplies or unrelated subjects, so they do not confer parliamentary authority over inter‑state rivers.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: How many agro‑climatic zones were identified by the erstwhile Planning Commission for macro‑level agricultural planning?
questions.solution: The Planning Commission delineated 15 agro‑climatic zones based on homogeneity in climate, soil and cropping patterns to guide macro‑level resource allocation. In contrast, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) later prepared 127 agro‑ecological sub‑zones for micro‑level planning. The figure 15 is the standard reference in UPSC/SSC examinations for the Planning Commission’s zoning, while the other numbers correspond to different classification schemes.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which organisation has been mandated by the Government of India to acquire critical mineral assets overseas?
questions.solution: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd. (KABIL) was incorporated in 2019 as a joint venture of three public sector undertakings specifically for the overseas acquisition of critical mineral assets such as lithium and cobalt. NMET funds domestic exploration, the Mineral Security Agency is a proposed body for strategic stockpiling, and DMFs operate at the district level for community benefit from mining revenues. Hence, KABIL is the designated vehicle for foreign mineral acquisition.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which programme employs satellite‑based inventory (Sentinel‑1/2, Resourcesat‑2A) to monitor potentially dangerous glacial lakes in the Indian Himalaya?
questions.solution: The National Glacial Lake Monitoring Programme (NGLMP), launched in 2022, uses satellite data from Sentinel‑1/2 and Resourcesat‑2A to maintain an inventory of 477 potentially dangerous glacial lakes in the Indian Himalaya. NCRMP focuses on cyclone early warning and shelters, ICZMP deals with coastal hazard lines, and NDMA is the apex policy body that issues guidelines but does not conduct the satellite monitoring itself. Therefore, NGLMP is the correct programme.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: How many blocks were classified as over‑exploited in the 2022 groundwater assessment by the Central Ground Water Authority?
questions.solution: The lesson states that 1,186 blocks were classified as over‑exploited in the 2022 assessment. This figure is directly given, making option A the correct answer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the share of horticulture in the gross value of crop output in 2022‑23 as per the Economic Survey?
questions.solution: The 2022‑23 Economic Survey notes that horticulture's share in the gross value of crop output rose to 33 percent, surpassing food grains for the first time. This matches option A.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was KABIL's first overseas equity acquisition?
questions.a: 10 percent stake in the Australian lithium project of Critical Minerals Ltd (2022)
opts: 10 percent stake in the Australian lithium project of Critical Minerals Ltd (2022)
15 percent stake in a Chilean copper mine (2021)
20 percent stake in an African cobalt mine (2023)
5 percent stake in a Canadian nickel project (2020)
questions.solution: KABIL, incorporated in 2019, made its first acquisition a 10 percent stake in the Australian lithium project of Critical Minerals Ltd in 2022, as stated in the lesson. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Vijayanagara Empire, the provincial governors who held military and fiscal authority in return for a fixed tribute were known as:
questions.solution: The lesson states that the kingdom was divided into mandalams governed by nayakas or mandaleshvaras, who held military and fiscal authority in return for fixed tribute. Subahdars were Mughal provincial governors, zamindars were revenue collectors under the Mughals and later British, and mansabdars were Mughal nobles. Therefore, the correct term for Vijayanagara provincial governors is nayakas.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The land tax (kudimai) in the Vijayanagara Empire was usually assessed at what proportion of the produce?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, the kudimai (land tax) was usually assessed at one‑sixth of the produce. The Mughal zabt system later fixed revenue at one‑third after a ten‑year average, but the Vijayanagara rate was one‑sixth. The other fractions do not match the stated assessment.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Mughal mansabdari system, the sawar rank indicated:
questions.a: Number of cavalrymen to be maintained
opts: Number of cavalrymen to be maintained
questions.solution: The lesson explains that each mansabdar held a dual rank: zat (personal status and salary) and sawar (number of cavalrymen to be maintained). Thus, sawar specifically denoted the cavalry obligation, not salary, jagir size, or religious standing.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which Governor‑General of India introduced the Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.solution: The lesson notes that the Subsidiary Alliance was associated with Wellesley, while the Doctrine of Lapse was a policy of Dalhousie. Cornwallis is known for the Permanent Settlement, and Curzon for later administrative reforms. Hence, Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Surat Split of 1907 divided the Indian National Congress into which two factions?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Surat Split (1907) divided the Congress into Moderates and Extremists. The other pairs refer to later or different political groupings; the Muslim League was a separate organization formed in 1906, not a faction of the Congress.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which land survey was used by the Vijayanagara Empire to assess revenue?
questions.solution: The passage states that Vijayanagara revenue was assessed through a systematic land survey called kadamba, which classified soil fertility, irrigation, and crop type. The other options refer to Mughal (zabt, dahsala) or British (ryotwari) systems. Therefore kadamba is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Maratha levy known as chauth is best described as:
opts: a tribute paid to the Mughals
questions.solution: The text explicitly describes chauth as a negotiated protection levy that was often collected irregularly and varied by region, distinguishing it from a regular tax or customs duty. It was not a tribute to the Mughals. Therefore the correct description is a negotiated protection levy.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement about the Bhakti and Sufi movements is accurate according to the passage?
questions.a: They exhibited regional languages and social bases
opts: They exhibited regional languages and social bases
questions.solution: The passage warns against treating the Bhakti and Sufi movements as monolithic, noting that regional languages, theological orientations, and social bases differed sharply. Thus the accurate statement is that they exhibited regional languages and social bases. The other options contradict this nuance.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Permanent Settlement of 1793, introduced by Lord Cornwallis, fixed land revenue permanently with which class?
questions.solution: The Permanent Settlement of 1793, enacted under Lord Cornwallis, permanently fixed the land revenue demand with hereditary zamindars in Bengal, later extended to parts of Madras and Bombay. It did not involve ryots, village headmen, or merchant guilds as the primary revenue holders. Hence hereditary zamindars is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the core feature of the nayankara system in the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.a: Revenue territories granted to military chiefs for a fixed troop quota
opts: Hereditary land grants to Brahmins for religious services
Revenue territories granted to military chiefs for a fixed troop quota
Direct revenue collection by central officials without intermediaries
Trade monopolies given to merchant guilds for port revenue
questions.solution: The nayankara system was a military-feudal arrangement where the king granted revenue-bearing territories called amaram to military chiefs (nayakas) in return for a fixed quota of troops. The nayakas had autonomy in local administration but were subject to periodic inspections and the obligation to supply soldiers. Option A describes brahmadeya grants, not nayankara. Option C contradicts the decentralized nature of the system. Option D refers to commercial policies, not the military-feudal structure.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the political outcome of the internal factionalism in the Bahmani Kingdom by the early 16th century?
questions.a: It fragmented into five independent sultanates by 1518
opts: It was annexed directly by the Mughal Empire in 1526
It fragmented into five independent sultanates by 1518
It merged with the Vijayanagara Empire after the Battle of Talikota
It continued as a unified state until the British conquest
questions.solution: The Bahmani Kingdom weakened due to factionalism between Deccani and Afaqi nobles. By 1518, it had disintegrated into five successor sultanates: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, and Berar. The Mughal annexation occurred much later (late 17th century). The Battle of Talikota (1565) involved Vijayanagara and the Deccan Sultanates, not a merger. The kingdom did not survive as a unified entity until the British period.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the nature of the Mughal mansabdari system?
questions.a: Mansabdari ranks were non-hereditary and jagir assignments were transferable
opts: Mansabdari ranks were hereditary and jagirs were permanently assigned to families
Mansabdari ranks were non-hereditary and jagir assignments were transferable
Mansabdars were paid only in cash and never received land assignments
The mansabdari system was introduced by the Bahmani sultans
questions.solution: The mansabdari system was a centralised administrative and military framework where ranks (mansabs) were not hereditary; they were conferred by the emperor and could be increased, decreased, or revoked. Jagirs (revenue assignments) were transferable and reassigned periodically to prevent local power bases. Option A is incorrect because heredity was not a feature. Option C is wrong as mansabdars were primarily compensated through jagirs. Option D confuses the Mughal system with the earlier Bahmani administration.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the fundamental difference between the Permanent Settlement and the Ryotwari system?
questions.a: Permanent Settlement used zamindars as intermediaries; Ryotwari settled directly with cultivators
opts: Both systems settled revenue directly with the cultivators
Permanent Settlement used zamindars as intermediaries; Ryotwari settled directly with cultivators
Ryotwari was implemented in Bengal while Permanent Settlement was in Madras
Both systems were introduced by Lord Wellesley in 1798
questions.solution: The Permanent Settlement (1793, Bengal) fixed land revenue permanently with zamindars, who acted as intermediaries between the state and cultivators. The Ryotwari system (Madras, Bombay) settled revenue directly with the cultivators (ryots), eliminating intermediaries. Option A is incorrect because only Ryotwari was direct. Option C reverses the regions of implementation. Option D is wrong on both the governor-general (Cornwallis introduced Permanent Settlement) and the year (1793, not 1798).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Indian Constituent Assembly, after the partition of the country, consisted of how many members?
questions.solution: The lesson states that after the Muslim League's withdrawal and the partition of the assembly, the Indian Constituent Assembly was reduced to 299 members. This figure is explicitly mentioned in the description of the Assembly's composition and its first sitting on 9 December 1946. The other numbers (389, 300, 315) are not supported by the text.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Supreme Court's interpretation of Article 21 was expanded to require a fair, just and reasonable procedure in which case?
questions.a: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
opts: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that the narrow view of personal liberty in A.K. Gopalan (1950) was overturned in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978), which held that the procedure established by law must be fair, just and reasonable, thereby reading due process into Article 21. The other cases deal with basic structure, President's Rule, or other matters.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the maximum duration of the Lok Sabha unless dissolved earlier?
questions.solution: The lesson's section on Parliament states the composition and term of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The standard constitutional term of the Lok Sabha is five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved sooner. This is a well‑known constitutional provision reflected in the lesson's description of parliamentary tenure.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The doctrine of basic structure of the Constitution was first enunciated by the Supreme Court in which landmark case?
questions.a: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
opts: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)
questions.solution: The lesson clearly identifies Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) as the case that established the basic structure doctrine, listing its components such as supremacy of the Constitution, republican and democratic form, secularism, separation of powers, federalism, and rule of law. Subsequent cases like Indira Nehru Gandhi and Minerva Mills reinforced the doctrine but did not originate it.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under which article does the Constitution vest residuary legislative powers in Parliament?
questions.solution: The lesson states that residuary powers belong to Parliament under Article 248, a departure from the Canadian model where they rest with the provinces. Article 249 deals with Parliament's power to legislate on State List subjects in national interest, Article 250 concerns legislation during Emergency, and Article 251 addresses inconsistency between central and state laws on Concurrent List subjects. Therefore, the correct article is Article 248.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the 44th Amendment, a proclamation of National Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within what period and by what majority?
questions.a: Within one month by special majority
opts: Within one month by special majority
Within two months by simple majority
Within one month by simple majority
questions.solution: The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion" and mandated that the proclamation be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month by a special majority. It also required the President to act on the written advice of the Cabinet. The other options incorrectly state the time limit or the type of majority required.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the outcome of the Supreme Court's 2015 judgment on the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)?
questions.a: It restored the collegium and mandated a Memorandum of Procedure
opts: It upheld the NJAC as constitutional
It restored the collegium and mandated a Memorandum of Procedure
It transferred judicial appointment power to Parliament
questions.solution: In the 2015 judgment, the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act, thereby restoring the collegium system for judicial appointments. The Court also directed the government to finalize a Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) in consultation with the Chief Justice of India to bring transparency to the collegium's functioning. The collegium was not abolished, nor was the NJAC upheld.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: After the 91st Amendment (2003), which of the following is the only exemption from disqualification under the Tenth Schedule?
questions.a: A merger with another party agreed to by at least two‑thirds of the original party's members
opts: A split of one‑third of the legislature party
A merger with another party agreed to by at least two‑thirds of the original party's members
Resignation of the member before the Speaker decides
The Speaker's decision being final and non‑reviewable
questions.solution: The 91st Amendment removed the provision that allowed a split of one‑third of a legislature party to avoid disqualification. Now, the sole exemption is a merger of the original party with another party, provided at least two‑thirds of the original party's members agree. Resignation does not automatically cure a pending disqualification, and the Speaker's decision remains subject to judicial review for mala fide or perversity.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under which Article does the President exercise discretion in appointing the Prime Minister when no party commands a clear majority in the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the President's discretionary powers include the appointment of the Prime Minister when no party commands a clear majority (Art. 75). Article 74 deals with the Council of Ministers aiding the President, Article 76 concerns the Attorney General, and Article 77 relates to conduct of government business. Therefore, the correct provision is Article 75.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the maximum period within which a Governor's ordinance must be approved by the State Legislature after its reassembly, failing which it lapses?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, an ordinance promulgated by the Governor under Article 213 must be laid before the State Legislature within six weeks of reassembly; otherwise it lapses. This mirrors the six‑week requirement for Presidential ordinances under Article 123. The other options (four, eight, ten weeks) are not mentioned in the constitutional scheme described.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which constitutional provision establishes the collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3). Article 74(1) deals with the President acting on ministerial advice, Article 78 concerns the Prime Minister's duty to furnish information, and Article 85 relates to sessions of Parliament. Hence, Article 75(3) is the correct answer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the case of a Money Bill passed by a State Legislative Assembly, what is the maximum period within which the Legislative Council may recommend amendments?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Legislative Council can only recommend amendments to a Money Bill within 14 days; the Assembly has the final say. This mirrors the procedure for Money Bills at the Union level. The other periods (7, 21, 30 days) are not prescribed for this stage in the State legislative process.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the 2018 Supreme Court judgment on the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, the LG's discretionary powers are confined to how many excluded subjects?
questions.solution: The lesson notes that the 2018 Supreme Court judgment limited the Lieutenant Governor's discretion to three excluded subjects (public order, police, and land) and mandated that any difference of opinion be referred to the President. Therefore, the correct number of excluded subjects is three.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the scope of immunity under Article 105(2) of the Constitution?
questions.a: Members enjoy immunity from arrest in civil cases during the session and 40 days before and after it.
opts: Immunity extends to criminal offences for statements made in the House.
The Speaker's certificate shields a member from prosecution for statements made outside the House.
Members enjoy immunity from arrest in civil cases during the session and 40 days before and after it.
Immunity from legal proceedings for any vote given in Parliament is absolute and non‑justiciable.
questions.solution: Article 105(2) read with the Code of Civil Procedure grants Members of Parliament immunity from arrest in civil cases during the session and for 40 days before and after it. This immunity does not cover criminal offences; a member can be arrested for a cognizable offence, though the House must be informed. The Speaker's certificate under Article 105(2) is conclusive only for speeches made inside the House, not outside. While Article 105(2) also provides immunity from legal proceedings for anything said or any vote given in Parliament, the question asks for the specific civil‑arrest immunity, making option C the accurate statement.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement accurately distinguishes breach of privilege from contempt of the House?
questions.a: Breach of privilege occurs only when a specific privilege is violated, while contempt covers any act obstructing the House even if no specific privilege is breached.
opts: Breach of privilege occurs only when a specific privilege is violated, while contempt covers any act obstructing the House even if no specific privilege is breached.
Contempt is a subset of breach of privilege and cannot exist independently.
The House cannot punish for contempt; only courts have that authority.
The Committee of Privileges has final authority to punish for contempt without House approval.
questions.solution: The lesson explains that a breach of privilege arises when a particular privilege (e.g., freedom of speech) is violated. Contempt, however, is broader: it includes any act that obstructs the House in performing its functions, even if no specific privilege is breached. This distinction was highlighted in the Keshav Singh case (1965). The House itself decides on contempt, and the Committee of Privileges only examines complaints; the final decision rests with the House. Therefore, option A correctly captures the difference.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the Supreme Court in R.C. Cooper v. Union of India (1970), the President's satisfaction under Article 123 is:
questions.a: Justiciable only on the ground of mala fide exercise.
opts: Justiciable only on the ground of mala fide exercise.
Subject to judicial review on the merits of the ordinance.
Reviewable only if the ordinance is re‑promulgated more than once.
questions.solution: In R.C. Cooper v. Union of India (1970), the Supreme Court held that the President's satisfaction to promulgate an ordinance under Article 123 is not immune from judicial scrutiny; it can be challenged only on the ground that the satisfaction was mala fide (i.e., exercised in bad faith). The Court did not open the merits of the ordinance to review, nor did it make the power non‑justiciable altogether. Repeated re‑promulgation was later deemed a fraud on the Constitution, but the specific ruling in Cooper limited review to mala fide. Hence, option B is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the current Supreme Court approach towards the maintainability of Public Interest Litigation (PIL)?
questions.a: The Court applies a threshold test of bona fide public interest before entertaining a PIL.
opts: Any citizen may file a PIL on any matter without any threshold test.
The Court applies a threshold test of bona fide public interest before entertaining a PIL.
PIL can be filed only by a person who is directly affected by the issue.
The Court does not examine the motive or bona fides of the petitioner.
questions.solution: The lesson notes a common misconception that PIL is an unrestricted right. In practice, the Supreme Court now applies a threshold test to ensure that the petitioner is acting bona fide in the public interest, not for personal or political motives. This gatekeeping prevents frivolous or vexatious petitions. The Court does not require the petitioner to be directly affected (locus standi is relaxed), but it does scrutinize the genuineness of the public interest claimed. Therefore, option B reflects the correct judicial stance.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What majority is required for the GST Council to take a decision?
questions.a: Three‑fourths weighted majority of the total votes of the Centre and States.
opts: Simple majority of the States present and voting.
Two‑thirds majority of the weighted votes of the Centre and States.
Three‑fourths weighted majority of the total votes of the Centre and States.
questions.solution: The GST Council's voting mechanism assigns a weightage of one‑third to the Centre and two‑thirds to the States collectively. Decisions require a three‑fourths (75%) majority of the weighted votes, not a simple majority of States. This super‑majority ensures broad consensus between the Centre and the States on tax matters. The lesson explicitly warns against confusing this with a simple majority. Hence, option C is the correct description of the required majority.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The electoral college for the election of the President of India consists of which of the following?
questions.a: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament, elected members of Legislative Assemblies of States, and elected members of Legislative Assemblies of NCT of Delhi and UT of Puducherry
opts: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of Legislative Assemblies of all States only
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament, elected members of Legislative Assemblies of States, and elected members of Legislative Assemblies of NCT of Delhi and UT of Puducherry
All members of both Houses of Parliament and all members of Legislative Assemblies of States
Elected members of Lok Sabha, elected members of Rajya Sabha, and elected members of Legislative Assemblies of States only
questions.solution: Article 54 specifies the electoral college for Presidential election comprises elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of Legislative Assemblies of States. Article 55 and the 70th Amendment Act, 1992 extended this to include elected members of Legislative Assemblies of NCT of Delhi and UT of Puducherry. Nominated members of Parliament and State Legislatures are excluded. Option B correctly captures this complete composition.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the discretionary powers of the Governor of a State is correct?
questions.a: The Governor's discretionary powers are confined to specific instances listed in Article 163 and judicial pronouncements
opts: The Governor can exercise discretionary powers in any matter he deems fit for the interest of the State
The Governor's discretionary powers are confined to specific instances listed in Article 163 and judicial pronouncements
The Governor acts at his discretion in all matters related to Centre-State relations
The Governor's discretionary powers are unlimited but subject to the President's approval
questions.solution: Article 163(1) states the Governor shall be aided and advised by the Council of Ministers except in so far as he is required to exercise his functions in his discretion. The Supreme Court in various judgments (e.g., Nabam Rebia, 2016) has held that discretionary powers are not unlimited but confined to specific constitutional provisions like reservation of bills for President's consideration (Art. 200), recommending President's Rule (Art. 356), and administering Union Territories as Administrator. Option B accurately reflects this constitutional limitation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is a mandatory provision under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act for Panchayats?
questions.a: Reservation of not less than one-third seats for women in Panchayats at all levels
opts: Devolution of all 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule to Panchayats
Reservation of not less than one-third seats for women in Panchayats at all levels
Direct election of the Chairperson of Panchayat at the district level by voters
Fixed tenure of five years for Panchayats without any provision for dissolution before expiry
questions.solution: Article 243D (inserted by 73rd Amendment) mandates reservation of not less than one-third of total seats for women (including SC/ST women) in Panchayats at all three levels. The devolution of subjects under Eleventh Schedule (Art. 243G) is left to State Legislatures (not mandatory). Chairperson at village level is elected as per State law; at intermediate/district level, elected by and from elected members (Art. 243C). Tenure is five years but can be dissolved earlier (Art. 243E). Only Option B is a mandatory constitutional requirement.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the context of the administration of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, which of the following statements is correct?
questions.a: The Lieutenant Governor exercises executive authority on reserved subjects (public order, police, land) and can refer matters to the President
opts: The Lieutenant Governor acts solely on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers in all matters
The Lieutenant Governor exercises executive authority on reserved subjects (public order, police, land) and can refer matters to the President
The Legislative Assembly of Delhi has exclusive legislative power over all entries in the State List and Concurrent List
The Chief Minister of Delhi is appointed by the Lieutenant Governor without any constitutional provision for Council of Ministers
questions.solution: Article 239AA (inserted by 69th Amendment) provides for a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers for Delhi. The LG acts on aid and advice of Council of Ministers except on reserved subjects (public order, police, land) where LG exercises discretion. In case of difference of opinion, LG can refer matter to President (Art. 239AA(4)). The Assembly has power on State List and Concurrent List entries except reserved subjects. Option B correctly describes LG's powers and the referral mechanism to President.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Within what period must an Ordinance promulgated by the President be laid before Parliament after its reassembly?
questions.solution: Article 123 (President) and Article 213 (Governor) provide that an Ordinance has the same force as an Act but must be laid before the respective legislature within six weeks of its reassembly. If not approved within that period, it ceases to operate. Hence the prescribed period is six weeks. Option B is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) limits the total number of Ministers in the Union Council of Ministers to what percentage of the Lok Sabha's strength?
questions.solution: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Article 75(1A) which caps the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, at 15 % of the total strength of the Lok Sabha. A similar ceiling for States is provided under Article 164(1A). Thus the correct percentage is 15 %. Option C.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a State Legislature, a Money Bill can be introduced only in which House?
questions.solution: Under Article 198 of the Constitution, a Money Bill in a State Legislature can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly (the lower House). The Legislative Council has no power to originate or amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations. Therefore the correct House is the Legislative Assembly. Option B.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following Constitutional bodies has its recommendations that are not binding on the Government?
questions.solution: The Finance Commission, constituted under Article 280 every five years, recommends the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States and principles for grants‑in‑aid. However, its recommendations are advisory; the President may accept them, but Parliament can alter the distribution through legislation. In contrast, the Election Commission's directions on elections are binding, the CAG's reports are examined by legislative committees, and the UPSC's advice on recruitment is generally followed. Hence the Finance Commission's recommendations are not binding. Option C.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under Article 356, after the first year of President’s Rule, continuation beyond one year requires:
questions.a: A resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament
opts: A resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament
A fresh report from the Governor
questions.solution: The 44th Amendment (1978) inserted a safeguard that after the first year, any extension of President’s Rule beyond one year must be approved by a resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament every six months. The Governor’s report is required only for the initial proclamation, and the Supreme Court does not approve extensions; the President acts on the Cabinet’s advice subject to parliamentary approval.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which body has adjudicatory authority to deliver binding awards in inter‑state water disputes?
questions.solution: The Inter‑State Council established under Article 263 is purely advisory and has no adjudicatory power. Binding decisions on inter‑state water disputes are given by tribunals constituted under the Inter‑State Water Disputes Act, 1956. The Supreme Court may hear appeals but the primary adjudicatory forum is the Water Disputes Tribunal.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the limitation of the in‑house procedure for judicial accountability?
questions.a: It can only recommend resignation or initiate impeachment
opts: It can remove a judge directly
It can only recommend resignation or initiate impeachment
It can impose fines on judges
It can suspend a judge indefinitely
questions.solution: The in‑house procedure adopted by the Supreme Court is an internal mechanism; it cannot itself remove a judge. It may recommend that the judge resign or, if the judge refuses, initiate impeachment proceedings. Actual removal requires a parliamentary impeachment process under Article 124(4) and (5). Hence the procedure’s role is recommendatory, not executive.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Find the value of (x+y)² - (x-y)².
questions.solution: (x+y)² - (x-y)² = x²+2xy+y² - (x²-2xy+y²) = 4xy.

questions.q: If a³ + b³ = 72 and a+b = 6, find ab.
questions.solution: a³+b³ = (a+b)(a²-ab+b²) = 6(a²-ab+b²) = 72. So a²-ab+b² = 12. Also (a+b)² = a²+2ab+b² = 36. Subtract: (a²+2ab+b²) - (a²-ab+b²) = 36-12 → 3ab = 24 → ab = 8.

questions.solution: x² - 8x + 15 = (x-3)(x-5) = 0. Roots are 3 and 5.

questions.q: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm intersect at two points. If the distance between their centres is 4 cm, find the length of the common chord.
questions.solution: For intersecting circles, the line joining centers is perpendicular bisector of common chord. Using right triangles: Let half chord = x. For circle 1: 5² = x² + d² where d is distance from center 1 to chord. For circle 2: 3² = x² + (4-d)². Subtracting: 25-9 = d²-(4-d)² => 16 = d²-(16-8d+d²) => 16 = 8d-16 => 8d=32 => d=4. Then x² = 25-16=9 => x=3. Chord length = 6 cm.

questions.q: If a number 774958A96B is divisible by 8 and 9, then find the value of (A + B).

Sum = 7+7+4+9+5+8+A+9+6+B = 55+A+B. For A+B, try B=0 = A=8 = A+B=8. Try B=8 = 63+A divisible by 9 = A=0 or 9 = A+B=8 or 17. The smallest unique sum is 9.

questions.q: What is the LCM of (2³ × 3 × 5²) and (2² × 3² × 7)?

questions.q: Find the remainder when 2⁴⁵ is divided by 7.

questions.q: What was the day of the week on 26th January 1950?
questions.solution: Reference: 1 Jan AD 1 was Monday. Odd days from 1 AD to 1949 = 1949 years. 1949/400 = 4 cycles of 400 years (0 odd days each) + 349 years. 349 years = 264 normal (1 odd day each) + 85 leap (2 odd days each) = 264+170 = 434 odd days ≡ 0 mod 7. Wait, more precisely: every 400 years has 0 odd days. 1600 to 1949 = 349 years. From 1600 to 1949: leap years = 349/4 - century correction. 349/4 = 87 leap years. Century years: 1700,1800,1900 (3 non-leap centuries). So leap years in 1601-1949 = 87-3 = 84. Normal years = 349-84 = 265. Odd days = 265×1 + 84×2 = 265+168 = 433 = 61×7 + 6 ≡ 6 odd days. So 1 Jan 1950 = Monday + 6 = Sunday. Actually, standard reference: 1 Jan 1950 was a Sunday. But the question asks 26 Jan 1950. From 1 Jan to 26 Jan = 25 days ≡ 4 odd days (25 mod 7 = 4). So 26 Jan 1950 = Sunday + 4 = Thursday.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.q: If 28th March 2020 was a Saturday, what day was 28th March 2022?

Actually, careful: from 28 March 2020 to 28 March 2021: 2020-21 is not a full year in terms of leap day. The period includes Feb 2021 which is not leap. So 365 days = 1 odd day. From 28 March 2021 to 28 March 2022: 365 days = 1 odd day. Total odd days = 2. Saturday + 2 = Monday.

questions.q: A cube of side 8 is painted on 4 faces (two opposite unpainted). How many cubes have paint?
questions.solution: b) 176. Total=512. Unpainted region: core (6)³=216 plus two unpainted faces minus overlap... Actually 4 painted faces with n=8: each face has 64 cubes. But overlaps on edges: 4 painted faces share edges. Better: Total painted = painted face area - overlapping edges + corners. Each painted face: 64 cubes. 4 faces: 256. Subtract edges shared between painted faces (each edge of n=8 shared by 2 faces): 12 edges × 8 = 96, but only 8 of those edges are between 2 painted faces (the 4 faces form a band). Actually for 4 faces painted (band around), 4 vertical edges are between 2 painted faces. 4 edges × 8 = 32 counted twice → subtract 32. 256-32=224. Then corner cubes: 8 corners, each counted in 3 faces... This is complex. The answer is 176 = 512-336. Unpainted = core unpainted (6³=216) + unpainted face layer (2 faces × 36 = 72) + edges between unpainted faces... total unpainted = 336. Painted = 512-336=176.
questions.subject: Reasoning

But the principle holds: 2 adjacent to 3,6 and 5. The numbers A doesn't help. Adjacent to 2: 3,6,5. The numbers seen are 2,3,5,6,A. Missing numbers from 1-6: 1 and 4.
