questions.solution: BOD5 is measured by incubating the water sample at 20°C in the dark for 5 days. The difference in DO before and after incubation gives the BOD value.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT directly involved in the catalytic destruction of stratospheric ozone?
questions.solution: CO2 is a greenhouse gas and does not participate in ozone destruction reactions. Cl, Br, NO, and OH radicals are all involved in catalytic ozone depletion cycles in the stratosphere.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Minamata disease is caused by the bioaccumulation of:
questions.solution: Minamata disease (Japan, 1956) is caused by methylmercury poisoning from industrial wastewater. Mercury bioaccumulates in fish, and consumption leads to severe neurological damage.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The pollutant responsible for marble cancer (Taj Mahal deterioration) is:
questions.solution: SO2 from the Mathura oil refinery forms H2SO4 in the atmosphere, which reacts with marble (CaCO3) to form gypsum (CaSO4). This causes surface erosion known as marble cancer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following gases has the highest Global Warming Potential (GWP)?
questions.solution: CFC-12 (CF2Cl2) has GWP ~10,900 over 100 years, which is the highest among common GHGs due to strong IR absorption and long atmospheric lifetime (100+ years). CO2 has GWP=1, CH4=25, N2O=298.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In wastewater treatment, the activated sludge process is a type of:
questions.solution: The activated sludge process is a secondary (biological) treatment method where aerobic microorganisms consume biodegradable organic matter in the presence of oxygen, reducing BOD by 85-95%.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The main reason for the Antarctic ozone hole is:
questions.solution: Polar stratospheric clouds (PSCs) form in the extremely cold Antarctic winter and provide surfaces for heterogeneous reactions that convert inactive chlorine reservoirs (HCl, ClONO2) into reactive Cl2, which photolyses in spring to release ozone-destroying Cl radicals.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: An example of a non-biodegradable pollutant is:
questions.solution: DDT is an organochlorine pesticide that is highly persistent and non-biodegradable (resists microbial degradation due to stable C-Cl bonds). It bioaccumulates and biomagnifies in food chains. Vegetable peels, paper, and cotton cloth are biodegradable.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The most stable carbocation among the following is:
questions.solution: Tertiary carbocation (3°) has maximum hyperconjugation (9 alpha-H) and is most stable.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which reagent is used to convert a carboxylic acid to an acid chloride?
questions.solution: All three (PCl₃, SOCl₂, PCl₅) convert RCOOH to RCOCl, but SOCl₂ is preferred because the by-products (SO₂, HCl) are gaseous. Hence option (d).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following shows geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution: But-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) has two different groups on each sp² carbon, so it exhibits cis-trans isomerism.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The product of the reaction of aniline with Br₂ water is:
questions.solution: Aniline is highly activating; undergoes tribromination in Br₂ water to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (white precipitate).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a condensation polymer?
questions.solution: Polythene is an addition polymer (free radical polymerization of ethene). Nylon-66, Terylene, and Bakelite are condensation polymers.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Lucas test is used to distinguish between:
questions.solution: Lucas reagent (ZnCl₂ + HCl) differentiates alcohols by turbidity: 3° immediate, 2° in 5-10 min, 1° no reaction at RT.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is a disaccharide?
questions.solution: Sucrose (glucose + fructose) is a disaccharide. Glucose/fructose are monosaccharides; cellulose is a polysaccharide.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the zeroth law of thermodynamics, if system A is in thermal equilibrium with system C, and system B is also in thermal equilibrium with system C, then A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other. This transitive property primarily enables which of the following?
questions.a: Definition of a temperature scale and calibration of thermometers
opts: Definition of a temperature scale and calibration of thermometers
Calculation of internal energy changes for any process
Determination of entropy changes in reversible cycles
Establishment of the sign convention for heat and work
questions.solution: The zeroth law states that thermal equilibrium is transitive. Because of this, a third body (a thermometer) can be used to compare the thermal state of two separate systems, allowing a consistent temperature scale to be defined. Without this principle, temperature could not be treated as a state function, and quantitative thermometry would be impossible. The other options refer to concepts introduced by the first, second, and third laws or by sign conventions, not by the zeroth law.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the sign convention used in chemistry for the first law (ΔU = q – w), which statement correctly describes the signs of heat (q) and work (w)?
questions.a: q is positive when heat is absorbed by the system; w is positive when work is done by the system
opts: q is positive when heat is released by the system; w is positive when work is done on the system
q is positive when heat is absorbed by the system; w is positive when work is done by the system
Both q and w are positive when energy enters the system
Both q and w are positive when energy leaves the system
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states: "The sign convention adopted in chemistry treats heat absorbed by the system as positive and work done by the system as positive." Therefore, q > 0 for heat input, and w > 0 for work output (expansion work). Option A reverses both signs, option C makes both positive for energy input, and option D makes both positive for energy output. Only option B matches the described convention.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The standard Gibbs free energy change (ΔG°) for a reaction at temperature T is related to the equilibrium constant K by which equation?
questions.solution: From the lesson: "ΔG° = –RT ln K" (or equivalently ΔG° = –2.303 RT log₁₀ K). This relationship follows from ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q and the condition ΔG = 0 at equilibrium (Q = K). Option A has the wrong sign, option C incorrectly places T in the denominator, and option D is dimensionally inconsistent. The negative sign indicates that a large K (product‑favoured) corresponds to a negative ΔG°, i.e., a spontaneous reaction under standard conditions.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For a buffer solution containing a weak acid HA and its conjugate base A⁻, the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation gives the pH as:
questions.solution: The lesson states the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation as pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]). This is derived from Ka = [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA] → –log[H⁺] = –log Ka + log([A⁻]/[HA]). Option A has the wrong sign before the log term, option B inverts the concentration ratio, and option D combines both errors. Only option C reproduces the correct form directly from the text.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: At 298 K, the Nernst equation for a galvanic cell with n electrons transferred and reaction quotient Q simplifies to which expression?
questions.solution: The lesson gives the Nernst equation at 298 K as E = E° – (0.05916/n) log₁₀ Q. The factor 0.05916 V arises from (RT/F) ln 10 at 298 K. The minus sign indicates that increasing Q (more products) lowers the cell potential. Option A has the wrong sign, option C incorrectly multiplies by n instead of dividing, and option D has both sign and n‑dependence errors. Therefore, option B is the exact form stated in the text.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A heat engine operates between a hot reservoir at 500 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K. What is the maximum possible (Carnot) efficiency of this engine?
questions.solution: The Carnot efficiency is given by η = 1 – TC/TH, where temperatures must be in kelvin. Substituting TH = 500 K and TC = 300 K gives η = 1 – 300/500 = 1 – 0.6 = 0.40, i.e. 40%. This is the upper bound for any engine working between these two reservoirs; no real engine can exceed it.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For a 1:1 electrolyte at ionic strength I = 0.001 mol L⁻¹, the Debye–Hückel limiting law (A = 0.509 mol⁻¹ᐟ² L¹ᐟ²) gives log₁₀γ± ≈ ?
questions.solution: The limiting law is log₁₀γ± = –A|z+z–|√I. For a 1:1 electrolyte |z+z–| = 1. √I = √0.001 = 0.03162. Multiplying: –0.509 × 0.03162 ≈ –0.0161. Hence log₁₀γ± ≈ –0.016.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The standard enthalpy change for a reaction is ΔH° = +50 kJ mol⁻¹. According to the Van’t Hoff equation, how does the equilibrium constant K vary with temperature?
questions.solution: The Van’t Hoff equation is d(ln K)/dT = ΔH°/(RT²). With ΔH° > 0 the derivative is positive, so ln K increases with temperature. Therefore K itself increases as T rises.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a redox titration of Fe²⁺ (E° = +0.77 V, n = 1) with MnO₄⁻ (E° = +1.51 V, n = 5), the equivalence‑point potential is calculated using Eeq = (n₁E₁° + n₂E₂°)/(n₁ + n₂). What is Eeq?
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The standard potential of the Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ couple is +0.77 V. In the presence of excess CN⁻ the formal potential shifts to +0.36 V. Which statement correctly explains this shift?
questions.a: Complexation lowers the activity of Fe³⁺ more than Fe²⁺, decreasing the reduction potential.
opts: Complexation lowers the activity of Fe³⁺ more than Fe²⁺, decreasing the reduction potential.
Complexation raises the activity of Fe²⁺ more than Fe³⁺, increasing the reduction potential.
Complexation does not affect the formal potential.
Complexation changes the number of electrons transferred in the half‑reaction.
questions.solution: CN⁻ forms very stable complexes [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ and [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻. The formation constant for the Fe³⁺ complex is larger, so the free Fe³⁺ activity is reduced more than the Fe²⁺ activity. In the Nernst equation E = E° – (0.05916/n)log(a_Fe²⁺/a_Fe³⁺), a smaller a_Fe³⁺ increases the ratio a_Fe²⁺/a_Fe³⁺, making the log term larger and the potential more negative. Hence the formal potential shifts to a lower value (+0.36 V).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which Maxwell relation is derived from the differential of Gibbs free energy dG = –S dT + V dP?
questions.solution: From dG = –S dT + V dP, the natural variables are T and P. Equality of mixed second derivatives gives ∂(–S)/∂P|_T = ∂V/∂T|_P, which simplifies to –(∂S/∂P)_T = (∂V/∂T)_P. Rearranging yields (∂S/∂P)_T = –(∂V/∂T)_P, matching option B.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Clapeyron equation for a first-order phase transition expressed in terms of enthalpy change is:
questions.solution: The Clapeyron equation is dP/dT = ΔS/ΔV. At equilibrium, ΔS = ΔH/T for the phase transition. Substituting gives dP/dT = ΔH/(T ΔV), which is the form in terms of enthalpy change. Option B states this correctly.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Butler–Volmer equation, the overpotential η is defined as:
questions.solution: Overpotential is the deviation of the electrode potential from its equilibrium value. By convention, η = E – E_eq. This sign convention is used in the Butler–Volmer equation to describe activation polarization. Option B matches this definition.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the construction of Pourbaix diagrams, horizontal boundary lines correspond to reactions where:
questions.a: the number of electrons transferred equals the number of protons involved
opts: the number of electrons transferred equals the number of protons involved
no protons participate in the reaction
the slope of the line is zero
questions.solution: The lesson states that horizontal boundaries arise from reactions with equal numbers of electrons and protons (m = n), giving a slope of –0.0591 V/pH. This directly corresponds to option A.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The critical compressibility factor Zc for a Van der Waals gas is:
questions.solution: For a Van der Waals gas, the critical constants yield Zc = Pc Vc / (R Tc) = 3/8 = 0.375. This value is often mistakenly treated as universal for all real fluids. Option A gives the correct fraction.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Onsager's reciprocal relations L_ij = L_ji are valid when the entropy production rate is expressed as a bilinear sum of fluxes and their conjugate forces. Which of the following statements describes this requirement?
questions.a: Entropy production is expressed as sum of products of fluxes and conjugate forces.
opts: Forces are gradients of intensive variables divided by temperature.
Fluxes are linearly related to forces through phenomenological coefficients.
Entropy production is expressed as sum of products of fluxes and conjugate forces.
The system is at thermodynamic equilibrium.
questions.solution: Onsager reciprocity follows from microscopic reversibility and the fluctuation‑dissipation theorem, but it holds only when the forces X_j and fluxes J_i are chosen such that the entropy production per unit volume σ = Σ_i J_i X_i is a bilinear form. This means σ must be written explicitly as the sum of products of each flux with its conjugate thermodynamic force. Option C states exactly this condition. The other options describe related concepts (definition of forces, linear regime, equilibrium) but do not specify the bilinear entropy production requirement that guarantees L_ij = L_ji.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the Kelvin relation derived from Onsager reciprocity, the Peltier coefficient Π and the Seebeck coefficient S are related by:
questions.solution: In the linear regime the Seebeck coefficient is S = (L_qe / L_ee) T and the Peltier coefficient is Π = (L_eq / L_ee) T. Onsager reciprocity gives L_qe = L_eq, therefore Π = S T. This is the Kelvin relation. Option B matches this result. The other options are dimensionally incorrect or represent mis‑remembered forms of the relation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For an electron‑transfer reaction with reorganization energy λ = 1.0 eV and standard free‑energy change ΔG° = –1.5 eV, the Marcus activation free energy ΔG* is:
questions.solution: Marcus theory gives ΔG* = (λ + ΔG°)² / (4λ). Substituting λ = 1.0 eV and ΔG° = –1.5 eV: (1.0 – 1.5)² / (4 × 1.0) = (–0.5)² / 4 = 0.25 / 4 = 0.0625 eV. This value corresponds to the inverted region because –ΔG° (1.5 eV) > λ (1.0 eV). Option A is the correct numerical result.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For a non‑reactive ternary system at constant temperature and pressure, the number of degrees of freedom in a two‑phase region is:
questions.solution: The Gibbs phase rule for a non‑reactive system is F = C – P + 2. At fixed T and P, two intensive variables are removed, so F = C – P. For a ternary system C = 3. In a two‑phase region P = 2, giving F = 3 – 2 = 1. This single degree of freedom corresponds to the composition variable along the tie‑line connecting the two equilibrium phases. Option B is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The molecular partition function q for an ideal gas factorises into translational, rotational, vibrational, and electronic contributions (q = q_trans q_rot q_vib q_elec). Which condition must hold for this factorisation to be valid?
questions.solution: The factorisation of the molecular partition function into independent contributions requires that the energy modes (translation, rotation, vibration, electronic) are separable, meaning the total energy is a sum of independent terms ε = ε_trans + ε_rot + ε_vib + ε_elec. This allows the Boltzmann factor exp(-ε/k_BT) to be written as a product of individual factors, so the sum over states factorises into a product of sums. If particles were distinguishable, the canonical partition function would be Q = q^N without the 1/N! factor, but factorisation of q itself would still hold. Strong intermolecular forces couple the motions of different molecules, breaking the independent-particle approximation. Near absolute zero, quantum effects become important but do not invalidate the factorisation if modes remain separable.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In an Eyring plot of ln(k/T) versus 1/T for a reaction following Transition State Theory, the slope of the straight line gives:
questions.solution: The Eyring equation is k = κ(k_BT/h) exp(-ΔG‡/RT). Substituting ΔG‡ = ΔH‡ - TΔS‡ gives k = κ(k_BT/h) exp(-ΔH‡/RT + ΔS‡/R). Taking the natural logarithm of k/T yields ln(k/T) = ln(κk_B/h) + ΔS‡/R - ΔH‡/RT. A plot of ln(k/T) versus 1/T is therefore linear with slope = -ΔH‡/R and intercept = ΔS‡/R + ln(κk_B/h). The slope directly provides the activation enthalpy ΔH‡. The intercept gives the activation entropy ΔS‡. The activation Gibbs energy ΔG‡ is not obtained directly from the slope.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The reversible voltage of a lithium-ion cell varies with the state of charge because:
questions.a: ΔG of the intercalation reaction depends on stoichiometry
opts: The internal resistance changes with Li content
ΔG of the intercalation reaction depends on stoichiometry
The Nernst equation does not apply to solid-state electrodes
questions.solution: The reversible cell voltage E_rev is related to the Gibbs free energy change by ΔG = -nFE_rev. In a lithium-ion battery, the overall reaction involves lithium intercalation into host structures (e.g., Li_xCoO_2 and Li_xC_6). The Gibbs free energy ΔG of this intercalation reaction depends on the lithium stoichiometry x, which changes during charge/discharge. Consequently, E_rev varies with the state of charge. Internal resistance affects the terminal voltage under current (irreversible polarization), not the reversible voltage. The temperature coefficient (∂E/∂T)_p is generally non-zero and relates to the entropy change. The Nernst equation applies to solid-state electrodes as long as the activities of the intercalated species are properly defined.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Pitzer equations for activity coefficients, the binary parameter β^(0) represents:
opts: A universal constant for all electrolytes
questions.solution: The Pitzer equations extend the Debye-Hückel model to higher ionic strengths by adding terms for short-range specific ion interactions. The parameter β^(0) is a binary interaction parameter that accounts for short-range forces (e.g., van der Waals, specific ion pairing) between a cation and an anion. It is an empirical coefficient determined from experimental data (osmotic coefficients, activity coefficients) for each specific electrolyte pair and varies with temperature. It is not the Debye-Hückel limiting slope (which is a universal function of temperature and solvent dielectric constant), nor does it represent the long-range electrostatic contribution (which is handled by the Debye-Hückel term). It is also not a universal constant; its value differs for different ion combinations.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Jarzynski equality ⟨exp(-W/k_BT)⟩ = exp(-ΔF/k_BT) allows estimation of equilibrium free-energy difference ΔF from non-equilibrium work measurements. A major practical difficulty in applying this equality is:
questions.a: The exponential average is dominated by rare low-work events and converges slowly
opts: The exponential average is dominated by rare low-work events and converges slowly
It only applies to systems at constant volume
The work W must be measured in the reversible limit
It requires knowledge of the transmission coefficient κ
questions.solution: The Jarzynski equality states that the exponential average of the non-equilibrium work W over many trajectories equals exp(-ΔF/k_BT). Because the exponential function weights low-work trajectories heavily, the average is dominated by rare events where the work done is significantly less than the average work. These rare trajectories are difficult to sample, requiring a very large number of experimental or simulation runs to achieve convergence. The equality holds for systems in contact with a heat bath at constant temperature (constant T), not necessarily constant volume. It explicitly applies to irreversible, non-equilibrium processes, not just the reversible limit. The transmission coefficient κ is a concept from Transition State Theory for reaction rates, not from fluctuation theorems.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For a binary mixture described by the two‑parameter Margules equation Gᴱ/RT = x₁x₂(A₂₁x₁ + A₁₂x₂), the activity coefficient of component 1 is given by which expression?
questions.solution: The two‑parameter Margules model writes Gᴱ/RT = x₁x₂(A₂₁x₁ + A₁₂x₂). The activity coefficient of component 1 follows from ln γ₁ = ∂(nGᴱ/RT)/∂n₁ at constant T,P,n₂. Carrying out the differentiation yields ln γ₁ = x₂²[A₁₂ + 2(A₂₁ − A₁₂)x₁]. This matches the standard textbook result and is the expression quoted in the lesson. The other options either interchange indices, omit the square on x₂, or use an incorrect linear dependence.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a Pb–Sn eutectic diagram at 200 °C, an alloy of overall composition 30 wt% Sn lies in the α + liquid region. The liquidus composition at this temperature is 40 wt% Sn and the solidus composition is 10 wt% Sn. What is the mass fraction of the α phase?
questions.solution: The lever rule for a two‑phase region gives the mass fraction of α as (C_liquid − C₀)/(C_liquid − C_solid), where C₀ is the overall composition. Substituting C_liquid = 40, C_solid = 10, C₀ = 30 gives (40 − 30)/(40 − 10) = 10/30 = 0.333. Thus the α phase constitutes one‑third of the total mass. The other options correspond to incorrect applications of the lever rule or simple arithmetic errors.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the Gouy‑Chapman‑Stern model, the differential capacitance of the diffuse layer at low electrolyte concentration exhibits which characteristic shape?
questions.solution: The lesson states that experimental differential capacitance curves for mercury in NaF solutions show a pronounced camel‑shape at low concentration (two maxima) and a bell‑shape at high concentration, consistent with the Gouy‑Chapman‑Stern framework. At low ionic strength the diffuse layer extends far into solution, producing two capacitance maxima (camel shape). As concentration increases, the diffuse layer compresses and the curve becomes a single bell‑shaped maximum. Therefore the correct description for low concentration is camel‑shaped.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A semipermeable membrane separates compartment 1 (containing a non‑diffusible anion A⁻ at concentration c_A and a diffusible salt MX) from compartment 2 (MX at concentration c₂). At Donnan equilibrium, the concentration of cation M⁺ in compartment 1 is given by which expression?
questions.solution: Equality of electrochemical potentials for M⁺ and X⁻ across the membrane gives c_{M,1}c_{X,1} = c₂². Electroneutrality in compartment 1 requires c_{M,1} = c_{X,1} + c_A. Solving these two equations yields a quadratic for c_{M,1}: c_{M,1}² − c_A c_{M,1} − c₂² = 0. The physically meaningful positive root is c_{M,1} = (c_A + √(c_A² + 4c₂²))/2. The other options either take the negative root, ignore the Donnan effect, or equate the concentration to the fixed charge.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For a cyclic reaction mechanism A ⇌ B ⇌ C ⇌ A, the Wegscheider condition (detailed balance) imposes which constraint on the elementary rate constants?
questions.a: k₁f k₂f k₃f = k₁r k₂r k₃r
opts: k₁f k₂f k₃f = k₁r k₂r k₃r
k₁f + k₂f + k₃f = k₁r + k₂r + k₃r
k₁f k₂r k₃f = k₁r k₂f k₃r
questions.solution: The principle of detailed balance requires that at equilibrium each elementary step proceeds forward and reverse at equal rates. For a closed cycle A ⇌ B ⇌ C ⇌ A, the product of the forward rate constants around the cycle must equal the product of the reverse rate constants: k₁f k₂f k₃f = k₁r k₂r k₃r. This is the Wegscheider condition for a single independent cycle. The other options represent incorrect algebraic combinations (ratio equality, sum equality, or mixed products) that do not follow from detailed balance.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The dimensional formula of gravitational constant G is:
questions.solution: F = Gm₁m₂/r² → G = Fr²/m₁m₂ = [MLT⁻²][L²]/[M²] = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²].
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A car moving at 20 m/s applies brakes and stops after 4 s. Find the stopping distance (constant retardation).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A projectile has maximum range of 100 m. Find its velocity of projection. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A block of mass 5 kg is pulled by a force of 25 N at 60° to horizontal. If μₖ = 0.2, find acceleration. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A spring of force constant 100 N/m is stretched by 0.1 m. Find the work done.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A disc and a ring of same mass and radius roll down an incline. Which reaches the bottom first?
questions.solution: a = g sinθ / (1 + I/mR²). For disc I/mR² = ½, for ring = 1. Smaller I/mR² gives larger acceleration. Disc reaches first.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A stone of mass 1 kg is whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1 m at constant speed 5 m/s. Find tension at the lowest point. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution: At lowest point: T - mg = mv²/r → T = mg + mv²/r = 10 + 1×25/1 = 35 N.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the angular momentum of an electron in the 2nd orbit of hydrogen atom? (Given L = nh/2π)
questions.solution: L = nh/2π. For n = 2: L = 2h/2π = h/π.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Two satellites of masses m and 2m orbit Earth at same radius r. Ratio of their orbital speeds is:
questions.solution: vₒ = √(GM/r). Orbital speed is independent of satellite mass. Ratio = 1:1.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A wire of length 1 m and area 2×10⁻⁶ m² is stretched by 0.5 mm under a 200 N force. Find Young's modulus.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Water flows from a tap of radius 0.5 cm at 2 m/s. If the stream radius reduces to 0.25 cm, what is the new speed?
questions.solution: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ → πr₁²v₁ = πr₂²v₂ → v₂ = (r₁/r₂)²v₁ = (0.5/0.25)²×2 = 4×2 = 8 m/s.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A body of mass 2 kg initially at rest is acted upon by a force that does 100 J work. Find its final speed.
questions.solution: Work = ΔKE = ½mv² - 0 → 100 = ½×2×v² → v² = 100 → v = 10 m/s.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 4 kg for 3 s. Find the impulse delivered.
questions.solution: Impulse = F × t = 20 × 3 = 60 N·s.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A circular track has radius 100 m. A car of mass 1200 kg takes a turn at 20 m/s. Find the centripetal force.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A solid cylinder (I = MR²/2) rolls without slipping down an incline of height 15 m. Find speed at bottom. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution: mgh = ½mv² + ½Iω² = ½mv²(1 + ½) = ¾mv². v = √(4gh/3) = √(4×10×15/3) = √200 m/s.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A body of mass 1 kg is acted upon by a force that varies with displacement as F = 2x + 3. Find work done from x = 0 to x = 5 m.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A planet orbits the Sun with period T and semi-major axis a. If semi-major axis becomes 8a, new period is:
questions.solution: T² ∝ a³. T₁²/T₂² = a₁³/a₂³ = (a/8a)³ = 1/512. T₂ = √512 T₁ = 16√2 T.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A ball is dropped from height h and rebounds to height h/4. Find coefficient of restitution.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The stopping potential for photoelectrons from a metal surface is 2 V. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is:
questions.solution: KE_max = eV₀ = e × 2V = 2 eV. The stopping potential directly gives the maximum kinetic energy in eV.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a CE transistor amplifier, the input resistance is 1 kΩ and the load resistance is 5 kΩ. If β = 100, the voltage gain is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The energy of the first line of the Lyman series of hydrogen is: (R = 1.097×10⁷ m⁻¹, hc = 12400 eV·Å)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A p-n junction diode is forward biased when:
questions.a: p-side is positive, n-side is negative
opts: p-side is positive, n-side is negative
p-side is negative, n-side is positive
questions.solution: In forward bias, the p-side is connected to the positive terminal and n-side to the negative terminal of the battery. This reduces the depletion width and allows current flow.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 4 days. What is its mean life?
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For an OR gate, the output is 1 when:
questions.solution: An OR gate gives output 1 when any of its inputs is 1. Y = A + B + ... Output is 0 only when all inputs are 0.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In non-uniform circular motion, the total acceleration vector makes an angle φ with the radial direction. The correct expression for tan φ is:
questions.solution: The radial (centripetal) acceleration is a_r = v²/r directed toward the centre. The tangential acceleration is a_t = rα directed along the velocity. The total acceleration is the vector sum a = a_r + a_t. Since a_r and a_t are perpendicular, the angle φ between a and the radial direction satisfies tan φ = opposite/adjacent = a_t / a_r. This matches the relation φ = tan⁻¹(a_t / a_r) given in the lesson.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A projectile is launched from a plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal with speed u at an angle θ to the horizontal. The time of flight until it strikes the plane again is:
questions.solution: Choosing axes along (x) and perpendicular (y) to the inclined plane, the initial velocity components are u_x = u cos(θ - α) and u_y = u sin(θ - α). The acceleration components are a_x = -g sin α and a_y = -g cos α. The projectile returns to the plane when y = 0, giving 0 = u_y T + ½ a_y T². Solving for T (T ≠ 0) yields T = -2u_y / a_y = 2u sin(θ - α) / (g cos α).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a reference frame rotating with constant angular velocity ω, the Coriolis acceleration term appearing in the equation of motion for a particle moving with velocity v_rot relative to the rotating frame is:
questions.solution: The acceleration in an inertial frame is related to the acceleration in a rotating frame by a_inertial = a_rot + 2 ω × v_rot + ω × (ω × r) + (dω/dt) × r. For constant ω, the term 2 ω × v_rot is the Coriolis acceleration. It is a fictitious acceleration that must be included when writing Newton's second law in the rotating frame. The lesson explicitly mentions the Coriolis term as 2 ω × v_rot.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In plane polar coordinates (r, θ), the radial component of acceleration of a particle is:
questions.solution: The position vector is r = r r̂. Differentiating twice gives velocity v = ṙ r̂ + r θ̇ θ̂ and acceleration a = (r̈ - r θ̇²) r̂ + (r θ̈ + 2 ṙ θ̇) θ̂. The radial component is therefore r̈ - r θ̇². The term -r θ̇² alone is the centripetal acceleration for circular motion (ṙ = 0), but the general radial acceleration includes the radial acceleration r̈ as well.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is an intrinsic semiconductor?
questions.solution: Intrinsic semiconductors are pure (undoped) — equal numbers of electrons and holes. Pure Si and Ge are intrinsic.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a p-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are:
questions.solution: p-type doping (trivalent impurity) creates excess holes. Holes are the majority carriers; electrons are minority carriers.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The knee voltage of a silicon diode is approximately:
questions.solution: Silicon diodes have a knee voltage of ~0.7 V. Germanium diodes have ~0.3 V.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In forward bias, the width of the depletion region:
questions.solution: Forward bias injects majority carriers into the depletion region, neutralising ions and narrowing it.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A Zener diode is used for:
questions.solution: Zener diodes operate in reverse breakdown and maintain a nearly constant voltage across them — ideal for regulation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The current gain β of a transistor in CE mode is 100. If I_B = 20 μA, then I_C is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which gate gives output 1 only when all inputs are 1?
questions.solution: AND gate outputs 1 only when ALL inputs are 1.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The output of a NOR gate is 1 when:
questions.solution: NOR = NOT + OR. The OR part gives 0 when all inputs are 0; NOT inverts to 1.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a common-emitter amplifier, the phase difference between input and output is:
questions.solution: CE amplifier produces a 180° phase shift — output is inverted relative to input.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The efficiency of a full-wave bridge rectifier is approximately:
questions.solution: Full-wave rectifier has efficiency = 81.2%. Half-wave is 40.6%.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Covalent bonds in a semiconductor are broken by:
questions.solution: Thermal energy provides enough energy to break covalent bonds, creating electron-hole pairs.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following has a band gap of about 1.1 eV at room temperature?
questions.solution: Si band gap = 1.1 eV. Ge = 0.67 eV. Copper (conductor) has no gap. Diamond > 5 eV (insulator).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The molar specific heat at constant volume for a monatomic gas is:
questions.solution: For a monatomic gas, f = 3 (translational only). Cv = (f/2)R = (3/2)R = ³⁄₂R.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The RMS speed of oxygen molecules (M = 32 g/mol) at 27°C is approximately:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The ratio of specific heats (γ = Cp/Cv) for a diatomic gas is:
questions.solution: For a diatomic gas (rigid), f = 5. Cv = 5R/2, Cp = 7R/2. γ = Cp/Cv = (7R/2)/(5R/2) = 7/5 = 1.40.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In which thermodynamic process is the work done equal to zero?
questions.solution: In an isochoric process, volume remains constant (ΔV = 0), so work done W = PΔV = 0.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: 100 g of water at 80°C is mixed with 200 g of water at 20°C. The final temperature is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A black body at 500 K radiates energy at a certain rate. If its temperature is increased to 1000 K, the rate increases by a factor of:
questions.solution: Stefan-Boltzmann law: P ∝ T⁴. P₂/P₁ = (T₂/T₁)⁴ = (1000/500)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The mean free path of gas molecules is λ. If pressure is doubled at constant temperature, the new mean free path is:
questions.solution: λ = kT/(√2 π d² P). At constant T, λ ∝ 1/P. So if P doubles, λ becomes λ/2.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A heat engine has 40% efficiency. If it rejects 300 J to the sink per cycle, the heat absorbed from the source is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A gas (γ = 5/3) at 300 K is compressed adiabatically to 1/8 of its initial volume. The final temperature is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: When 1 g of steam at 100°C condenses to water at 100°C, the heat released is: (Lv = 540 cal/g)
questions.solution: Heat released = m × Lv = 1 g × 540 cal/g = 540 cal.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A gas expands from 2 L to 6 L isothermally at 300 K. If the initial pressure is 3 atm, the work done is: (1 L atm = 101.3 J)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: For which gas is Cv = 3R?
questions.solution: For polyatomic gas, f = 6. Cv = (f/2)R = 3R.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The coefficient of performance of a Carnot refrigerator operating between 27°C and −3°C is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string depends on:
questions.solution: v = √(T/μ). It depends only on tension T and linear mass density μ. Frequency and amplitude do not affect wave speed.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A wave is given by y = 0.05 sin(200πt - 2πx). Find the wave speed.
questions.solution: Comparing with y = A sin(ωt - kx): ω = 200π, k = 2π. v = ω/k = 200π/2π = 100 m/s.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a stationary wave, the distance between a node and the next antinode is:
questions.solution: Distance between successive nodes = λ/2. Distance between node and adjacent antinode = λ/4.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: An open pipe of length L has fundamental frequency f. If it is closed at one end, the fundamental frequency becomes:
questions.solution: f(open) = v/2L, f(closed) = v/4L = f(open)/2.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 480 Hz and 484 Hz produce beats. The beat frequency is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A train moving at 30 m/s sounds its whistle (500 Hz) as it approaches a tunnel. What frequency is heard by a stationary observer ahead? (v = 330 m/s)
questions.solution: Source moving towards observer: f' = f x v/(v - vs) = 500 x 330/(330 - 30) = 500 x 330/300 = 550 Hz.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A closed pipe has fundamental frequency 200 Hz. What is the frequency of the next resonance?
questions.solution: Closed pipe has only odd harmonics: f1 = 200 Hz, f3 = 3 x 200 = 600 Hz.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The speed of sound in air at 27°C is 340 m/s. Find the speed at 0°C.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A string of length 0.5 m is vibrating in its second harmonic. The wavelength of the wave is:
questions.solution: For nth harmonic on a string: λn = 2L/n. n = 2: λ = 2 x 0.5/2 = 0.5 m.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Doppler effect, if the source moves away from a stationary observer, the apparent frequency:
questions.solution: When source moves away, waves are stretched, wavelength increases, so frequency decreases. f' = f x v/(v + vs).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A closed organ pipe of length 0.25 m produces its fundamental frequency. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, what is the frequency of the 5th harmonic?
questions.solution: For closed pipe: f1 = v/4L = 340/(4 x 0.25) = 340 Hz. 5th harmonic of a closed pipe = 5 x f1 = 5 x 340 = 1700 Hz. Option (c).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: An observer moves towards a stationary source of sound at 34 m/s. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. If the source frequency is 500 Hz, the apparent frequency is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Two waves of frequencies 512 Hz and 516 Hz produce beats. The beat period is:
questions.solution: f(beat) = |512 - 516| = 4 Hz. T(beat) = 1/4 = 0.25 s. Option (a).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave on a string depends on tension T and linear mass density μ. If the tension is quadrupled and the linear mass density is doubled, the wave speed becomes:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A source of sound of frequency 600 Hz is moving away from a stationary observer at 30 m/s. Speed of sound = 330 m/s. The apparent frequency is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a standing wave on a string fixed at both ends, the distance between successive antinodes is:
questions.solution: Distance between successive antinodes = λ/2. Similarly, distance between successive nodes = λ/2. Distance between a node and adjacent antinode = λ/4. Option (c).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: An open pipe and a closed pipe have the same length L. The ratio of their fundamental frequencies (f(open) : f(closed)) is:
questions.solution: f(open) = v/2L, f(closed) = v/4L. Ratio = (v/2L) : (v/4L) = 2 : 1. Option (b).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The intensity of a wave is proportional to:
questions.solution: I ∝ A^2. I = ½ρvω^2A^2. Doubling amplitude quadruples intensity. Option (b).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A string of length 1 m and mass per unit length 0.005 kg/m is under tension 200 N. The fundamental frequency of vibration is:
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Doppler effect, if both source and observer move away from each other, the apparent frequency:
questions.solution: Both moving away: f' = f(v - vo)/(v + vs). Since the numerator decreases and denominator increases, the apparent frequency decreases. Option (b).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Statement: 'All employees must submit their project reports by Friday to avoid penalty.' Assumptions: I. Employees currently have pending project reports. II. Friday is the deadline for submission. Which is/are implicit?
questions.solution: Both are implicit. The need for a deadline implies reports are pending (I). The statement explicitly mentions Friday as the deadline (II).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.q: Situation: The city has seen a sharp rise in road accidents in the past year. Course of Action: I. Install speed cameras at all major intersections. II. Ban all private vehicles in the city. Which course(s) of action is/are appropriate?
questions.solution: Only I follows. Speed cameras can deter rash driving and reduce accidents. II is impractical — banning all private vehicles would cripple daily life. A balanced traffic management approach is better.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.q: Statement: 'The government should increase spending on public healthcare to improve health outcomes.' Which of the following is the strongest argument in favour?
questions.a: Many countries with higher healthcare spending have better health indicators
opts: Increased spending always leads to better outcomes
Many countries with higher healthcare spending have better health indicators
Private hospitals are too expensive for most people
The current government has a surplus budget
questions.solution: b) is the strongest argument. It provides empirical evidence that higher spending correlates with better health outcomes. a) is too absolute. c) and d) are not directly about the relationship between spending and outcomes.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.q: Passage: 'Studies show that students who participate in extracurricular activities perform better academically. Therefore, schools should mandate participation in at least one extracurricular activity.' Which of the following, if true, weakens the argument?
questions.a: Students with better time management skills tend to join more activities
opts: Extracurricular activities teach teamwork and leadership
Students with better time management skills tend to join more activities
Many schools lack adequate sports facilities
questions.solution: b) weakens the argument by suggesting reverse causality — students who already perform well academically may be more likely to join activities, rather than activities causing better performance.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.q: Which characteristic of a computer is defined by its ability to perform repetitive tasks tirelessly and consistently without loss of concentration or accuracy?
questions.solution: Section 1.2 lists the key characteristics. It defines 'Diligence' specifically as the ability to perform repetitive tasks tirelessly and consistently without loss of concentration or accuracy, unlike humans. 'Speed' refers to the rate of operations per second. 'Accuracy' refers to the precision of execution given correct input. 'Versatility' refers to the ability to perform different tasks by loading different software. Therefore, Diligence is the correct term for the described capability.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Who is regarded as the "Father of the Computer" for designing the Analytical Engine, a general-purpose mechanical computer in the 19th century?
questions.solution: Section 1.3 on Historical Evolution explicitly states: "In the 19th century, Charles Babbage, often regarded as the 'Father of the Computer,' designed the Analytical Engine, a general-purpose mechanical computer...". Alan Turing is known for theoretical computer science and codebreaking. John von Neumann is known for the stored-program architecture. J. Presper Eckert co-invented ENIAC. Only Charles Babbage matches the description in the text.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In touch typing technique, which keys constitute the home row for the left and right hands respectively?
questions.solution: Section 6.3 on Effective Practice Techniques explicitly instructs candidates to "Focus on learning the home row keys (ASDF JKL;)". This identifies the left-hand home keys as A, S, D, F and the right-hand home keys as J, K, L, ;. Option A represents the top row (QWERTY row). Option C represents the bottom row. Option D incorrectly lists H, J, K, L for the right hand, omitting the semicolon key and including H which is not a standard home key for the index finger (J is).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which process state transition occurs when an I/O operation completes?
questions.solution: The lesson states that I/O completion causes a transition from Waiting (or Blocked) to Ready. When a process finishes its I/O request, it becomes eligible for CPU scheduling again, moving to the Ready queue. The other transitions correspond to I/O request (Running→Waiting), scheduler dispatch (Ready→Running), and process exit (Running→Terminated). Therefore, the correct transition for I/O completion is Waiting → Ready.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which scheduling algorithm uses a fixed time quantum to provide fairness and responsiveness for interactive systems?
questions.solution: The lesson describes Round‑Robin (RR) as the algorithm that employs a time quantum, giving each ready process a slice of CPU time. This design ensures fairness and low latency, which are essential for interactive environments. FCFS and SJN do not use a quantum, and priority scheduling may be preemptive or non‑preemptive but does not inherently guarantee a fixed time slice for every process. Hence, Round‑Robin is the correct answer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What does the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) cache to avoid page‑table walks?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, the TLB caches recent translations of logical pages to physical frames, allowing the processor to bypass a full page‑table walk on each memory reference. It does not store process control blocks, disk block addresses, or CPU register contents. This caching of page‑table entries directly speeds up virtual‑to‑physical address translation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which normal form eliminates transitive dependencies among non‑key attributes?
questions.solution: The lesson specifies that Third Normal Form (3NF) removes transitive dependencies, i.e., dependencies where a non‑key attribute depends on another non‑key attribute. 1NF requires atomic values, 2NF removes partial dependencies on a composite key, and BCNF strengthens 3NF for certain multi‑candidate‑key anomalies. Therefore, 3NF is the normal form that directly addresses transitive dependencies.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A candidate types 300 correct characters in a 5‑minute test with 4 errors. The examination uses a penalty factor of 1 WPM per error. Using the formula Net WPM = (Correct Characters ÷ 5) ÷ Time(min) − (Error Count × Penalty Factor), what is the Net WPM?
questions.solution: First compute gross words: 300 correct characters ÷ 5 = 60 words. Divide by test duration: 60 ÷ 5 min = 12 WPM (gross). Apply penalty: 4 errors × 1 WPM/error = 4 WPM. Net WPM = 12 − 4 = 8 WPM. The other options correspond to gross WPM (12), an incorrect addition (16), or the penalty alone (4). Thus the correct Net WPM is 8.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a classic 5-stage pipeline (fetch, decode, execute, memory, write-back), an instruction requires the result of the immediately preceding instruction which is still in the execute stage. Which hazard type occurs and what is the primary hardware technique to resolve it without stalling?
opts: Control hazard resolved by branch prediction
Structural hazard resolved by resource duplication
Data hazard resolved by pipeline flush
questions.solution: The scenario describes a data hazard: the current instruction depends on a result not yet written back. The text states that data hazards occur when an instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction still in the pipeline, and that forwarding (bypassing) and stall insertion mitigate these. Forwarding routes the result directly from the execute stage to the decode/execute stage of the dependent instruction, avoiding a stall. Control hazards relate to branches, structural hazards to resource conflicts, and pipeline flush is used for branch misprediction recovery, not for simple data dependencies.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the typical cache hierarchy parameters given, which level uses a write-through policy and what is its associativity?
questions.solution: The lesson provides a table of Typical Cache Parameters. It lists L1 I-cache as 32 KB, 4-way associativity, 1 cycle latency, and Write-through policy. The L1 D-cache is 8-way and Write-back. L2 and L3 are both Write-back. Therefore, the only cache level using write-through is the L1 Instruction cache with 4-way associativity.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A railway administration requires a cloud service where they manage the operating systems, applications, and runtime environments, but the provider manages the physical hardware, virtualization layer, storage, and networking. Which service model matches this requirement?
questions.solution: The lesson defines the three primary service models as a stack. IaaS provides virtual machines, storage, and networks — the consumer manages the OS, middleware, runtime, and applications. PaaS adds runtime environments, databases, and development tools, meaning the provider manages the OS and runtime. SaaS delivers complete applications. Since the scenario requires OS-level control by the consumer, IaaS is the correct model.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which RAID level suffers from a read-modify-write penalty for small random writes because it must read the old data and parity blocks before writing updated data and recalculated parity?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states in the 'Common Pitfalls' section: 'Assuming RAID 5 provides the same write performance as RAID 10; remember the read-modify-write penalty for small random writes.' RAID 5 uses distributed parity; updating a single block requires reading the old data and old parity, computing new parity, and writing both new data and new parity. RAID 10 (mirrored stripes) writes to multiple mirrors without parity calculation. RAID 0 has no redundancy. RAID 1 mirrors without parity.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: A digital communication system uses a modulation scheme that encodes 6 bits per symbol. If the system switches to a scheme encoding 4 bits per symbol to improve noise immunity, which modulation schemes are being used before and after the switch?
questions.solution: The lesson provides a 'Modulation vs. Bits per Symbol' table. It lists 64-QAM as 6 bits/symbol and 16-QAM as 4 bits/symbol. The question describes a switch from 6 bits/symbol to 4 bits/symbol, which corresponds to moving from 64-QAM to 16-QAM. Higher-order QAM (more bits/symbol) increases spectral efficiency but requires better SNR; falling back to lower-order QAM improves noise immunity. QPSK is 2 bits/symbol and BPSK is 1 bit/symbol.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Coffman's four necessary conditions for a deadlock?
questions.solution: Coffman's four conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. The condition listed as "Preemption" is the opposite of "no preemption"; therefore it is not a required condition for deadlock. If preemption were allowed, the no‑preemption condition would be violated and deadlock could be avoided. The other three options appear directly in the lesson as necessary conditions.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which page‑replacement algorithm suffers from Belady's anomaly, where increasing the number of frames can increase page faults?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly says FIFO evicts the oldest page and suffers from Belady's anomaly, where increasing frames can increase faults. LRU approximates optimal behaviour and does not exhibit this anomaly. The optimal algorithm is theoretical and also immune. Clock is an approximation of LRU and inherits its property of not showing Belady's anomaly.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of DSCP marking in the IP header as described in the QoS section?
questions.a: To identify traffic classes for classification and marking
opts: To reserve bandwidth end‑to‑end for a flow
To identify traffic classes for classification and marking
To guarantee zero latency for voice packets
To replace TCP congestion control mechanisms
questions.solution: The lesson states that classification and marking (DSCP in IP header) identify traffic classes. DSCP itself does not reserve bandwidth, guarantee zero latency, or replace TCP congestion control; it merely tags packets so that downstream QoS mechanisms such as policing, shaping, and queuing can treat them according to policy.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which benchmark provides consensus‑based configuration guides for Windows, Linux, macOS, and network devices?
questions.solution: The lesson identifies CIS Benchmarks as consensus‑based configuration guides for Windows, Linux, macOS, and network devices. DISA STIGs are mandatory for DoD systems, NIST SP 800‑53 maps control families to hardening and patching, and ISO/IEC 27001 is a compliance framework, not a hardening benchmark. Hence, option C is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In ITIL Incident Management, prioritisation of incidents is performed using which matrix?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Incident Management lifecycle includes prioritisation using an Impact × Urgency matrix. This matrix combines the business impact of the incident with the urgency of resolution to assign priority. The other matrices listed are not mentioned for incident prioritisation in the provided material.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which disaster recovery site model combined with synchronous replication achieves a near‑zero Recovery Point Objective (RPO)?
questions.solution: The lesson explains that only a synchronous hot site or continuous replication achieves near‑zero RPO. A hot site maintains fully operational systems ready for immediate failover, and synchronous replication ensures data is written to both primary and secondary sites simultaneously, minimizing data loss. Cold and warm sites involve longer recovery times and asynchronous replication introduces a data loss window, so they cannot provide near‑zero RPO.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Working‑Set Model, what set of pages does the operating system aim to keep resident in memory?
questions.a: Pages referenced in the most recent Δ time units
opts: Pages referenced in the most recent Δ time units
Pages with the highest reference‑bit count
Pages with the lowest access frequency
Pages currently on the active list
questions.solution: The working set W(t, Δ) is defined as the set of pages referenced in the most recent Δ time units. The OS keeps this working set resident; pages outside it become eviction candidates. The other options describe metrics used by other replacement schemes (reference bits, frequency counters, active/inactive lists) but do not define the working set itself.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under snapshot isolation provided by MVCC, which anomaly can still occur unless Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI) is enabled?
questions.solution: Snapshot isolation prevents dirty reads, lost updates, and phantom reads by giving each transaction a consistent snapshot. However, write‑skew — where two concurrent transactions read overlapping data and then write disjoint updates that together violate a constraint — can still happen. The lesson notes that write‑skew persists under snapshot isolation unless SSI is enabled.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What major change does TLS 1.3 introduce compared with TLS 1.2 regarding key exchange?
opts: Adds a new certificate validation step
Replaces symmetric encryption with a new cipher
questions.solution: TLS 1.3 simplifies the handshake by eliminating RSA key exchange and other static‑RSA mechanisms, relying solely on (EC)DHE for forward secrecy. The lesson states that TLS 1.3 removes RSA key exchange and changes the transcript hash, while certificate validation and symmetric encryption remain conceptually similar.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which requirement is essential for achieving the URLLC guarantees (1 ms latency, 99.999 % reliability) in FRMCS?
questions.solution: The lesson emphasizes that FRMCS URLLC guarantees require end‑to‑end network slicing to isolate signalling, voice, and passenger Wi‑Fi on a shared infrastructure. Merely upgrading the radio interface, using dual‑mode radios, or adding GSM‑R interworking does not provide the deterministic latency and reliability; slicing across the entire network path is mandatory.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In a copy-on-write (CoW) file system such as ZFS or Btrfs, how does a snapshot initially consume storage space?
questions.a: It consumes no additional space until divergent writes occur after the snapshot.
opts: It reserves a fixed percentage of the pool capacity for snapshot metadata.
It consumes no additional space until divergent writes occur after the snapshot.
It immediately duplicates all referenced blocks to a separate snapshot area.
It allocates space equal to the current used capacity of the file system.
questions.solution: In a copy-on-write (CoW) file system, a snapshot is created by simply referencing the current root of the block tree. No data blocks are copied at snapshot creation time. The original blocks remain shared between the live file system and the snapshot. Additional space is consumed only when either the live file system or the snapshot modifies a shared block, triggering the allocation of a new block for the modified data. This is a fundamental advantage of CoW snapshots over traditional block-level snapshots, which require reserved space upfront. Therefore, option B correctly describes the initial zero-space consumption characteristic.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the recurrence pattern of key current affairs categories as outlined in Section 1.3?
questions.a: Union Budget appears annually; Railway Board safety circulars may be issued monthly
opts: Union Budget appears quarterly; Railway Board safety circulars appear annually
Union Budget appears annually; Railway Board safety circulars may be issued monthly
Both Union Budget and Railway Board safety circulars appear monthly
Union Budget appears biennially; Railway Board safety circulars appear weekly
questions.solution: Section 1.3 states: "Each category follows a distinct pattern of recurrence: for instance, the Union Budget appears once a year, while the Railway Board's safety circulars may be issued monthly." This makes option B the only accurate representation. The Union Budget is an annual event (presented each February), whereas safety circulars from the Railway Board are higher-frequency documents that can be released monthly, requiring proportionally more revision time.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Kavach system, mentioned in Section 4.2, is primarily associated with which aspect of railway operations?
questions.solution: Section 4.2 is titled "Safety Enhancements and the Kavach System Rollout," directly linking Kavach to safety improvements. The Kavach system is India's indigenous Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system designed to prevent collisions and overspeeding, making it a core safety technology. The other options refer to distinct areas: freight corridor financing (Section 4.1), high-speed rail (Section 4.1), and passenger service digitisation (Section 4.3).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which international body awarded the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project the "Project of the Year" award in 2025, as per Section 6.3?
questions.solution: Section 6.3 explicitly states: "The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project received the International Federation of Consulting Engineers (FIDIC) Project of the Year award in 2025 for its innovative financing model and environmental mitigation measures." FIDIC is the global representative body for consulting engineering firms. The other organisations listed (UIC, World Bank, ADB) are involved in railways or infrastructure financing but were not identified in the lesson as the awarding body for this specific honour.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: As per Section 7.2, which of the following is NOT listed among the most reliable primary sources for current affairs preparation?
questions.solution: Section 7.2 enumerates four specific primary sources: "The Press Information Bureau releases, the Railway Ministry's monthly 'Railway Gazette', the Ministry of External Affairs' 'MEA Weekly', and the Reserve Bank of India's 'Monthly Bulletin'." NITI Aayog's "Strategy Document" series is not mentioned in this list. While NITI Aayog publications may be useful for policy analysis, the lesson identifies only the four named sources as the "most reliable primary sources" for examination-focused current affairs preparation.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a milestone captured in the Railway Board’s Project Monitoring Unit (PMU) dashboard?

questions.q: For a reaction at 298 K, the standard Gibbs free energy change ΔG° is -5.7 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the approximate value of the equilibrium constant K? (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.solution: Use ΔG° = -RT ln K. Convert ΔG° to J: -5700 J mol⁻¹. Then ln K = -ΔG°/(RT) = 5700 / (8.314 × 298) ≈ 5700 / 2478 ≈ 2.30. Thus K = e²·³⁰ ≈ 10. Option C matches. Options A and B correspond to positive ΔG° and ΔG°=0 respectively. Option D would require ΔG° ≈ -11.4 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The rate constant k for a reaction is measured at two temperatures: 300 K and 310 K. A plot of ln k versus 1/T yields a straight line with slope -6000 K. What is the activation energy Ea? (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.solution: From the Arrhenius equation in linear form: ln k = ln A - Ea/(RT). The slope of ln k vs 1/T is -Ea/R. Given slope = -6000 K, so -Ea/R = -6000 → Ea = 6000 × R = 6000 × 8.314 = 49884 J mol⁻¹ ≈ 50 kJ mol⁻¹. Option B is correct. Option A would correspond to slope ≈ -3000 K, C to -9000 K, D to -12000 K.

questions.q: A patient exhibits high plasma cortisol levels but low ACTH levels. Which endocrine feedback mechanism best explains this pattern?
questions.a: D. Primary adrenal hyperfunction suppressing pituitary ACTH
opts: A. Positive feedback loop enhancing cortisol secretion
B. Negative feedback failure at the pituitary level
C. Ectopic ACTH production overriding normal feedback
D. Primary adrenal hyperfunction suppressing pituitary ACTH
questions.solution: High cortisol with low ACTH indicates the adrenal gland is overproducing cortisol independently (primary hyperfunction, e.g., adrenal adenoma). The excess cortisol exerts negative feedback on the pituitary, suppressing ACTH secretion. This matches option D. Option A (positive feedback) would increase both. Option B (pituitary feedback failure) would cause high ACTH. Option C (ectopic ACTH) would cause high ACTH, not low.

questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, light of wavelength 400 nm is incident on a metal surface with a work function of 2.0 eV. What is the stopping potential required to prevent the most energetic photoelectrons from reaching the anode? (Use hc = 1240 eV·nm)
questions.solution: Photon energy E = hc/λ = 1240 eV·nm / 400 nm = 3.1 eV. Maximum kinetic energy K_max = E - φ = 3.1 eV - 2.0 eV = 1.1 eV. Stopping potential V_s = K_max / e = 1.1 V. The linear relationship K_max = hν - φ yields Planck's constant from the slope, and the stopping potential directly measures K_max in electron-volts.

questions.q: For a Daniell cell (Zn|Zn²⁺||Cu²⁺|Cu) at 298 K with E° = 1.10 V, if [Zn²⁺] = 0.1 M and [Cu²⁺] = 1.0 M, what is the cell potential E? (Use 0.05916 V for 2.303RT/F at 298 K)
questions.solution: The Nernst equation at 298 K is E = E° - (0.05916/n) log₁₀ Q. For the Daniell cell, n = 2 and Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] = 0.1/1.0 = 0.1. log₁₀(0.1) = -1. Substituting: E = 1.10 - (0.05916/2) × (-1) = 1.10 + 0.02958 = 1.12958 V ≈ 1.13 V. As the cell discharges, Q increases and E decreases until equilibrium (E = 0).

questions.q: What is the stereochemical outcome when (R)-2-bromobutane undergoes hydrolysis via an SN1 mechanism in aqueous NaOH?
opts: Formation of 1-butene as the major product
questions.solution: The SN1 mechanism proceeds through a planar, sp²-hybridised carbocation intermediate. Because the carbocation is planar, the nucleophile (OH⁻) can attack with equal probability from either face, leading to loss of stereochemistry. This results in a racemic mixture (50% R, 50% S). The text explicitly warns against confusing SN1 racemisation with SN2 inversion and notes that carbocation planarity leads to loss of stereochemistry.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes cyclic photophosphorylation in chloroplasts?
questions.a: It involves only Photosystem I and produces ATP without NADPH evolution
opts: It produces both ATP and NADPH using Photosystems I and II
It involves only Photosystem I and produces ATP without NADPH evolution
It splits water to release O₂ while generating a proton gradient
It operates independently of light energy input
questions.solution: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves only Photosystem I (PSI). Electrons from ferredoxin cycle back to plastoquinone, driving proton pumping across the thylakoid membrane to synthesise ATP via ATP synthase. This process does not involve Photosystem II, does not split water, does not evolve O₂, and does not reduce NADP⁺ to NADPH. The text states that cyclic photophosphorylation produces only ATP, not NADPH, and is essential to meet the Calvin cycle's additional ATP demand.

questions.q: Which substance's renal clearance is considered the gold standard for measuring Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) because it is freely filtered and neither reabsorbed nor secreted by the tubules?
questions.solution: Inulin is a polysaccharide that is freely filtered at the glomerulus and is neither reabsorbed nor secreted by the renal tubules. Therefore, its clearance exactly equals the GFR. Creatinine clearance overestimates GFR due to tubular secretion. Urea is reabsorbed, so its clearance underestimates GFR. PAH is both filtered and secreted, so its clearance approximates renal plasma flow (RPF). The text explicitly states: "inulin clearance = GFR".

questions.q: Which electron configuration of chromium (Cr) follows the (n+l) filling rule and the exception for a half‑filled d subshell?
questions.solution: The Aufbau principle and (n+l) rule predict the order 3d before 4s, but the actual filling for Cr is an exception. A half‑filled d subshell (d⁵) gains extra exchange energy, making it more stable than the expected 3d⁴ 4s². Therefore Cr adopts the configuration [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹, placing one electron in 4s and five in 3d. The other options either follow the regular filling order or represent impossible electron counts for Cr (Z=24).

questions.q: For the exothermic reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) (ΔH = –92 kJ/mol), what is the effect of increasing the temperature on the equilibrium position according to Le Chatelier’s principle?
questions.a: Shifts reverse toward N₂ and H₂
opts: Shifts reverse toward N₂ and H₂
questions.solution: Le Chatelier’s principle states that a system at equilibrium will counteract a disturbance. Raising temperature adds heat; for an exothermic reaction heat is a product. The system therefore shifts in the direction that consumes heat, i.e., the reverse (endothermic) direction, producing more reactants N₂ and H₂. The equilibrium constant K decreases with temperature for exothermic reactions, but the principle predicts the directional shift without needing K’s value. Pressure changes affect the position but do not alter the temperature‑driven shift described here.

questions.q: In the standard Streptococcus pyogenes CRISPR‑Cas9 system, what DNA sequence must be present adjacent to the target site for Cas9 to cleave?
questions.a: A 5′‑NGG‑3′ PAM sequence downstream of the target
opts: A 5′‑NGG‑3′ PAM sequence downstream of the target
A 5′‑NAG‑3′ PAM sequence upstream of the target
questions.solution: Cas9 from Streptococcus pyogenes recognizes a protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) of the form 5′‑NGG‑3′ (where N is any nucleotide) located immediately downstream (3′) of the target DNA sequence complementary to the guide RNA. Without this PAM, the Cas9‑gRNA complex cannot bind and cleave the target. Variants such as NAG can function with reduced efficiency, but the canonical requirement is NGG. The other options describe sequences that are not the PAM for the standard Cas9.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the valency (number of antigen‑binding sites) of IgM and IgG antibodies?
questions.a: IgM is a pentamer with 10 binding sites; IgG is a monomer with 2 binding sites
opts: IgM is a monomer with 2 binding sites; IgG is a pentamer with 10 binding sites
IgM is a pentamer with 10 binding sites; IgG is a monomer with 2 binding sites
Both IgM and IgG are monomers with 2 binding sites each
Both are pentamers with 10 binding sites each
questions.solution: IgM is secreted as a pentamer composed of five monomeric units, each monomer having two antigen‑binding sites, giving a total of 10 binding sites per IgM molecule. IgG exists as a single monomer with two identical antigen‑binding sites. This structural difference underlies IgM’s high avidity (due to multiple simultaneous bindings) versus IgG’s lower valency but higher affinity per site. The other options reverse or misstate the quaternary structures.

questions.q: The average ecological efficiency (Lindeman efficiency) for energy transfer between successive trophic levels is approximately:
questions.solution: Ecological efficiency, also called Lindeman efficiency, is the percentage of energy transferred from one trophic level to the next. The lesson states that this efficiency typically ranges from 5% to 20%, averaging ~10%, often referred to as the “10% rule”. While actual values vary with ecosystem type and trophic level, the accepted average for exam purposes is 10%. The other options represent the lower bound, a value below the typical range, and the upper bound, respectively.

questions.q: In an n-type extrinsic semiconductor at room temperature, how does the Fermi level position compare to the intrinsic Fermi level, and which charge carrier dominates conduction?
questions.a: Fermi level shifts toward the conduction band; electrons are majority carriers
opts: Fermi level shifts toward the valence band; holes are majority carriers
Fermi level shifts toward the conduction band; electrons are majority carriers
Fermi level remains at mid-gap; electron and hole concentrations are equal
Fermi level shifts toward the conduction band; holes are majority carriers
questions.solution: Doping with donor impurities introduces energy levels just below the conduction band. At thermal equilibrium, these donors ionize, releasing electrons into the conduction band and raising the electron concentration far above the hole concentration. The Fermi level (EF) moves upward from the intrinsic position (near mid-gap) toward the conduction band edge to reflect the increased electron population. Consequently, electrons become the majority carriers. Option B correctly describes both the Fermi level shift and the majority carrier type. Option A describes p-type behavior, option C describes intrinsic material, and option D contradicts itself by pairing an n-type Fermi shift with hole majority.

questions.q: According to the proton-pumping stoichiometry given for the mitochondrial electron transport chain, how many protons are translocated from the matrix to the intermembrane space per pair of electrons passing through Complex I, Complex III, and Complex IV combined?
questions.solution: The lesson states the H⁺/2e⁻ ratios: Complex I pumps 4 H⁺ per 2 e⁻, Complex III pumps 4 H⁺ per 2 e⁻, and Complex IV pumps 2 H⁺ per 2 e⁻. Summing these contributions gives 4 + 4 + 2 = 10 protons translocated per electron pair traversing the three proton-pumping complexes. Complex II does not pump protons. Therefore, the total is 10, corresponding to option B.

questions.q: What is the key atmospheric function of peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN) in the context of photochemical smog and nitrogen oxide chemistry?
questions.a: It acts as a temporary reservoir for NOx, transporting it downwind before thermal decomposition releases it again
opts: It is a primary pollutant emitted directly from combustion sources
It acts as a temporary reservoir for NOx, transporting it downwind before thermal decomposition releases it again
It catalytically destroys ozone in the lower troposphere
It rapidly hydrolyzes to form nitric acid, directly causing acid rain
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly warns against "overlooking that PAN acts as a temporary NOx reservoir, transporting NOx downwind before thermal decomposition releases it again." PAN forms from the reaction of peroxyacetyl radicals with NO₂. It is thermally unstable; at lower temperatures it sequesters NO₂, allowing long-range transport. Upon warming, it decomposes, releasing NO₂ back into the atmosphere where it can participate in ozone formation far from the original emission source. It is not a primary emission (ruling out A), does not catalytically destroy ozone (ruling out C), and its hydrolysis is not the primary acid rain pathway compared to direct NO₂ + OH → HNO₃ (ruling out D).

questions.q: Which pairing of a G-protein α-subunit family with its canonical second messenger pathway is correct?

questions.q: According to the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) guidelines (2021) for Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) response, which of the following is mandated as a state-level coordination action?
questions.a: Coordination with the Central Water Commission (CWC) for downstream reservoir operation adjustments.
opts: Community-level siren activation within 5 minutes of sensor threshold breach.
Coordination with the Central Water Commission (CWC) for downstream reservoir operation adjustments.
Real-time water-level sensor deployment in glacial lakes.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the NDMA guidelines (2021) mandate a three-tier response for GLOF. Option A describes a community-level action, and Option B describes a district-level action. Financing demand-side measures like crop-water budgeting and micro-irrigation.
Mandating the use of only injection wells for aquifer recharge.
Promoting groundwater extraction for industrial use in targeted gram panchayats.
