questions.q: Why is the repo rate not equal to the banks' marginal cost of funds (MCLR/EBLR)?
questions.a: MCLR/EBLR includes a spread for operating cost and risk premium
opts: Repo rate includes a risk premium
MCLR/EBLR includes a spread for operating cost and risk premium
MCLR is fixed by the RBI
questions.solution: The lesson highlights a common trap: equating the repo rate with the marginal cost of funds. It clarifies that banks' MCLR/EBLR incorporates a spread over the policy rate to cover operating costs and risk premium. Hence, the repo rate alone does not reflect the full marginal cost of funds for banks.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In fiscal accounting, how are Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs) treated?
questions.a: Part of market borrowings and counted toward the fiscal deficit
opts: Off‑budget and excluded from fiscal deficit
Part of market borrowings and counted toward the fiscal deficit
questions.solution: The lesson states that Sovereign Green Bonds are accounted as part of market borrowings and count toward the fiscal deficit. They are not off‑budget, nor are they merely capital receipts or excluded from debt statistics. This treatment means the issuance of SGrBs increases the government's fiscal deficit just like conventional dated securities.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What were the horizontal distribution weights recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission (2020‑25) for inter‑state sharing of Union tax proceeds?
questions.a: 45% population (2011 Census), 15% area, 15% forest and ecology, 12.5% income distance, 10% demographic performance, 2.5% tax effort
opts: 45% population (2011 Census), 15% area, 15% forest and ecology, 12.5% income distance, 10% demographic performance, 2.5% tax effort
40% population, 20% area, 10% forest, 15% income distance, 10% demographic performance, 5% tax effort
50% population, 10% area, 10% forest, 10% income distance, 15% demographic performance, 5% tax effort
30% population, 20% area, 20% forest, 15% income distance, 10% demographic performance, 5% tax effort
questions.solution: The Fifteenth Finance Commission retained the 41% vertical devolution share and prescribed a new horizontal formula. According to the lesson, the weights are: 45% for population (2011 Census), 15% for area, 15% for forest and ecology, 12.5% for income distance, 10% for demographic performance and 2.5% for tax effort. Option A matches this exact breakdown, while the other options present different percentage allocations not mentioned in the text.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under Article 279A, what is the voting weight of the Union and the States in the GST Council and what majority is required for decisions?
questions.a: Union one‑third, States two‑thirds; three‑fourths majority
opts: Union one‑third, States two‑thirds; simple majority
Union one‑third, States two‑thirds; three‑fourths majority
Union one‑half, States one‑half; three‑fourths majority
Union two‑thirds, States one‑third; simple majority
questions.solution: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A. The lesson states that the Union holds one‑third of the voting weight, the States together hold two‑thirds, and decisions require a three‑fourths majority. This structure gives States a veto on rate changes while preserving the Centre’s ability to push reforms. Option B correctly reflects both the voting weights and the required majority.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the applicability of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act?
questions.a: It binds only the Central government; States have their own separate FRBM legislation.
opts: It sets a uniform fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP for both the Centre and all States.
It binds only the Central government; States have their own separate FRBM legislation.
It mandates a debt‑to‑GDP target of 40% for both the Centre and States by 2024‑25.
It requires the Centre to maintain a 3% fiscal deficit while States must target 4%.
questions.solution: The FRBM Act, 2003 (amended in 2012, 2018, 2021) applies only to the Central government, prescribing a debt‑to‑GDP target of 40% by 2024‑25 and a fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP. States are governed by their own FRBM laws enacted by respective legislatures. The lesson explicitly warns against assuming a single deficit target for both tiers. Therefore, option B is the accurate description.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the prescribed timeline for a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the IBC and what is the average actual resolution time as of March 2024?
questions.a: 180 days extendable by 90 days; average resolution 420 days
opts: 180 days with no extensions; average resolution 180 days
180 days extendable by 90 days; average resolution 420 days
120 days for all cases; average resolution 200 days
questions.solution: The IBC mandates that a resolution plan be approved by 66% of financial creditors within 180 days, extendable by a further 90 days. The lesson notes that extensions are routine and the average resolution time for admitted cases (including extensions) stands at 420 days as of March 2024. Option B correctly captures both the statutory timeline with extension provision and the observed average duration.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: How does the National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (NARCL) / India Debt Resolution Company Ltd (IDRCL) structure its acquisition of stressed assets?
questions.a: 15% cash and 85% security receipts backed by government guarantee for assets above ₹500 crore
opts: 100% cash payment for assets above ₹500 crore
15% cash and 85% security receipts backed by government guarantee for assets above ₹500 crore
50% cash and 50% security receipts for assets above ₹1,000 crore
85% cash and 15% security receipts for assets above ₹500 crore
questions.solution: The ‘Bad Bank’ comprising NARCL and IDRCL was set up in 2021 to acquire stressed assets above ₹500 crore. The lesson specifies the consideration as 15% cash and 85% security receipts backed by a government guarantee. This structure aims to limit upfront cash outlay while providing a sovereign-backed instrument for the balance. Option B matches this description exactly.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the vertical devolution share of the divisible pool recommended by the 15th Finance Commission for the period 2020‑25?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 15th Finance Commission retained the 41 per cent vertical devolution recommended by the 14th Finance Commission. This share applies to the divisible pool for the award period 2020‑25. Therefore the correct answer is 41 per cent.

questions.q: As of March 2024, what approximate share of India’s total outstanding liabilities is accounted for by internal debt?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, internal debt accounted for roughly 90 per cent of total outstanding liabilities as of March 2024. The remaining portion is external debt. Hence the correct figure is 90 per cent.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the current holding limit for a retail CBDC (CBDC‑R) wallet as prescribed by the RBI?
questions.solution: The lesson lists regulatory safeguards for CBDC‑R, including a holding limit of ₹1 lakh per user (subject to revision) and a non‑interest‑bearing design to avoid bank disintermediation. Hence the current limit is ₹1 lakh.

questions.q: Under the FRBM Act (as amended in 2018), what is the maximum deviation from the fiscal deficit target permitted by the escape clause?
questions.solution: The FRBM Act includes an escape clause that allows a temporary deviation of up to 0.5 % of GDP from the prescribed fiscal deficit anchor of 3 % of GDP, and only for specified contingencies. The lesson clarifies that the legal limit is 0.5 % of GDP, not 1 %.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Since April 2022, which rate has served as the floor of the RBI’s interest rate corridor?
questions.solution: Before April 2022 the reverse repo rate acted as the corridor floor. From April 2022 onward, the RBI designated the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate as the new floor of the interest rate corridor, as noted in the lesson’s monetary policy transmission section.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following accurately describes the function of the National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL)?
questions.a: It purchases select stressed assets from banks at a discount, subject to due diligence.
opts: It acquires all non‑performing assets from banks automatically.
It purchases select stressed assets from banks at a discount, subject to due diligence.
It provides recapitalisation funds to public sector banks.
It adjudicates insolvency cases under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
questions.solution: NARCL is set up to buy selected stressed assets from banks at a discounted price after conducting due diligence. It does not automatically acquire all bad loans, nor does it provide recapitalisation or adjudicate insolvency cases. The lesson explicitly states this selective, discount‑based purchase mechanism.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the composition and jurisdiction of the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) as of 2024?
questions.a: Consists of a judicial member (former High Court judge) and a technical member (IRS officer); benches functional in five cities; Supreme Court retains appellate jurisdiction under Article 136
opts: Consists of a judicial member (former High Court judge) and a technical member (IRS officer); benches functional in five cities; Supreme Court retains appellate jurisdiction under Article 136
Consists of two judicial members (former Supreme Court judges); benches functional in all state capitals; High Courts retain appellate jurisdiction under Article 226
Consists of a judicial member (former District Judge) and a technical member (IAS officer); benches functional in three cities; no further appeal lies to the Supreme Court
Consists of a single member (former High Court judge); benches functional in New Delhi only; Supreme Court retains appellate jurisdiction under Article 131
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states: 'The Tribunal consists of a judicial member (a former High Court judge) and a technical member (an officer of the Indian Revenue Service). As of 2024, the Tribunal's benches are functional in New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and Hyderabad... The Supreme Court retains appellate jurisdiction over GSTAT decisions under Article 136.' Option A matches all these details. Option B has wrong composition, bench coverage, and appellate route. Option C has wrong member qualifications and denies Supreme Court appeal. Option D has wrong composition (single member), bench coverage, and cites wrong Article (131 is original jurisdiction).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is a key design difference between the wholesale CBDC (e₹-W) and retail CBDC (e₹-R) regarding interest payment and access?
questions.a: e₹-W is account-based, accessible to regulated financial institutions, and bears interest at the repo rate; e₹-R is token-based, held in digital wallets, and does not carry interest
opts: e₹-W is account-based, accessible to regulated financial institutions, and bears interest at the repo rate; e₹-R is token-based, held in digital wallets, and does not carry interest
e₹-W is token-based, accessible to the public, and bears interest at the reverse repo rate; e₹-R is account-based, held in bank accounts, and does not carry interest
Both e₹-W and e₹-R are account-based and bear interest at the repo rate, but e₹-W is for institutions while e₹-R is for individuals
Both e₹-W and e₹-R are token-based and non-interest-bearing, but e₹-W settles on a permissioned ledger while e₹-R uses a public blockchain
questions.solution: The lesson clearly differentiates: 'e₹-W is account‑based, accessible only to regulated financial institutions, and bears interest at the prevailing repo rate... e₹-R is token‑based, held in digital wallets provided by participating banks, and does not carry interest'. Option A captures this exact distinction. Option B reverses the account/token basis and access. Option C incorrectly makes both account-based and interest-bearing. Option D incorrectly makes both token-based and non-interest-bearing, and mentions public blockchain which is not in the text.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What specific measure has the RBI implemented during the retail CBDC pilot to monitor disintermediation effects on bank deposits?
questions.a: Capped individual wallet holdings at ₹1 lakh and limited merchant acceptance to QR-code based transactions
opts: Capped individual wallet holdings at ₹1 lakh and limited merchant acceptance to QR-code based transactions
Mandated that all e₹-R wallets be linked to a savings account with a minimum balance of ₹10,000
Required commercial banks to pay interest on e₹-R holdings at the savings deposit rate
Restricted e₹-R usage to person-to-person transfers only, prohibiting person-to-merchant payments
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'The RBI has therefore capped individual wallet holdings at ₹1 lakh during the pilot and limited merchant acceptance to QR‑code based transactions to monitor disintermediation effects.' This matches option A exactly. Option B introduces a savings account linkage and minimum balance not mentioned. Option C contradicts the text which says e₹-R 'does not carry interest'. Option D is incorrect because the text explicitly mentions the retail pilot targets both 'person‑to‑person (P2P) and person‑to‑merchant (P2M) payments'.

questions.q: How does a GST rate cut affect the absolute tax devolution to states under the current Finance Commission formula, and why?
questions.a: Reduces the absolute transfer because the divisible pool shrinks while the states' percentage share (41%) remains unchanged
opts: Reduces the absolute transfer because the divisible pool shrinks while the states' percentage share (41%) remains unchanged
Increases the absolute transfer because the rate cut stimulates consumption and expands the tax base
Has no effect on absolute transfers because the Finance Commission adjusts the percentage share to compensate
Reduces the absolute transfer only for the Centre, while states' share remains protected by the compensation cess
questions.solution: The lesson explains the feedback loop: 'a rate cut reduces the divisible pool, which in turn lowers the absolute transfer to states, even though the percentage share remains unchanged.' The Finance Commission's vertical devolution is 41% of the divisible pool (net proceeds of CGST and IGST after deducting Centre's share of compensation cess). A rate cut reduces the pool size, so 41% of a smaller pool yields a lower absolute amount. Option A captures this mechanism. Option B assumes a dynamic revenue effect not stated in the text. Option C suggests automatic percentage adjustment which contradicts 'percentage share remains unchanged'. Option D incorrectly isolates the impact to the Centre and mentions compensation cess protection which ended in June 2022.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which regions did the Indus Valley Civilization have long-distance trade links with, as evidenced by seals found in Sumerian contexts?
questions.a: Mesopotamia, the Persian Gulf and the Arabian Peninsula
opts: Mesopotamia, the Persian Gulf and the Arabian Peninsula
questions.solution: The lesson text explicitly states that long-distance trade links extended to Mesopotamia, the Persian Gulf and the Arabian Peninsula, attested by seals bearing the unicorn motif found in Sumerian contexts. Options A, C, and D mention regions not supported by the provided text.

questions.q: Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism and propagation of Dhamma was prompted by which event?
questions.solution: The lesson text clearly mentions: "Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism after the brutal Kalinga war (c. 261 BCE) prompted the propagation of Dhamma." The other events listed occurred at different times and are not linked to Ashoka's conversion in the provided material.

questions.q: Which event galvanised a more assertive nationalist response during the Moderate Phase of the Indian National Congress?
questions.a: Partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Curzon
opts: Partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Curzon
Partition of Bengal in 1911 by Lord Hardinge
Partition of Punjab in 1905 by Lord Curzon
Partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Minto
questions.solution: The text states: "the partition of Bengal in 1905 by Lord Curzon, justified on administrative grounds but widely perceived as a divide-and-rule tactic, galvanised a more assertive nationalist response." This matches option A exactly. The other options contain incorrect years, regions, or Viceroys.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly identifies the primary literary sources of the Sangam period?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the primary sources of the Sangam period are the anthologies of Tamil poetry — Ettuthokai (Eight Anthologies) and Pattuppattu (Ten Idylls) — together with the grammatical treatise Tolkāppiyam. The other options refer to later Sanskrit epics, legal texts, and Puranic literature, which are not the Sangam sources. Therefore, option A is the only choice that matches the textual evidence.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the Sangam poems, which sacrificial rite was performed by the king (ventar)?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that the king (ventar) performed velvi (sacrificial rites) as part of the political organisation described in the poems. The terms yajna, homa, and ashvamedha are generic or later Vedic sacrificial forms not specified for the Sangam king in the provided text. Hence, option A is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea lists which three ports as major exporters of pepper, pearls, ivory and textiles to the Roman Empire?
opts: Palghat Gap, Kaveri delta, Vaigai basin
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (mid‑1st century CE) and Ptolemy’s Geography list Muziris, Tyndis and Korkai as major ports exporting pepper, pearls, ivory and textiles. The other groups are archaeological sites, capital cities, or geographical features, not the ports named in the Periplus. Therefore, option A is the correct answer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which Alvar concept of surrender to the divine parallels the Sufi notion of fana (annihilation of the self)?
questions.solution: The lesson notes that the Alvars’ prapatti (surrender) mirrors the Sufi concept of fana, both emphasising a direct, personal relationship with the divine that bypasses priestly mediation. Bhakti is the broader devotional path, moksha denotes liberation, and dharma refers to duty; none of these specifically correspond to the Sufi idea of self‑annihilation. Thus, option A is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was repealed after public outcry in which year?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that the Vernacular Press Act (1878) was repealed in 1882 after public outcry, demonstrating the press’s capacity to mobilise opinion. The other years are not mentioned in the text. Consequently, option A is the only verifiable answer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which legislative act was a direct response to the Santhal Hul (1855‑56)?
questions.solution: The Santhal Hul erupted in 1855‑56 against zamindari exactions and loss of forest access. The colonial state responded by creating the Santhal Parganas district through the Santhal Parganas Act of 1855, which aimed to isolate the rebellion’s leadership and restore revenue control. The Deccan Agriculturists’ Relief Act (1879) followed the Deccan Riots, the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act (1908) followed the Munda Ulgulan, and the Bengal Land Reforms Act (1950) followed the Tebhaga Movement. Therefore, the correct legislative response to the Santhal Hul is the Santhal Parganas Act 1855.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Who hoisted the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan during the Quit India Movement after the arrest of senior leaders?
questions.solution: During the Quit India Movement (1942), after the arrest of top Congress leaders, Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, becoming a symbol of defiance. Sarojini Naidu and Kasturba Gandhi were active in the Non‑Cooperation Movement, Usha Mehta ran the clandestine Congress Radio, and Matangini Hazra led a procession in Tamluk where she died under police fire. The text explicitly identifies Aruna Asaf Ali as the person who hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which constitutional document introduced universal adult franchise in India?
questions.solution: The Government of India Act 1919 granted only limited voting rights to women, not universal adult franchise. The 1935 Act proposed a federal scheme that never came into force because princely states did not accede. Universal adult franchise was finally established by the Constitution of India adopted in 1950, which extended the vote to all adult citizens regardless of gender, property, or education. Hence, the 1950 Constitution is the correct answer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the nature of production in the Mughal karkhana system?
questions.solution: The Mughal karkhana system organized artisans in state‑run workshops for cannon casting, textile weaving, and other crafts. However, production remained craft‑based and carried out in batches; it did not achieve standardized interchangeable parts, assembly lines, or full mechanization. The text explicitly warns against the misconception that the karkhanas produced standardized interchangeable parts, clarifying that they remained craft‑based batch production.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Chola Kudimaramath system for irrigation maintenance relied on which institutional arrangement?
opts: Private contractors appointed by the king
questions.solution: The Chola empire’s Kudimaramath system obliged village assemblies (ur) to maintain irrigation tanks and channels. The Uttaramerur inscriptions (c. 920 CE) detail elected tank committees with accountability clauses, showing that maintenance was managed by village‑level elected bodies, not a centralized bureaucracy, private contractors, or merchant guilds alone. The text also notes the misconception of treating Kudimaramath as a purely state‑run bureaucracy, confirming the role of elected committees.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately describes the political consequence of the 1945 Red Fort trials of INA officers?
questions.a: The trials triggered mass demonstrations and a joint defence by Congress, Muslim League, and Communist Party, eroding British Indian Army morale.
opts: The trials led to the immediate disbandment of the British Indian Army.
The trials were boycotted by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.
The trials triggered mass demonstrations and a joint defence by Congress, Muslim League, and Communist Party, eroding British Indian Army morale.
The trials resulted in the execution of all three accused officers, sparking the 1946 Royal Indian Navy mutiny.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the November–December 1945 Red Fort trials of Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sahgal, and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon triggered mass demonstrations. Congress, the Muslim League, and the Communist Party jointly defended them, turning the trials into a referendum on British legitimacy. Public sympathy eroded British Indian Army morale, contributing to the February 1946 Royal Indian Navy mutiny. Option A is incorrect as the army was not immediately disbanded. Option B is false because major parties jointly defended the accused. Option D is false; the officers were not executed.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding the Permanent Settlement of 1793, which statement is correct?
questions.a: It fixed land revenue demand permanently and recognised zamindars as proprietors of the land.
opts: It introduced the Ryotwari system in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
It fixed land revenue demand permanently and recognised zamindars as proprietors of the land.
It was implemented in the Madras Presidency under Lord Cornwallis.
It abolished intermediate tenures such as jotedars to protect peasant rights.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states the Permanent Settlement (1793) fixed the land revenue demand in perpetuity and conferred proprietary rights on zamindars in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. It did not introduce ryotwari (that was the Madras and Bombay systems), nor was it applied in Madras. Intermediate tenures such as jotedars proliferated under the settlement rather than being abolished. This matches the examiner's trap explanation provided in the text.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the nature of the 'guarantee system' used to finance railway construction in colonial India?
questions.a: A contingent liability where the Government of India guaranteed a fixed rate of return on capital, converting shortfalls into a sterling debt obligation.
opts: A direct annual subsidy paid by the British Parliament to railway companies.
A contingent liability where the Government of India guaranteed a fixed rate of return on capital, converting shortfalls into a sterling debt obligation.
A profit-sharing agreement where the British government received 50% of railway surplus revenue.
A land-grant system where railway companies were given free land in lieu of interest payments.
questions.solution: The lesson identifies a common confusion: 'Treating the railway guarantee system as a direct British government subsidy rather than a contingent liability that became a sterling debt obligation.' The guarantee system meant the Government of India guaranteed a minimum return (typically 5%) to private investors; if earnings fell short, the deficit was covered by Indian revenues and recorded as a sterling debt, not a direct parliamentary subsidy. Options A, C, and D describe mechanisms not mentioned in the lesson.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: When and where was the first Indian Civil Service (ICS) examination held simultaneously in India?
questions.a: 1922 in Allahabad following partial adoption of the Islington Commission recommendations.
opts: 1912 in Allahabad as recommended by the Islington Commission.
1922 in Allahabad following partial adoption of the Islington Commission recommendations.
1935 in Delhi under the Government of India Act.
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'The 1912 Islington Commission proposed simultaneous exams in India and Britain, partially adopted in 1922 with the first Indian exam at Allahabad.' It also lists as a confusion point: 'Believing the ICS examinations were held simultaneously in India and Britain from the outset; the first Indian‑held exam occurred only in 1922.' Option B incorrectly cites 1912 (the year of the commission report, not implementation). Option D refers to the 1935 Act which expanded provincial autonomy but did not initiate the Indian exam.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following accurately reflects the Constituent Assembly's decision on minority representation in 1949?
questions.a: Separate electorates for Muslims were abolished and replaced with joint electorates with reserved seats, while reservations for Scheduled Castes and Tribes continued.
opts: Separate electorates were abolished for all minorities including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Separate electorates for Muslims were abolished and replaced with joint electorates with reserved seats, while reservations for Scheduled Castes and Tribes continued.
The Assembly adopted permanent separate electorates for Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, and Anglo-Indians.
Minority safeguards were entirely rejected in favour of a uniform adult franchise with no reservations.
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'The Assembly adopted temporary separate electorates for Muslims, abolished in 1949 for joint electorates with reserved seats.' It also lists as a confusion point: 'Overstating the immediate abolition of separate electorates for all minorities in 1949; only Muslim separate electorates were removed, while reservations for Scheduled Castes and Tribes continued.' Option A is incorrect because SC/ST reservations continued. Option C is wrong as separate electorates were not made permanent. Option D is false as minority safeguards (reservations) were retained.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The "martial races" theory that directed recruitment toward communities such as Sikhs, Gurkhas, Dogras, Rajputs and certain Punjabi Muslims was formalized in which period and by whom?
opts: Immediately after the 1857 revolt by the Crown
By the Partition Council chaired by Field Marshal Auchinleck
questions.solution: The lesson states that the martial races theory was formalized in the 1880s under Lord Roberts. It was not a direct outcome of the 1857 revolt, nor was it introduced by Kitchener's 1903 reforms or the Partition Council. Therefore, option B is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between Wood's Despatch (1854) and the Universities Act (1857)?
questions.a: The Universities Act 1857 created the universities based on Wood's Despatch recommendations
opts: Wood's Despatch created the Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras
The Universities Act 1857 created the universities based on Wood's Despatch recommendations
Wood's Despatch abolished the existing universities
The Universities Act 1857 recommended the establishment of universities
questions.solution: Wood's Despatch of 1854 recommended a hierarchical education system including universities, while the Universities Act of 1857 actually established the Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras as examining bodies. Thus, the Act implemented the Despatch's recommendations, making option B correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which princely states did not sign Instruments of Accession before 15 August 1947?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that Hyderabad and Junagadh acceded later, implying they had not signed Instruments of Accession before 15 August 1947. The other pairs listed had acceded earlier. Hence, option A is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The first Indian census to introduce systematic caste enumeration was conducted in which year?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, the 1881 census began systematic caste enumeration. Earlier censuses did not have this systematic approach, and later censuses built upon it. Therefore, option B is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What was the jurisdiction of the Federal Court of India established under the Government of India Act 1935?
opts: Original jurisdiction over centre-province disputes only
Both original and appellate jurisdiction over all matters
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Federal Court (operational 1937) served as the highest appellate body for constitutional disputes between the Centre and provinces and for appeals from High Courts, with advisory functions. It did not have original jurisdiction over fundamental rights. Thus, option B correctly describes its jurisdiction.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the Cabinet Mission Plan, what was the original composition of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.a: 389 members: 292 elected by provincial assemblies, 93 nominated by princely states
opts: 389 members: 292 elected by provincial assemblies, 93 nominated by princely states
299 members: all elected by provincial assemblies
389 members: all nominated by the British Crown
292 members: 93 elected, 299 nominated by princely states
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Constituent Assembly was constituted in November 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan and originally comprised 389 members. Of these, 292 were elected by the provincial legislative assemblies and 93 were nominated by the princely states. After partition in 1947, the membership reduced to 299. Option A matches this exact description. Option B describes the post-partition strength but incorrectly states all were elected. Option C is factually wrong as members were not nominated by the British Crown. Option D reverses the numbers and categories.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which set of keywords describes the nature of the Indian Republic as stated in the Preamble?
questions.solution: Section 2.2 of the lesson explicitly lists the keywords as "Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic" when discussing the Preamble's interpretation. This is the standard description of the Indian Republic's nature in the Preamble. Option B substitutes "Federal" for "Socialist" and "Secular". Option C includes "Federal" and "Parliamentary" which are features of the Constitution but not the Preamble's defining keywords. Option D includes "Federal" instead of "Secular" and omits "Republic".
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under which Articles are the Directive Principles of State Policy enumerated in the Constitution?
questions.solution: Section 3.2 of the lesson clearly states: "Directive Principles of State Policy: Articles 36 to 51". Articles 12 to 35 (Option B) cover Fundamental Rights as per Section 3.1. Article 51A (Option C) deals with Fundamental Duties as per Section 3.3. Articles 1 to 11 (Option D) cover the Union and its territory, citizenship, etc., not Directive Principles.

questions.q: As per the current administrative framework, the Railway Board comprises the Chairman and how many other functional members?
questions.a: Four members responsible for traffic, engineering, mechanical, and electrical matters, plus a Financial Commissioner
opts: Four members responsible for traffic, engineering, mechanical, and electrical matters, plus a Financial Commissioner
Three members responsible for traffic, engineering, and mechanical matters only
Five members including a Member Finance and a Member Staff
Six members with separate members for signalling and telecommunications
questions.solution: Section 6.2 states: "The Board comprises the Chairman and four other members responsible for traffic, engineering, mechanical, and electrical matters, together with a Financial Commissioner." This matches Option A exactly. Option B mentions only three members and omits electrical and Financial Commissioner. Option C mentions five members with incorrect designations (Member Finance, Member Staff). Option D mentions six members with incorrect portfolios (signalling, telecommunications).

questions.q: Since 2017, through which mechanism is the Railway Board's financial scrutiny primarily conducted in Parliament?
questions.a: The Railway Budget merged with the General Budget
opts: The Railway Budget merged with the General Budget
A separate Railway Budget presented by the Minister of Railways
The Report of the Committee on Railways on CAG findings only
Questions and debates during the Zero Hour only
questions.solution: Section 6.3 explicitly states: "The Board's decisions are subject to parliamentary scrutiny through the Railway Budget (merged with the General Budget since 2017), questions, debates and the reports of the Committee on Railways." Option A correctly identifies the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget since 2017 as the primary mechanism. Option B describes the pre-2017 practice. Option C and D mention only partial mechanisms (Committee reports, Zero Hour) but not the primary budgetary scrutiny mechanism.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment required ratification by the legislatures of not less than one‑half of the states?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) affected local self‑government, a State subject, and therefore mandated ratification by at least half the State legislatures under Article 368(2). The 24th and 42nd Amendments were passed using the special majority only, while the 39th Amendment dealt with election disputes and did not involve federal‑structure changes. Hence the 73rd Amendment is the correct example of an amendment requiring State ratification.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the Indian Constitution, the residuary legislative power is vested in which authority?
opts: Both Parliament and State Legislatures concurrently
questions.solution: Article 248 and the Seventh Schedule assign all subjects not enumerated in the Union, State or Concurrent Lists to the Union. The lesson explicitly warns against the misconception that residuary power belongs to the States, confirming that it vests exclusively in Parliament. Therefore, the correct answer is Parliament exclusively.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: During a proclamation of National Emergency, which fundamental rights remain enforceable and cannot be suspended?
questions.solution: The lesson notes that a common error is to assume a National Emergency suspends all fundamental rights. It clarifies that Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and 21 (protection of life and personal liberty) continue to be enforceable even during an Emergency. Other rights, particularly those under Article 19, may be suspended. Thus, Articles 20 and 21 are the rights that remain operative.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the current mechanism for the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts in India?
questions.solution: The lesson explains that the NJAC was struck down by the Supreme Court and the collegium system remains the operative mechanism for judicial appointments. The collegium, comprising the Chief Justice of India and senior judges, recommends appointments, which the President then formalises. Therefore, the collegium system is the present practice.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which statement accurately describes the legal status of the Railway Board after the 2020 reorganisation?
questions.a: It is an executive body deriving its powers from executive delegation
opts: It is a statutory corporation created under the Indian Railways Act, 1989
It is an executive body deriving its powers from executive delegation
It is an independent regulatory authority reporting directly to Parliament
It is a subsidiary of the Ministry of Finance
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that the Railway Board is not a statutory corporation but an executive body; its powers stem from executive delegation under the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, not from a separate enactment. The 2020 reforms introduced a corporate‑style governance framework but did not alter its fundamental character as a departmental undertaking of the Union. Hence, the correct description is that it is an executive body deriving powers from executive delegation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which exception to the anti‑defection disqualification was removed by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003?
questions.a: Split exception (one‑third of a legislature party)
opts: Split exception (one‑third of a legislature party)
Merger exception (two‑thirds majority of the legislature party)
questions.solution: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 tightened the Tenth Schedule by deleting the "split" exception that earlier allowed one‑third of a legislature party to defect without disqualification. The "merger" exception survives but now requires a two‑thirds majority of the legislature party to merge with another party. Therefore, the split exception is the one that was removed.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under Article 123, when does an ordinance promulgated by the President cease to operate if not approved by Parliament?
questions.a: Six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament
opts: Six weeks from the date of promulgation
Six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament
questions.solution: Article 123 provides that an ordinance has the same force as an Act of Parliament but must be laid before both Houses when they reassemble. It ceases to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament unless approved earlier; the President may also withdraw it at any time. Hence the six‑week period is counted from the reassembly, not from promulgation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: How often is the Finance Commission’s vertical devolution share revised, and by what mechanism can it be altered?
questions.a: It is revised every five years and can be altered by Presidential order
opts: It is fixed permanently by the Constitution
It is revised every five years and can be altered by Presidential order
It is revised every ten years by the Finance Commission itself
It is determined by the GST Council
questions.solution: The Finance Commission is constituted every five years and its recommendations, including the vertical share of taxes, are implemented by a Presidential order. The vertical share is not fixed; it is revised with each Commission (i.e., every five years) and the President may alter the distribution through the order accepting the Commission’s report.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the 2023 Supreme Court judgment in Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India, who constitute the committee for appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners?
questions.a: A committee comprising the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition, and Chief Justice of India
opts: The President alone on the advice of the Council of Ministers
The Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
A committee comprising the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition, and Chief Justice of India
questions.solution: The 2023 judgment directed that appointments to the Election Commission be made by a high‑powered committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party), and the Chief Justice of India. This replaced the earlier practice of appointment solely on the advice of the Council of Ministers, thereby enhancing institutional independence.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: To which forum can an appeal be filed against an order of the Railway Claims Tribunal?
questions.a: To the High Court under Article 226
opts: Directly to the Supreme Court under Article 136
To the High Court under Article 226
No appeal is provided; the Tribunal’s order is final
questions.solution: The Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 provides that appeals against the Tribunal’s orders lie to the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution. The Tribunal’s decisions are not final; they are subject to judicial review by the High Court, and further appeal to the Supreme Court is possible only through the normal appellate route.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which constitutional provision was abrogated in 2019 through a Presidential order under Article 370(3) without requiring ratification by the concerned state legislature?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 2019 abrogation of Article 370 was effected by a Presidential order under Article 370(3) followed by the Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019. It explicitly notes that the Centre invoked the "constituent power" of Parliament to alter a provision that originally required the concurrence of the state's constituent assembly, a body that had ceased to exist. Articles 371A, 371 and 356 are unrelated to this specific abrogation process. Therefore, the correct answer is Article 370.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under Article 110 of the Constitution, a Money Bill may contain provisions for all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.a: Regulation of interstate trade and commerce
opts: Imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of taxes
Borrowing of money or giving of guarantees by the Government of India
Regulation of interstate trade and commerce
Custody of the Consolidated Fund or Contingency Fund
questions.solution: Article 110 exhaustively lists the matters a Money Bill may deal with: taxes, borrowing/guarantees, custody of the Consolidated Fund or Contingency Fund, appropriation from the Consolidated Fund, declaring expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund, and receipt of money. Regulation of interstate trade and commerce is not mentioned in this list; it falls under the Union List but is not a Money Bill subject. Hence the exception is regulation of interstate trade and commerce.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Supreme Court's power of judicial review over the President's pardon under Article 72 is limited to which ground(s)?
opts: Advice of the Council of Ministers only
Grant of pardon to a foreign national only
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that the President's pardon power under Article 72 is "subject to limited judicial review for arbitrariness or mala fides." It does not restrict review to procedural errors, the advice of the Council of Ministers, or the nationality of the beneficiary. Therefore, the only ground on which the Court may examine the pardon is arbitrariness or mala fides.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Inter‑State Council from the Zonal Councils?
questions.a: Inter‑State Council is a constitutional body chaired by the Prime Minister; Zonal Councils are statutory bodies chaired by the Home Minister
opts: Both are constitutional bodies chaired by the Prime Minister
Inter‑State Council is a constitutional body chaired by the Prime Minister; Zonal Councils are statutory bodies chaired by the Home Minister
Zonal Councils are constitutional bodies chaired by the Home Minister; Inter‑State Council is a statutory body chaired by the Prime Minister
Both are statutory bodies chaired by the Home Minister
questions.solution: The lesson warns against "equating the Inter‑State Council (constitutional, chaired by PM) with Zonal Councils (statutory, chaired by Home Minister)." This directly indicates that the Inter‑State Council derives from the Constitution (Article 263) and is chaired by the Prime Minister, whereas Zonal Councils are created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (a statute) and are chaired by the Union Home Minister. The other options misrepresent the constitutional/statutory nature or the chairpersons.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad), which statement about its power over Money Bills is accurate?
questions.a: It has no power over Money Bills
opts: It can delay Money Bills for up to three months
It has no power over Money Bills
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Council's legislative role "mirrors that of the Rajya Sabha at the state level: it can delay non‑Money Bills for up to three months (first passage) and one month (second passage), but cannot amend or reject Money Bills." Consequently, the Council possesses zero authority over Money Bills — it cannot reject, amend, or delay them. The correct description is that it has no power over Money Bills.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the application of the doctrine of pith and substance, what is the first step a court takes to determine the validity of a law that incidentally encroaches on another list?
questions.a: Identify the dominant purpose of the statute by reviewing its preamble, title, scheme, and operative provisions.
opts: Examine the legislative motive behind the enactment.
Identify the dominant purpose of the statute by reviewing its preamble, title, scheme, and operative provisions.
Apply a strict literal interpretation of the entries in the Seventh Schedule.
Presume the law is invalid unless the enacting legislature proves otherwise.
questions.solution: The doctrine of pith and substance requires the court to first ascertain the true nature and character of the legislation. The lesson outlines the steps: identify the dominant purpose by examining the preamble, title, scheme, and operative provisions; then locate the matching entry in the Seventh Schedule. Legislative motive is irrelevant, and there is no presumption of invalidity. Hence the correct first step is described in option B.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding the constitutional position of the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, which of the following is correct?
questions.a: The Lieutenant Governor’s discretion is limited to the three reserved subjects of public order, police, and land; on other matters he acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
opts: The Lieutenant Governor exercises discretion on all matters of the Union Territory, similar to a Governor of a State.
The Lieutenant Governor’s discretion is limited to the three reserved subjects of public order, police, and land; on other matters he acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
The Lieutenant Governor has no discretionary powers and must always follow the Council of Ministers’ advice.
The Lieutenant Governor’s discretion extends to all subjects in the State List for Delhi.
questions.solution: The lesson specifies that in Delhi the Lieutenant Governor’s discretion is confined to three reserved subjects — public order, police, and land. On all other matters the LG acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers. This distinguishes Delhi from other Union Territories where the Administrator acts on the President’s directions. Options A, C, and D incorrectly broaden or eliminate the LG’s discretion. Hence option B is correct.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is a mandatory provision under Part IX of the Constitution for States with a population exceeding 20 lakhs?
questions.a: Constitution of a three‑tier Panchayat structure at village, intermediate, and district levels.
opts: Establishment of a two‑tier Panchayat system.
Reservation of not less than one‑half of the total seats for women in Panchayats.
Constitution of a three‑tier Panchayat structure at village, intermediate, and district levels.
Direct election of the Chairperson of the District Panchayat by the people.
questions.solution: Article 243B mandates a three‑tier Panchayat structure (village, intermediate, district) in every State with a population over 20 lakhs; smaller States may have two tiers. The reservation for women is not less than one‑third, not one‑half. The Chairperson of the District Panchayat is elected indirectly by the elected members, not directly by the people. Therefore option C correctly states the mandatory provision.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the doctrine of harmonious construction from the doctrine of pith and substance?
questions.a: Harmonious construction is a rule of interpretation applied before invoking Article 254, whereas pith and substance is a test of legislative competence.
opts: Harmonious construction determines legislative competence, while pith and substance is a rule of interpretation.
Harmonious construction is a rule of interpretation applied before invoking Article 254, whereas pith and substance is a test of legislative competence.
Both doctrines are used to resolve repugnancy under Article 254(1).
Pith and substance is applied only when harmonious construction fails, and it decides which law prevails.
questions.solution: The lesson states that harmonious construction is a rule of interpretation used to reconcile overlapping Union and State statutes before resorting to the repugnancy test under Article 254. In contrast, the doctrine of pith and substance is a test of legislative competence that determines the true character of a law to decide whether it falls within the enacting legislature's assigned entries. Therefore, option B accurately captures this distinction: harmonious construction is interpretive and precedes Article 254, while pith and substance assesses competence.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under Article 254(2), a State law on a Concurrent List subject that has been reserved for the President's assent and received it can prevail over a Union law, but this protection is not absolute. Which statement accurately reflects the limitation?
questions.a: Parliament can still enact a law that overrides the State law, either expressly or by necessary implication.
opts: The State law becomes immune from any future Union legislation on the same subject.
Parliament can still enact a law that overrides the State law, either expressly or by necessary implication.
The President's assent converts the State law into a Union law, removing the repugnancy.
The State law prevails only until the next general election.
questions.solution: Article 254(2) allows a reserved State law to operate in that State despite repugnancy, but the lesson explicitly notes that Parliament retains the power to override such a State law by enacting a subsequent Union law, either expressly or by necessary implication. This means the protection is conditional and not permanent. Options A, C, and D misstate the constitutional position: immunity is not granted, the law does not become a Union law, and there is no electoral time limit.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the nature of the Supreme Court's opinion rendered under Article 143 of the Constitution?
questions.a: It is advisory in character and not binding on the President or any authority.
opts: It is binding on all courts and the executive, equivalent to a judgment under Article 131.
It is advisory in character and not binding on the President or any authority.
It has the force of law until Parliament enacts a contrary statute.
It can be reviewed only by a larger bench of the Supreme Court.
questions.solution: Article 143 empowers the President to refer a question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its opinion. The lesson clarifies that this advisory jurisdiction is distinct from the Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 and that the opinion given is advisory, not binding on the President or any other authority. Hence, option B correctly describes the nature of the opinion, while the other options incorrectly attribute binding force or review mechanisms that do not apply.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the S.R. Bommai judgment, the Governor's discretionary powers under Article 163 are confined to specific situations. Which of the following is NOT one of those situations?
questions.a: Reservation of a State Bill for the President's consideration.
opts: Appointment of a Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority in the Legislative Assembly.
Dismissal of a Ministry that has lost majority support but refuses to resign.
Reservation of a State Bill for the President's consideration.
Dissolution of the Legislative Assembly on the advice of a Ministry that has lost majority.
questions.solution: The lesson identifies three situations from the Bommai case where the Governor may exercise discretion: (1) appointing a Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority, (2) dismissing a Ministry that has lost majority support but refuses to resign, and (3) dissolving the Assembly on the advice of a Ministry that has lost majority. Reservation of a State Bill for the President's consideration is mentioned as a discretionary act of the Governor, but it is not listed among the three Bommai situations. Therefore, option C is the correct choice.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General's audit jurisdiction does not automatically extend to all local bodies. Under which condition does the CAG audit a local body?
questions.a: Only if the local body is substantially financed by the Union or State government.
opts: Only if the local body is a municipal corporation.
Only if the local body is substantially financed by the Union or State government.
Only if the State Legislature passes a specific resolution.
Only if the local body requests an audit.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the CAG does not audit the accounts of local bodies unless they are substantially financed by the Union or State governments, referencing Articles 243J and 243Z. This condition is the sole basis for extending CAG audit to local bodies. Options A, C, and D introduce criteria not mentioned in the constitutional scheme or the lesson, such as municipal corporation status, legislative resolution, or a request from the body itself.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which domestic cricket trophy features a match between the reigning Ranji Trophy champions and a Rest‑of‑India XI?
questions.solution: According to the classification section, the Irani Cup matches the reigning Ranji champions against a Rest‑of‑India XI, serving as a high‑profile showcase for emerging talent. The Duleep Trophy pits zonal sides, while the Vijay Hazare and Syed Mushtaq Ali trophies are limited‑overs competitions.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which sports award was renamed to the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna in 2021?
questions.solution: The lesson notes that the government renamed the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna to the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna in 2021, shortly after Neeraj Chopra's Olympic gold. The Arjuna, Dronacharya, and Dhyan Chand awards retain their original names.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Who won India's first individual Olympic gold medal, and in which event and year did it occur?
questions.solution: The lesson states that Abhinav Bindra's gold in the 10‑metre air rifle at the 2008 Beijing Olympics marked India's first individual Olympic gold. Vijender Singh, Sushil Kumar, and Neeraj Chopra won medals later or in different events.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory member of the Final Selection Committee for National Sports Awards, as per the provided text?
questions.a: President of the Indian Olympic Association
opts: President of the Indian Olympic Association
questions.solution: The lesson text explicitly lists the mandatory members of the Final Selection Committee. It states that the committee is chaired by the Union Sports Minister and includes the Secretary (Sports), the Director General of SAI, two eminent sportspersons (one male, one female) nominated by the IOA, and a representative of the Ministry of Home Affairs for the Dhyan Chand award. While the IOA nominates sportspersons, its President is not listed as a mandatory member of the committee itself. Therefore, the President of the Indian Olympic Association is not a mandatory member.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the 2023-2027 media rights cycle for the Indian Premier League (IPL), what percentage of the revenue is distributed equally among the ten franchises?
questions.solution: The lesson text details the revenue architecture of the IPL, specifically mentioning the distribution of the 2023-2027 media rights cycle. It states that the ₹48,390 crore media rights are split as follows: 50 % to the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), 45 % distributed equally among the ten franchises, and 5 % retained for league operations. Therefore, 45 % of the revenue is distributed equally among the ten franchises.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the mandated target for female representation in coaching and administrative roles within National Sports Federations (NSFs) by 2025, and how is compliance monitored?
questions.a: 30 % representation, monitored through the National Sports Governance Observer (NSGO) dashboard
opts: 25 % representation, monitored by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
30 % representation, monitored through the National Sports Governance Observer (NSGO) dashboard
40 % representation, monitored by a whistle-blower portal
questions.solution: The lesson text on Governance Structures of National Sports Federations states that the Code of Conduct requires NSFs to adopt a gender-equity policy ensuring at least 30 % female representation in coaching and administrative roles by 2025. It further specifies that compliance with this policy is monitored through the National Sports Governance Observer (NSGO) dashboard. Options A, C, and D contain incorrect percentages or monitoring mechanisms.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: How did India's overall medal conversion rate at the Summer Olympics change from London 2012 to Tokyo 2020 (held 2021), and which sports primarily drove this change?
questions.a: Improved from 0.032 to 0.058, driven by shooting, wrestling, boxing, and athletics.
opts: Decreased from 0.058 to 0.032, driven by archery and badminton.
Improved from 0.032 to 0.058, driven by shooting, wrestling, boxing, and athletics.
Remained constant at approximately 0.045, with no specific sport identified as a primary driver.
Improved from 0.032 to 0.058, driven by table tennis and weightlifting.
questions.solution: The section on Medal Conversion Analytics states that India’s overall conversion rate at the Olympics improved from 0.032 (6 medals / 187 athletes) in London 2012 to 0.058 (7 medals / 121 athletes) in Tokyo 2020 (held 2021). The text explicitly attributes this rise to targeted investment in shooting, wrestling, boxing, and athletics under TOPS, where conversion rates exceed 0.15. Therefore, option B accurately reflects both the change in conversion rate and the driving sports.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following transparency measures was explicitly stated to have been strengthened 'after controversies in 2018' regarding the National Sports Awards selection process?
questions.a: Publication of the Final Selection Committee's minutes on the ministry website within 30 days of the announcement.
opts: Introduction of a Public Feedback Module for objections.
Publication of the Final Selection Committee's minutes on the ministry website within 30 days of the announcement.
Mandatory anti-doping clearance certificates from NADA for every nominee.
Institutionalization of character and antecedent verification from state police.
questions.solution: The lesson text discusses several transparency measures. It specifically states: 'The committee’s minutes are published on the ministry website within 30 days of the announcement, a transparency measure strengthened after controversies in 2018.' While other measures like the Public Feedback Module (2021 revision) and NADA clearance (since 2020) were also introduced or mandated after 2018, the publication of minutes is the one explicitly linked to being 'strengthened after controversies in 2018'. Character and antecedent verification was institutionalized after a 2016 incident.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: In the Indian sports dispute resolution architecture, which body serves as the appellate forum for decisions of a National Sports Federation's internal Dispute Resolution Committee (DRC)?
opts: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
questions.solution: The National Sports Development Code requires each recognised NSF to constitute a Dispute Resolution Committee (DRC). Decisions of the DRC are appealable to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Ethics Commission, an independent body. Only after exhausting this internal appeal can a party approach the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). The Sports Authority of India (SAI) and the Ministry do not serve as the first appellate forum for DRC decisions. Therefore, the correct appellate body is the IOA Ethics Commission.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under which Indian legislation are foreign arbitral awards of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) enforced in domestic courts?
questions.solution: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended) governs the enforcement of foreign arbitral awards in India. CAS awards are treated as foreign arbitral awards under the New York Convention, and the Act provides the statutory framework for their recognition and enforcement by Indian courts. The Indian Contract Act, 1872 deals with contractual obligations, while the National Sports Development Code and SAI Act are policy and administrative instruments, not enforcement statutes. Hence, the applicable legislation is the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: The revised National Sports Development Code mandates a minimum threshold of female representation in coaching, technical, and administrative positions within NSFs. Which mechanism monitors compliance with this gender‑equity policy?
questions.solution: The revised National Sports Development Code introduced a binding gender‑equity policy with a minimum female representation threshold. Compliance is tracked through the National Sports Governance Observer (NSGO) dashboard, which publishes periodic compliance reports. Federations falling short receive show‑cause notices. The SAI annual audit, IOA Ethics Commission, and Ministry’s internal review are not the designated monitoring tools for this specific policy. Thus, the NSGO dashboard is the correct monitoring mechanism.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the Emerging Sports Framework (ESF), which organisation is designated as the nodal agency for talent identification, coaching certification, and international exposure for emerging sports?
opts: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
questions.solution: The Emerging Sports Framework (ESF) designates the Sports Authority of India (SAI) as the nodal agency responsible for talent identification, coaching certification, and international exposure for emerging sports such as sport climbing, skateboarding, breaking, esports, and surfing. The IOA, Ministry, and National Institute of Sports have other roles but are not named as the nodal agency under the ESF. Therefore, SAI is the correct answer.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the prescribed three‑tier qualification pathway for athletes in emerging sports to secure berths in multi‑sport events under the ESF?
questions.a: National Championships → Continental Qualifiers → World Ranking/Olympic Qualifying Series
opts: National Championships → World Ranking/Olympic Qualifying Series → Continental Qualifiers
Continental Qualifiers → National Championships → World Ranking/Olympic Qualifying Series
National Championships → Continental Qualifiers → World Ranking/Olympic Qualifying Series
World Ranking/Olympic Qualifying Series → National Championships → Continental Qualifiers
questions.solution: Under the ESF, qualification for multi‑sport events follows a three‑tier pathway: (1) National Championships serve as the primary selection trial; (2) Continental Qualifiers (e.g., Asian Championships or Asian Games qualifiers) organised by the respective Asian Continental Federation; (3) World Ranking or Olympic Qualifying Series where athletes must achieve a minimum ranking or accumulate qualifying points at IF‑sanctioned events. This sequence is explicitly stated in the lesson. Options A, B, and D reorder the stages incorrectly. Hence, the correct order is National Championships → Continental Qualifiers → World Ranking/Olympic Qualifying Series.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: What is the mandated composition of a national classification panel conducted by the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI)?
questions.a: A certified classifier, a medical doctor, and a technical official.
opts: A certified classifier, a medical doctor, and a technical official.
Officials nominated solely by the concerned National Sports Federation.
A two-member panel comprising a classifier and a team coach.
Representatives from SAI, the Ministry, and the IPC.
questions.solution: The lesson states: “In India, the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) conducts national classification panels with a certified classifier, a medical doctor, and a technical official.” This three-member composition is mandatory. Option B reflects the examiner’s trap of confusing the panel with NSF-only officials. Option C incorrectly reduces the panel to two members and substitutes a coach for the medical doctor. Option D lists administrative bodies not mentioned as panel members.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the three verticals of the Sports Science and Sports Medicine Centre (SSSMC) established in 2020?
questions.solution: The text specifies: “The SSSMC established 2020 under SAI… Three verticals: physiology, biomechanics, nutrition.” Option A matches this exactly. Option B replaces physiology and biomechanics with psychology and physiotherapy. Option C substitutes nutrition with psychology. Option D lists entirely different verticals not mentioned in the lesson.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Regarding officiating technologies adopted in India, which statement is factually correct?
questions.a: Hawk-Eye uses a calibrated camera array for ball tracking with a small margin of error.
opts: Hawk-Eye uses a calibrated camera array for ball tracking with a small margin of error.
VAR in the ISL reviews all fouls and offside decisions during a match.
DRS components (Hawk-Eye, UltraEdge, Hot Spot) are optional in BCCI bilateral series.
Goal-Line Technology sends an encrypted signal to the referee’s watch within 10 seconds.
questions.solution: The lesson states: “Hawk-Eye uses a calibrated camera array for ball tracking with a small margin of error.” Option A is verbatim. Option B falls into the examiner’s trap – VAR is limited to four match-changing situations, not all fouls. Option C contradicts the text that DRS is mandatory in BCCI bilateral series and the IPL. Option D is incorrect because GLT sends the signal within a second, not 10 seconds.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the Athlete Welfare Framework (AWF) notified in 2021, what constitutes the three-tier support architecture?
opts: Central government, state government, and SAI officials.
TOPS athletes, Khelo India athletes, and para-athletes.
Medical officers, psychologists, and nutritionists at each camp.
questions.solution: The text explicitly states: “The AWF, notified in 2021, establishes a three-tier support architecture with national, state, and camp-level officers.” Option A matches this definition. Option B misidentifies the tiers as governmental bodies. Option C confuses athlete categories with administrative tiers. Option D describes professional roles, not the structural tiers mandated by the AWF.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: According to the 2022 judgment in All India Football Federation v. Union of India, what key principle was reinforced regarding the National Sports Development Code?
questions.a: The Ministry must follow principles of natural justice before imposing sanctions under the NSDC.
opts: The NSDC provisions are non-justiciable policy guidelines.
The Ministry must follow principles of natural justice before imposing sanctions under the NSDC.
The age limit of 70 years for office-bearers is unconstitutional.
The NSDC does not apply to the Board of Control for Cricket in India.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 2022 judgment in All India Football Federation v. Union of India "reinforced that the Code's provisions are justiciable and that the Ministry must follow principles of natural justice before imposing sanctions." Option B directly reflects this. Option A is incorrect because the provisions are justiciable. Option C is not mentioned in the judgment summary. Option D is incorrect because the 2018 Supreme Court judgment in BCCI v. State of Tamil Nadu extended NSDC principles to the BCCI.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.q: Under the Companies Act, 2013 and the 2021 CSR Rules amendment, which of the following sports-related expenditures qualifies as eligible CSR spending, provided it is not part of the company's normal business operations?
questions.a: Donation of sports equipment to a rural school for athletics training.
opts: Construction of a new stadium for a professional league franchise.
Donation of sports equipment to a rural school for athletics training.
Sponsorship of a corporate employee sports tournament.
Funding the operational expenses of a company-owned professional sports team.
questions.solution: The lesson's "traps" section explicitly states: "Confusing CSR eligibility for 'sports equipment donation' with 'building a stadium' – only the former qualifies if not part of core business." While the main text mentions "sports infrastructure, equipment, coaching, and athlete welfare" as qualifying, the trap clarifies the specific examination rule that equipment donation qualifies whereas stadium construction does not.
