Permanent Indus Commission → Court of Arbitration → Neutral Expert
questions.solution: The Indus Waters Treaty provides a three‑tier ladder: the Permanent Indus Commission (PIC) meets annually; if unresolved, the matter goes to a Neutral Expert; and finally to a Court of Arbitration. The lesson notes disputes over Kishanganga and Ratle followed this order.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which statement accurately describes the role of Khanij Bidesh India Limited (KABIL)?
questions.a: It is an overseas acquisition vehicle for critical mineral assets
opts: It conducts domestic exploration of critical minerals
It is an overseas acquisition vehicle for critical mineral assets
It processes critical minerals within India
It regulates the export of critical minerals
questions.solution: KABIL (Khanij Bidesh India Limited) was formed as a joint venture of three PSUs to acquire critical mineral assets abroad. The lesson clarifies that KABIL is exclusively an overseas acquisition vehicle, not a domestic explorer or processor.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is the primary objective of the Amrit Sarovar Mission launched in 2022?
questions.a: To rejuvenate 75,000 existing water bodies of minimum one acre
opts: To designate new Ramsar sites across India
To create new wetlands of at least one acre each
To rejuvenate 75,000 existing water bodies of minimum one acre
To establish blue‑carbon credit markets for mangroves
questions.solution: The Amrit Sarovar Mission aims to rejuvenate 75,000 existing water bodies (minimum one acre each) by converging MGNREGS labour, Finance Commission grants and CSR funds. It does not create new wetlands nor confer Ramsar status, as stated in the lesson.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: As of March 2024, how many automated water‑level sensors were transmitting real‑time data to the IMD Flood Forecasting Centre for GLOF early warning?
questions.solution: The lesson states that as of March 2024, 31 sensors transmit real‑time data to the Indian Meteorological Department’s Flood Forecasting Centre, providing a median warning lead of 45 minutes. The 47 figure refers to the number of highest‑risk lakes identified, not the sensors installed. The 1 200 and 9 000 figures relate to potentially dangerous lakes and total glacial lakes respectively.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is the minimum solar reflectance recommended for cool‑roof coatings in the NIUA Urban Heat Island Mitigation Toolkit (2021)?
questions.solution: The toolkit recommends cool‑roof coatings with solar reflectance ≥ 0.70, demonstrated to lower roof‑top temperatures by 8‑10 °C in pilot wards of Ahmedabad. The other values are lower than the specified threshold.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What budget was allocated for the Deep‑Earth Mission in the 2024‑25 budget?
questions.solution: The lesson states: "The 2024‑25 budget allocated ₹2 500 crore for the ‘Deep‑Earth Mission’, aiming to drill 150 km of cumulative core across five priority belts by 2028." The other amounts correspond to GLOF structural works (₹1 200 crore) and shoreline protection (₹1 100 crore).
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: According to the 2022 Shoreline Change Assessment report, what length of coastline was classified as high‑risk?
questions.solution: The 2022 SCA report identified 1 200 km of “high‑risk” shoreline where the End Point Rate exceeds 1 m yr⁻¹ and population density exceeds 500 persons km⁻². The 300 km figure is the target for stabilisation by 2027, 7 516 km is the total coastline length, and 45% is the proportion experiencing net erosion.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The 2022 revision of the National Water Policy introduced a 'water security index' for river basins. Which of the following correctly describes its composition and the consequence of a basin scoring below the national threshold?
questions.a: It combines per-capita availability, groundwater stress, and flood-risk metrics; basins below the threshold trigger a mandatory basin re-balancing plan within two years.
opts: It combines per-capita availability, groundwater stress, and flood-risk metrics; basins below the threshold trigger a mandatory basin re-balancing plan within two years.
It combines only per-capita availability and groundwater stress; basins below the threshold trigger a voluntary re-balancing plan within one year.
It is calculated annually by the Central Water Commission using only flood-risk metrics; the Ganga basin scored 0.52 in 2023.
It combines water quality, per-capita availability, and industrial demand; basins below the threshold face immediate central takeover of water allocation.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 2022 NWP revision introduced a water security index combining three metrics: per-capita availability, groundwater stress, and flood-risk metrics. Basins scoring below the national threshold trigger a mandatory 'basin re-balancing plan' within two years. The Ganga basin received such a directive in 2023 after its index fell to 0.42. Option A matches this description exactly. Option B incorrectly omits flood-risk metrics and changes the timeline and mandatory nature. Option C misstates the calculating body, metrics, and Ganga's score. Option D lists incorrect metrics and an unmentioned consequence.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Regarding groundwater quality standards in India, which statement accurately distinguishes the permissible limit for fluoride from the WHO guideline for arsenic?
questions.a: The permissible limit for fluoride is 1.5 mg/L, while the WHO guideline for arsenic is 10 µg/L.
opts: The permissible limit for fluoride is 1.5 mg/L, while the WHO guideline for arsenic is 10 µg/L.
The permissible limit for fluoride is 10 µg/L, while the WHO guideline for arsenic is 1.5 mg/L.
Both fluoride and arsenic share a common permissible limit of 1.5 mg/L under Indian standards.
The permissible limit for fluoride is 1.5 µg/L, while the WHO guideline for arsenic is 10 mg/L.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that fluoride exceeds the permissible limit of 1.5 mg L⁻¹ in affected districts. It also highlights a common error: confusing this fluoride limit (1.5 mg/L) with the WHO guideline for arsenic (10 µg/L). Option A correctly states both values with their proper units (mg/L for fluoride, µg/L for arsenic). Option B reverses the values. Option C incorrectly claims a common limit. Option D uses incorrect units for both (µg/L for fluoride, mg/L for arsenic), misrepresenting the orders of magnitude.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is the current status of 'sponge city' implementation in India under the AMRUT scheme?
questions.a: Sponge city pilots are voluntary demonstrations under AMRUT and are not nationally mandated standards.
opts: Sponge city pilots are voluntary demonstrations under AMRUT and are not nationally mandated standards.
Sponge city standards are nationally mandated under the National Water Policy 2022 for all urban local bodies.
Sponge city implementation is compulsory for all cities with population above one million under AMRUT 2.0.
The sponge city concept is a mandatory component of the Smart Cities Mission for all selected cities.
questions.solution: The lesson's 'common errors' section explicitly states: 'Treating sponge‑city pilots as nationally mandated standards; they remain voluntary demonstrations under AMRUT.' Option A reflects this accurately. Option B incorrectly attributes a national mandate to the NWP 2022. Option C invents a compulsory requirement under AMRUT 2.0 with a population threshold not mentioned in the text. Option D incorrectly links it to the Smart Cities Mission as mandatory. The text only mentions sponge city concepts in the context of urban flood resilience and clarifies their voluntary, pilot status under AMRUT.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Under what conditions can the Critical Mineral Reserve Agency (CMRA) release reserves, and what authority is required for such release?
questions.a: Release is triggered when the Import Dependence Index exceeds 80% for two consecutive quarters and requires a formal Cabinet-level notification.
opts: Release is triggered when the Import Dependence Index exceeds 80% for two consecutive quarters and requires a formal Cabinet-level notification.
Release occurs automatically when the Import Dependence Index exceeds 80% for one quarter without needing Cabinet approval.
Release protocols are triggered by the Critical Mineral Dashboard when recycling rates fall below 10% for any critical mineral.
Release is decided solely by the Ministry of Mines when global prices exceed a predefined threshold.
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'Reserve release protocols are triggered when the Import Dependence Index for any critical mineral exceeds 80% for two consecutive quarters.' The common errors section adds: 'Believing the Critical Mineral Reserve Agency can release reserves without a Cabinet‑level decision; release requires a formal notification.' Option A combines both conditions correctly. Option B reduces the trigger to one quarter and removes the Cabinet requirement. Option C invents a recycling-rate trigger linked to the Dashboard. Option D assigns unilateral authority to the Ministry of Mines and adds a price trigger not mentioned in the text.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately describes a key limitation of William Morris Davis's geographical cycle of erosion as discussed in the historical development of geomorphic thought?
questions.a: It assumed stable tectonic conditions and was criticised for limited applicability to tectonically active regions.
opts: It overemphasised the role of catastrophic events like megafloods in landscape evolution.
It assumed stable tectonic conditions and was criticised for limited applicability to tectonically active regions.
It rejected the principle of uniformitarianism in favour of a purely quantitative, statistical approach.
It failed to identify distinct stages of landscape development such as youthful, mature, and old stages.
questions.solution: The lesson text explicitly states that Davis's model 'described a predictable sequence of youthful, mature and old stages of landscape development driven by fluvial erosion under stable tectonic conditions' and was 'later criticised for its deterministic nature and limited applicability to tectonically active regions'. Option A describes catastrophism (Cuvier), not Davis. Option C is incorrect because Davis worked within the uniformitarian tradition; quantitative geomorphology (Horton, Leopold) emerged later. Option D is false because identifying those stages was the core contribution of the Davisian cycle.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: According to the principle of process-form linkage in modern geomorphology, which landform-process pair is correctly matched?
opts: Chemical weathering at grain scale produces continental-scale mountain ranges.
questions.solution: The lesson text states: 'The principle of process-form linkage asserts that specific processes generate characteristic forms; for example, fluvial incision creates V-shaped valleys, while glacial abrasion produces U-shaped troughs.' Option A reverses the correct pairing. Option B also reverses the pairing. Option D misrepresents scale dependence; the text notes processes at grain scale (chemical weathering) are distinct from large-scale landforms, and scale dependence recognises that processes operate differently across scales.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which terrestrial biome is characterised by cool wet winters and hot dry summers, selecting for sclerophyllous shrubs with thick, leathery leaves that resist desiccation?
questions.solution: The lesson text explicitly describes Mediterranean ecosystems as those 'found around the Mediterranean Sea, central Chile, the Cape region of South Africa, southwestern Australia and California' that 'experience cool wet winters and hot dry summers, selecting for sclerophyllous shrubs with thick, leathery leaves that resist desiccation.' Tropical rainforests have no pronounced dry season and high precipitation. Savannas have a distinct dry season but are tropical and fire-adapted grasslands. Boreal forests have short growing seasons and podzolised soils.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The δ¹⁸O composition of precipitation recorded in ice cores is used as a temperature proxy, while foraminiferal δ¹⁸O in marine sediments records a combined signal. Which statement accurately reflects this distinction?
questions.a: A 1 ‰ shift in ice‑core δ¹⁸O corresponds to roughly a 1.5 °C temperature change in polar regions, while marine foraminiferal δ¹⁸O reflects both deep‑water temperature and global ice volume.
opts: Ice‑core δ¹⁸O varies only with local temperature, whereas marine foraminiferal δ¹⁸O varies only with global ice volume.
A 1 ‰ shift in ice‑core δ¹⁸O corresponds to roughly a 1.5 °C temperature change in polar regions, while marine foraminiferal δ¹⁸O reflects both deep‑water temperature and global ice volume.
Both ice‑core and marine δ¹⁸O are direct, unambiguous thermometers for past surface temperature.
Marine foraminiferal δ¹⁸O is a pure temperature proxy because the ice‑volume effect is negligible in deep‑sea records.
questions.solution: The lesson notes that a 1 ‰ shift in ice‑core δ¹⁸O corresponds to about 1.5 °C in polar regions, establishing it as a temperature proxy. In contrast, marine foraminiferal δ¹⁸O records a combination of global ice volume and deep‑water temperature. Option B captures this distinction. Option A incorrectly assigns exclusive controls, option C overstates the directness of both proxies, and option D wrongly claims the ice‑volume effect is negligible in marine records.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The average limestone dissolution rate in tropical karst settings can exceed which of the following values?
questions.solution: The lesson states that temperate dissolution rates average 0.02–0.05 mm yr⁻¹, whereas tropical rates can exceed 0.2 mm yr⁻¹ because high temperature, abundant rainfall and dense vegetation raise soil CO₂ partial pressures 10–30 times atmospheric values. This makes 0.2 mm yr⁻¹ the threshold that tropical rates can surpass, while the lower values represent temperate conditions.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In monsoonal regions, the primary control on speleothem δ¹⁸O variation is:
questions.solution: The lesson highlights a common trap: misidentifying temperature as the main driver of speleothem δ¹⁸O shifts. In monsoonal settings the dominant influence is the rainfall amount effect, which alters the isotopic composition of precipitation more strongly than temperature, vegetation or prior calcite precipitation.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which intra‑seasonal mode, besides the Madden‑Julian Oscillation, is known to influence monsoon break spells?
questions.solution: The lesson lists a common trap: attributing monsoon break spells solely to the MJO while ignoring the quasi‑biweekly Rossby wave mode. ENSO and IOD are interannual phenomena, not intra‑seasonal, and the MJO is already mentioned as the primary mode, so the additional intra‑seasonal driver is the quasi‑biweekly Rossby wave.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Bruun rule for shoreline retreat is least reliable when applied to coasts that have:
questions.a: Significant sediment supply or engineered structures
opts: Significant sediment supply or engineered structures
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly warns against uncritical application of the Bruun rule to coasts with significant sediment supply or engineered structures, because the rule assumes a closed sediment budget and simple profile translation. Low wave energy, uniform sandy beaches, and minimal tidal range are conditions where the rule performs better.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the spatial pattern of Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA)?
questions.a: Spatially variable with uplift in formerly glaciated areas and subsidence in peripheral forebulge regions
opts: Spatially variable with uplift in formerly glaciated areas and subsidence in peripheral forebulge regions
questions.solution: The lesson explains that GIA is a spatially variable field: formerly glaciated regions (e.g., Hudson Bay) experience uplift of 8–10 mm yr⁻¹, while the peripheral forebulge (e.g., U.S. Atlantic coast) subsides at 1–2 mm yr⁻¹. It is not uniform globally, nor confined to polar uplift only.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which combination of sediment calibre and bank cohesion favours the development of braided river channels?
questions.solution: Braided channels form where sediment supply is high relative to transport capacity, typically in steep, glacially fed valleys with abundant coarse bed material (gravel to cobbles) and non‑cohesive banks. The coarse sediment provides high bed‑load transport, while the lack of bank cohesion allows the channel to split into multiple threads around transient bars. Fine sediment and cohesive banks instead promote meandering or anastomosing planforms. Therefore, coarse sediment with non‑cohesive banks is the correct controlling combination.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In speleogenesis, vadose canyon enlargement occurs under which hydrogeological condition?
questions.a: Partially air‑filled conduits with free‑surface flow
opts: Fully water‑filled conduits under phreatic conditions
Partially air‑filled conduits with free‑surface flow
Deep confined aquifers with high pressure
questions.solution: Vadose zone processes operate where the conduit is not completely saturated; air occupies part of the void and water flows as a free‑surface stream. This allows mechanical erosion and dissolution to enlarge the conduit into a canyon‑shaped passage. In contrast, phreatic tube development occurs in fully water‑filled, pressurised conduits where dissolution is uniform around the perimeter. Deep confined aquifers and surface rainfall alone do not define the vadose canyon mechanism.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Solifluction rates vary exponentially with which two primary factors?
questions.solution: The lesson states that solifluction rates vary exponentially with active‑layer thickness and slope angle. A thicker active layer provides more mobile material, while steeper slopes increase the gravitational driving stress, both accelerating downslope flow. Vegetation, snow depth, soil moisture, grain size, temperature range, and precipitation influence periglacial processes but are not identified as the exponential controls on solifluction velocity.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In the upwelling velocity formula w ≈ (1/ρf) ∂τ/∂x, which symbol represents the Coriolis parameter?
questions.solution: The formula given is w ≈ (1/ρf) ∂τ/∂x, where ρ is seawater density, τ is the alongshore wind stress, x is the cross‑shore coordinate, and f is the Coriolis parameter. The Coriolis parameter appears in the denominator multiplied by density, controlling the magnitude of the Ekman transport and thus the upwelling velocity. Therefore, the symbol f corresponds to the Coriolis parameter.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In the context of Glacial Isostatic Adjustment, what is the typical relative sea‑level change observed near the former centre of a large ice sheet?
opts: Highly variable with no consistent pattern
questions.solution: During deglaciation the crust beneath the former ice centre rebounds upward at rates of 1–10 mm yr⁻¹. This uplift outpaces the global mean sea‑level rise, so the sea surface relative to the land falls. The lesson explicitly states that near the former ice centre uplift outpaces global mean sea‑level rise, producing a relative sea‑level fall. Therefore the correct description is a relative sea‑level fall.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The source‑to‑sink framework for a river basin quantifies which set of processes as fluxes?
questions.solution: The lesson defines the source‑to‑sink system as treating the basin as a conveyor belt where erosion, transport, storage, and deposition are quantified as fluxes. This comprehensive view integrates all four components, not just a single process. Hence the correct answer includes all four fluxes.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is the consequence of using coarse‑resolution ocean models without eddy parameterisation for poleward heat transport in the Southern Ocean?
opts: Accurate simulation of poleward heat transport
No impact on poleward heat transport
questions.solution: The lesson lists a common error: using coarse‑resolution ocean models without eddy parameterisation leads to underestimation of poleward heat transport in the Southern Ocean. Mesoscale eddies play a major role in moving heat poleward; omitting them reduces the simulated transport. Thus the correct outcome is an underestimation.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which permafrost process can mobilise deep, carbon‑rich yedoma deposits on decadal timescales and potentially double the carbon feedback relative to gradual active‑layer deepening?
questions.a: Abrupt thaw processes such as thermokarst lake formation
opts: Abrupt thaw processes such as thermokarst lake formation
questions.solution: The lesson states that abrupt thaw processes — thermokarst lake formation, retrogressive thaw slumps, and coastal erosion — can mobilise deep, carbon‑rich yedoma deposits (up to 50 m thick) on decadal timescales. Remote sensing and field data indicate abrupt thaw could double the permafrost carbon feedback by 2100 compared with gradual active‑layer deepening alone. Hence the correct process is abrupt thaw.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In the Himalayan orogen, which process is the dominant mechanism for crustal thickening?
questions.solution: The lesson states that in the Himalaya thrust stacking dominates, with the Main Central Thrust and Main Boundary Thrust accommodating >2000 km of convergence since the Eocene, whereas magmatic addition contributes only ~30% in the Andes. Thus, crustal shortening by thrust stacking is the primary thickening mechanism in the Himalaya.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which thermochronometer has a closure temperature of approximately 70°C?
questions.solution: The text lists closure temperatures: apatite (U‑Th)/He ~70°C, zircon (U‑Th)/He ~180°C, and ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar on muscovite ~350°C. Apatite fission‑track ages are mentioned for the Alps but its closure temperature is not given as 70°C. Hence, apatite (U‑Th)/He is the correct choice.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What primarily drives the exchange flux between surface water and groundwater in the hyporheic zone?
questions.a: Stream‑bed topography such as pool‑riffle sequences creating pressure gradients.
opts: Stream‑bed topography such as pool‑riffle sequences creating pressure gradients.
Temperature differences between stream and sediment.
Root water uptake by riparian vegetation.
questions.solution: The text explains that stream‑bed topography (pool‑riffle sequences) generates pressure gradients that drive downwelling in riffles and upwelling in pools, controlling the exchange flux q. While hydraulic conductivity contrasts modulate the flux, the primary driver is the bedform‑induced pressure gradient. Hence, option B is correct.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What does the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantee to each rural household per year?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment per household per year, providing a safety net against seasonal unemployment and creating rural assets. The other figures are not mentioned in the text.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which constitutional articles were interpreted by the Supreme Court to include a citizen's right to information, forming the constitutional basis for transparency?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that the Constitution enshrines transparency through Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression) and Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty), and that the Supreme Court in Union of India v. N. S. Raghavan (1995) interpreted these provisions to include a citizen's right to information. The other article pairs are not referenced for this purpose.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which e‑governance initiative is credited with the digitisation of land records, thereby reducing disputes over land ownership that disproportionately affect tribal and Dalit communities?
opts: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
questions.solution: The lesson states that the digitisation of land records via the Digital India platform reduces disputes over land ownership, which disproportionately affect tribal and Dalit communities. PMJDY, PMUY and MGNREGA are welfare schemes, not the e‑governance platform responsible for land‑record digitisation.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is created by the integration of Aadhaar with Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) that can be examined through RTI requests?
opts: A mandatory biometric verification for all schemes
questions.solution: The lesson explains that integrating Aadhaar with DBT not only streamlines fund flow but also creates an audit trail that can be examined through RTI requests. The other options either overstate the effect (elimination of all leakages) or describe only a part of the mechanism without mentioning the audit trail.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), 2005, which of the following statements accurately describes the statutory social audit process?
questions.a: It is mandated under Section 17 to be conducted at least once every six months by an independent Social Audit Unit, with the process driven by the Gram Sabha.
opts: It is conducted by the Block Development Officer on a quarterly basis and reported to the Zila Parishad.
It is mandated under Section 17 to be conducted at least once every six months by an independent Social Audit Unit, with the process driven by the Gram Sabha.
It is an internal departmental inspection carried out by the District Programme Coordinator to verify muster rolls and wage payments.
It is a voluntary community exercise facilitated by NGOs, with findings submitted to the State Employment Guarantee Council for advisory action.
questions.solution: The lesson states that Section 17 of MGNREGA mandates a social audit of all works in a Gram Panchayat at least once every six months. The audit is conducted by an independent Social Audit Unit (SAU) constituted by the state government, but the process is driven by the Gram Sabha, which examines muster rolls, measurement books, wage payment records, and asset registers. Option A is incorrect because it describes a quarterly internal audit by a BDO, not the statutory SAU/Gram Sabha process. Option C incorrectly characterizes it as an internal departmental inspection by the District Programme Coordinator; the Coordinator only initiates a formal inquiry after irregularities are found. Option D is wrong because social audit is statutory, not voluntary, and findings go to the Gram Sabha, not an advisory council.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: According to the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, as operationalised in 2019, and the Lokpal Rules, 2020, which of the following is a correct procedural requirement for a citizen approaching the Lokpal?
questions.a: Prior representation to the competent authority is required before the Lokpal can entertain a complaint.
opts: A complaint can be filed directly with the Lokpal without any prior representation to the concerned department.
The Lokpal has jurisdiction over the Prime Minister without any safeguards or procedural restrictions.
Prior representation to the competent authority is required before the Lokpal can entertain a complaint.
The Lokpal can only inquire into allegations against Group A officers, excluding Ministers and Members of Parliament.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states in the 'Confusing...' section: 'Assuming Lokpal can be approached without exhausting departmental remedies — Lokpal Rules 2020 require prior representation to the competent authority.' This makes Option C correct. Option A contradicts this rule. Option B is incorrect because the text specifies the Lokpal has jurisdiction over the Prime Minister 'with safeguards'. Option D is wrong because the text lists the Lokpal's jurisdiction as covering the Prime Minister, Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Group A-D officers.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes Outcome Budgeting from traditional plan outlay-based budgeting in the context of Public Financial Management for Social Justice?
questions.a: Outcome Budgeting demands measurable output and outcome indicators linked to quarterly reporting through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).
opts: Outcome Budgeting merely re-labels plan outlays with new nomenclature while retaining the same financial heads.
Outcome Budgeting focuses exclusively on reducing fiscal deficit by capping expenditure on social sector schemes.
Outcome Budgeting demands measurable output and outcome indicators linked to quarterly reporting through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).
Outcome Budgeting replaces the Comptroller and Auditor General's (CAG) audit role with internal ministry-level performance reviews.
questions.solution: The lesson states in the 'Confusing...' section: 'Treating outcome budgeting as mere re‑labeling of plan outlays — it demands measurable output/outcome indicators and quarterly PFMS reporting.' This directly supports Option C. Option A describes the misconception that the lesson warns against. Option B is incorrect because outcome budgeting is about performance measurement, not fiscal deficit reduction through expenditure caps. Option D is wrong because the lesson notes the CAG's performance audits shape outcome-budget reforms ('Neglecting the role of the CAG's performance audits in shaping outcome‑budget reforms'), not that outcome budgeting replaces the CAG.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Regarding the Aadhaar-enabled delivery model for welfare schemes, what is the correct legal position following the Supreme Court's 2018 judgment?
questions.a: Aadhaar authentication can be made compulsory only for schemes backed by a specific law enacted by Parliament.
opts: Aadhaar authentication is mandatory for all central and state welfare schemes to prevent duplication.
Aadhaar authentication can be made compulsory only for schemes backed by a specific law enacted by Parliament.
Aadhaar linking is voluntary for all schemes, and no beneficiary can be denied benefits for non-enrolment.
The Supreme Court struck down the Aadhaar Act, 2016, rendering all Aadhaar-based authentication illegal.
questions.solution: The lesson states in the 'Confusing...' section: 'Believing Aadhaar authentication is mandatory for all welfare schemes — the 2018 Supreme Court ruling limits compulsory linking to schemes backed by law.' This matches Option B. Option A is the misconception the lesson identifies. Option C is incorrect because the ruling allows compulsory linking for schemes backed by law, so it is not universally voluntary. Option D is factually wrong; the Supreme Court upheld the Aadhaar Act, 2016, with certain limitations, but did not strike it down entirely.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is the maximum percentage of the approved outlay that states may re‑allocate across components within the same Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the flexi‑fund provision without prior central approval?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the flexi‑fund component introduced in 2017 allows states to re‑allocate up to 25 % of the approved outlay across components within the same scheme without prior central approval. This flexibility is intended to accommodate local contextual variations. The other percentages (10 %, 15 %, 30 %) are not mentioned in the text. Therefore, the correct answer is 25 %.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which institution coordinates the quarterly outcome monitoring of Centrally Sponsored Schemes through State Performance Audit Units (SPAUs)?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) under NITI Aayog coordinates quarterly outcome monitoring of CSS through State Performance Audit Units (SPAUs). The CAG conducts performance audits, the Finance Commission recommends devolution, and the Ministry of Finance issues CSS guidelines, but the specific quarterly monitoring coordination role belongs to DMEO.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: How does the Deprivation Index (DI) used for intersectional targeting differ from the older Below Poverty Line (BPL) list?
opts: DI uses a single income threshold
DI is based solely on caste
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly warns against confusing the Deprivation Index with the older BPL list, noting that the DI is a multi‑dimensional score, not a binary classification. The BPL list relied on a single income/consumption threshold, whereas the DI incorporates several deprivation dimensions (e.g., health, education, housing) to capture intersectional vulnerabilities. Hence, the correct distinction is that DI is a multi‑dimensional score.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA), what is the primary function of the Consent Manager?
questions.a: Logs consent artefacts for data sharing
opts: Logs consent artefacts for data sharing
questions.solution: The lesson highlights that overlooking the role of the Consent Manager in DEPA leads to violations of the proportionality test because data sharing without a logged consent artefact is not permitted. The Consent Manager’s role is to record and manage user consent for each data‑sharing transaction, ensuring that consent is explicit, auditable, and revocable. It does not store data centrally, perform Aadhaar authentication, or issue digital signatures.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is a mandatory prerequisite for Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and ASHAs to receive their annual performance‑linked honorarium increment?
questions.a: Completion of Foundation Course and at least eight refresher webinars per year
opts: Completion of Foundation Course and at least eight refresher webinars per year
Submission of monthly service delivery reports
questions.solution: The lesson states that completion of the Foundation Course and at least eight refresher webinars per year is a prerequisite for the annual performance‑linked honorarium increment (₹500 for AWWs, ₹300 for ASHAs). While VHSNC attendance, report submission, and smartphone possession are part of the accountability framework, they are not listed as the specific prerequisite for the honorarium increment.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General's 2015 performance audit of MGNREGS (Report No. 12 of 2015) recommended the institutionalisation of which mechanism to address the finding that social audit findings were rarely fed back into the planning cycle?
questions.solution: The 2015 CAG performance audit of MGNREGS (Report No. 12 of 2015) found that only 38% of Gram Panchayats conducted social audits within the statutory 90-day window and that findings were rarely fed back into planning. The CAG recommended institutionalising a Social Audit Action Taken Report (SAATR) to close this accountability loop. The Ministry of Rural Development adopted this recommendation in 2017, making the SAATR a prerequisite for the release of the second tranche of funds. NeFMS relates to wage payments, ONORC to PDS portability, and OOMF to CSS monitoring.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Under the One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) scheme, which of the following is a mandatory prerequisite for a beneficiary to access portability benefits across State borders?
questions.a: Aadhaar seeding and onboarding of both home and host States
opts: Enrollment in the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin
Completion of social audit in the home Gram Panchayat
Aadhaar seeding and onboarding of both home and host States
Possession of a job card under MGNREGS
questions.solution: The ONORC scheme, launched nationally on 1 June 2020 under the NFSA, enables ration card portability for migrant workers. However, the lesson explicitly states that assuming portability is automatic is a misconception; Aadhaar seeding of the beneficiary's ration card and the onboarding of both the home and host States onto the central portal are mandatory technical prerequisites for the system to authenticate and record the transaction. Options A, B, and D refer to unrelated schemes or processes.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: What is the consequence for a State that fails to report data on the Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework (OOMF) for two consecutive quarters under a Centrally Sponsored Scheme?
questions.a: The central share for the subsequent quarter is withheld until compliance (fund-hold)
opts: The State's share in vertical devolution is permanently reduced by 1%
The central share for the subsequent quarter is withheld until compliance (fund-hold)
The scheme is converted from a 'core' to an 'optional' CSS for that State
The State is barred from accessing the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Expenditure
questions.solution: The Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework (OOMF), introduced by the Ministry of Finance in 2021, mandates quarterly reporting of output and outcome indicators on the PFMS and DM-CSS dashboards. The lesson explicitly states that States failing to report for two consecutive quarters face a 'fund-hold', where the central share for the subsequent quarter is withheld until compliance is achieved. This was evidenced in 2023 when five States experienced fund-holds under the National Health Mission due to delayed HMIS reporting. The other options describe consequences not mentioned in the text.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The 2022 Guidelines for Social Registry Data Quality issued by the Department of Rural Development mandate a minimum match rate between Aadhaar-seeded records and field-verified household surveys before a scheme can draw down funds. What is this prescribed minimum match rate?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states: "The 2022 'Guidelines for Social Registry Data Quality' issued by the Department of Rural Development require a minimum 95 % match rate between Aadhaar-seeded records and field-verified household surveys before a scheme can draw down funds." This is a specific factual detail from the Unified Social Registry section. Options A, B, and D are incorrect percentages not mentioned in the text.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the evolution of performance budgeting in India, which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Outcome Budget (2005-06) from the Performance Budget (2017-18)?
questions.a: Outcome Budget linked funds to results; Performance Budget added quarterly physical-financial reviews with Ministry of Finance, NITI Aayog's DMEO, and CAG.
opts: Outcome Budget introduced quarterly physical-financial reviews; Performance Budget linked funds to results for the first time.
Outcome Budget linked funds to results; Performance Budget added quarterly physical-financial reviews with Ministry of Finance, NITI Aayog's DMEO, and CAG.
Performance Budget replaced the Outcome Budget and removed the requirement for SDG-linked indicators.
Outcome Budget mandated gender-disaggregated data; Performance Budget extended this to disability-disaggregated data only.
questions.solution: The text states: "Performance budgeting in India evolved from the traditional line-item 'Demand for Grants' to a results-oriented framework beginning with the Outcome Budget (2005-06), followed by the Performance Budget (2017-18) and the integration of the PFMS... The Outcome Budget obliges each ministry to map every CSS to a set of output indicators... and outcome indicators... The Performance Budget adds a quarterly 'Physical-Financial Review' where the Ministry of Finance, NITI Aayog's DMEO, and the CAG jointly assess variance against targets." Option B accurately captures this sequential evolution and distinction. Option A reverses the roles. Option C is incorrect as Performance Budget did not replace Outcome Budget. Option D misstates the annexure requirements.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The 2018 Supreme Court judgment in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India had a specific impact on the mandatory use of Aadhaar for welfare schemes. What was the Court's ruling regarding Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016?
questions.a: Read down Section 7 to require that any mandatory Aadhaar linkage must be backed by a parliamentary law.
opts: Struck down Section 7 entirely, prohibiting any mandatory Aadhaar linkage for welfare benefits.
Upheld Section 7 without modification, allowing mandatory Aadhaar for all central and state schemes.
Read down Section 7 to require that any mandatory Aadhaar linkage must be backed by a parliamentary law.
Delegated the authority to mandate Aadhaar linkage to the respective Ministry implementing the scheme.
questions.solution: The lesson states: "The 2018 Aadhaar judgment (Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India) struck down Section 57 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016, which permitted private entities to demand Aadhaar authentication, and read down Section 7 to require that any mandatory Aadhaar linkage be backed by a parliamentary law." Option C accurately reflects this 'reading down' of Section 7. Option A is incorrect as Section 7 was not struck down. Option B is incorrect as the Court imposed a condition (parliamentary law). Option D has no basis in the judgment described.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a performance audit from a compliance audit as described in the CAG's mandate?
questions.a: A performance audit evaluates outcomes against predefined indicators and assesses whether the programme design is fit for purpose.
opts: A compliance audit evaluates outcomes against predefined indicators such as person‑days generated or immunisation coverage.
A performance audit verifies adherence to rules, sanctions and procedures only.
A performance audit evaluates outcomes against predefined indicators and assesses whether the programme design is fit for purpose.
Both audits focus solely on financial regularity and do not examine programme outcomes.
questions.solution: The lesson states that a compliance audit verifies adherence to rules, sanctions and procedures, whereas a performance audit evaluates outcomes against predefined indicators — person‑days generated, calories delivered, immunisation coverage — and assesses whether the programme design itself is fit for purpose. Option C captures this distinction exactly. Options A and B reverse the roles, and option D incorrectly claims both audits ignore outcomes.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Under the One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) scheme, which set of technical and administrative requirements must be satisfied for a beneficiary to lift subsidised foodgrains from any Fair Price Shop in the country?
questions.a: Aadhaar seeding of the ration card, integration with the IM‑PDS platform, and functional POS devices at every FPS.
opts: Only a valid ration card issued by the home state.
Aadhaar seeding of the ration card, integration with the IM‑PDS platform, and functional POS devices at every FPS.
Registration on a central portal and approval from the Ministry of Consumer Affairs for each transaction.
A biometric verification at the home state FPS before any inter‑state purchase.
questions.solution: The lesson explains that ONORC operates on the Integrated Management of Public Distribution System (IM‑PDS) platform and requires the ration card to be seeded with Aadhaar, IM‑PDS integration across states, and functional point‑of‑sale (POS) devices at every Fair Price Shop. Option B lists all three mandatory conditions. Options A, C and D omit essential components or add non‑existent steps.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Behavioural Insights Team (BIT) – India, known as the Nudge Unit, was established under which institution and applies which analytical framework for redesigning citizen‑facing processes?
questions.a: NITI Aayog, using the EAST framework (Easy, Attractive, Social, Timely).
opts: Ministry of Finance, using the COM‑B model exclusively.
NITI Aayog, using the EAST framework (Easy, Attractive, Social, Timely).
Prime Minister’s Office, using nudge theory without a structured framework.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, using default enrolment as the sole tool.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Nudge Unit was set up under NITI Aayog in 2020 and applies the “EAST” framework — Easy, Attractive, Social, Timely — to redesign citizen‑facing processes. Option B matches both the institutional home and the framework. Options A, C and D incorrectly identify the parent body or the analytical tool.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the institutional mechanism introduced in 2016 to ensure that CAG performance audit findings inform policy decisions?
questions.a: The Ministry of Finance mandated a Performance Audit Action Taken Report (PAATR) within six months, aggregated by NITI Aayog's DMEO into a national dashboard.
opts: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) was given statutory powers to enforce CAG recommendations within a fixed timeline.
The Ministry of Finance mandated a Performance Audit Action Taken Report (PAATR) within six months, aggregated by NITI Aayog's DMEO into a national dashboard.
The CAG was authorised to directly modify scheme guidelines based on audit findings without executive approval.
A new Parliamentary Committee on Performance Audit was constituted to replace the PAC and COPU for centrally sponsored schemes.
questions.solution: The lesson states: "Since 2016, the Ministry of Finance has required all centrally sponsored schemes to submit a 'Performance Audit Action Taken Report' (PAATR) within six months of the CAG's final report. The NITI Aayog's 'Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO)' aggregates these PAATRs into a national dashboard, enabling cross-scheme comparative analysis." This matches option B. Option A is incorrect because PAC examines reports but does not have statutory enforcement powers over timelines. Option C is incorrect as CAG does not modify guidelines directly. Option D is incorrect as no such new committee replaced PAC/COPU.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which event in 1947 led to the creation of two sovereign states, India and Pakistan, and left a legacy of contested borders and competing national narratives in South Asia?
questions.solution: The lesson states that the modern map of South Asia emerged from the partition of British India in 1947, which created India and Pakistan and left contested borders, refugee flows, and competing narratives. The Independence Act was the legislative instrument, but the partition itself is the event described as creating the two states and the legacy. The accession of princely states added complexity later, and the Lahore Declaration occurred in 1999. Therefore, the correct answer is the Partition of British India.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which treaty governs the sharing of river waters between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly mentions that the core disputes between India and Pakistan centre on Kashmir, cross‑border terrorism, and water sharing under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960. The Simla Agreement dealt with bilateral relations after the 1971 war, the Lahore Declaration was a confidence‑building measure in 1999, and the Composite Dialogue was a broader negotiation framework. Hence, the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 is the correct treaty for water sharing.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: How many member states does BIMSTEC have, and which South Asian country is excluded from its membership compared to SAARC?
questions.solution: According to the lesson, SAARC has 8 member states including Pakistan, while BIMSTEC has 7 member states and excludes Pakistan. The comparison table in the text shows BIMSTEC's membership as 7 (excludes Pak). Therefore, the correct description is that BIMSTEC has 7 members and excludes Pakistan.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately describes the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR)?
questions.a: It is located in Gurugram and fuses AIS feeds, coastal radar chains, satellite imagery, and white-shipping agreements with over 20 partner nations.
opts: It was inaugurated in 2015 as part of the SAGAR doctrine implementation.
It is located in Gurugram and fuses AIS feeds, coastal radar chains, satellite imagery, and white-shipping agreements with over 20 partner nations.
It operates under the Indian Coast Guard and focuses exclusively on EEZ surveillance and search-and-rescue coordination.
It replaced the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) as the primary forum for littoral navy capacity building.
questions.solution: The lesson text explicitly states: "Domain awareness is anchored by the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC‑IOR), inaugurated in Gurugram in 2018. The centre fuses Automatic Identification System (AIS) feeds, coastal radar chains, satellite imagery, and white‑shipping agreements with over 20 partner nations to produce a near‑real‑time maritime picture." Option A is incorrect because IFC-IOR was inaugurated in 2018, not 2015. Option C is incorrect because IFC-IOR is a Navy-led domain awareness centre, not a Coast Guard entity focused exclusively on EEZ. Option D is incorrect because IONS continues as a separate forum for littoral navies, chaired by India in 2021-22.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: In the context of India's strategic autonomy and multi-alignment, which statement best reflects the current operationalisation of this policy?
questions.a: India simultaneously deepens ties with competing powers like the US, Russia, and China while avoiding binding alliances that constrain decision-making.
opts: India has formed a formal military alliance with the United States, Japan, and Australia through the Quad to counter China.
India avoids all engagement with competing powers to maintain complete independence in decision-making.
India simultaneously deepens ties with competing powers like the US, Russia, and China while avoiding binding alliances that constrain decision-making.
India has abandoned the Non-Aligned Movement principles and aligned exclusively with the Western bloc.
questions.solution: The lesson defines strategic autonomy as "the capacity to pursue national interests without external coercion" and states that in the contemporary multipolar order, "autonomy is operationalised through 'multi‑alignment': simultaneous deepening of ties with competing powers while avoiding binding alliances that could constrain decision‑making." Option A is incorrect because the Quad is described as a "consultative framework without mutual‑defence obligations," not a formal military alliance. Option B describes isolationism, which the lesson explicitly distinguishes from autonomy. Option D is incorrect as India maintains engagement with Russia (BRICS, SCO) and China (BRICS, SCO) alongside Western partnerships.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Regarding Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL), which of the following statements is correct?
questions.a: KABIL, a joint venture of three public-sector undertakings, has signed agreements for lithium exploration in Argentina and Australia.
opts: KABIL is a private-sector consortium formed to develop domestic rare-earth processing facilities in Gujarat.
KABIL, a joint venture of three public-sector undertakings, has signed agreements for lithium exploration in Argentina and Australia.
KABIL was established under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for advanced chemistry cell batteries.
KABIL's mandate is limited to recycling critical minerals from electronic waste within India.
questions.solution: The lesson states: "Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL), a joint venture of three public‑sector undertakings, was mandated to acquire overseas mineral assets. KABIL has signed agreements for lithium exploration in Argentina and Australia and is scouting assets in Chile and Bolivia." Option A is incorrect because KABIL is a public-sector joint venture focused on overseas acquisition, not domestic processing. Option C is incorrect because KABIL is separate from the PLI scheme for ACC batteries. Option D is incorrect because KABIL's mandate is overseas asset acquisition, not domestic e-waste recycling.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following accurately describes India's 'Vaccine Maitri' initiative during 2021?
questions.a: It supplied over 66 million doses to 95 countries through a mix of grants, commercial exports, and COVAX obligations between January and October 2021.
opts: It was exclusively a grant-based humanitarian programme supplying vaccines only to least-developed countries.
It supplied over 66 million doses to 95 countries through a mix of grants, commercial exports, and COVAX obligations between January and October 2021.
It was a Quad-led initiative where India manufactured vaccines funded by the US and distributed by Japan and Australia.
It replaced India's COVAX commitments and focused solely on commercial exports to generate revenue.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states: "Between January and October 2021, India supplied over 66 million doses to 95 countries under 'Vaccine Maitri' — a mix of grants, commercial exports, and COVAX obligations." Option A is incorrect because it was not exclusively grant-based nor limited to least-developed countries. Option C is incorrect because Vaccine Maitri was India's own initiative, not a Quad-led programme (the Quad Vaccine Partnership was a separate 2021 pledge for 1 billion doses by 2022). Option D is incorrect because Vaccine Maitri included COVAX obligations, not replaced them, and was not solely commercial.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: With reference to the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF), which statement correctly describes India's participation?
questions.a: India joined the supply-chain and clean-economy pillars but opted out of the trade pillar, citing concerns over labour and environmental standards.
opts: India joined all four IPEF pillars — trade, supply chains, clean economy, and fair economy — as a founding member.
India joined only the trade and fair economy pillars, opting out of supply chains and clean economy due to sovereignty concerns.
India joined the supply-chain and clean-economy pillars but opted out of the trade pillar, citing concerns over labour and environmental standards.
India declined to join IPEF entirely, preferring to focus on the Quad and I2U2 for economic cooperation.
questions.solution: The lesson states: "IPEF, launched by the United States in May 2022 with 14 initial partners (including India), comprises four pillars: trade, supply chains, clean economy, and fair economy. India joined the supply‑chain and clean‑economy pillars but opted out of the trade pillar, citing concerns over labour and environmental standards that could constrain policy space." Option A is incorrect because India did not join the trade pillar. Option B reverses the pillars India joined and opted out of. Option D is incorrect because India is a founding partner of IPEF and participates in two pillars.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides a fast-track naturalisation path for which specific group?
questions.a: Non-Muslim minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India before 31 December 2014
opts: All refugees residing in India regardless of nationality or religion
Non-Muslim minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India before 31 December 2014
Rohingya refugees from Myanmar registered with UNHCR
Sri Lankan Tamil refugees housed in camps in Tamil Nadu
questions.solution: The lesson states: 'The 2019 Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) provides a fast‑track naturalisation path for non‑Muslim minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India before 31 December 2014.' It further clarifies a misconception: 'Assuming the Citizenship (Amendment) Act applies uniformly to all refugees — it targets specific religious minorities from three neighbouring countries and excludes others such as Rohingya.' Option B matches the textual description precisely. Option A is incorrect due to the religious and country-specific criteria. Option C is incorrect as Rohingya are explicitly excluded. Option D is incorrect as Sri Lankan Tamils are not covered under CAA.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: As of March 2024, what is the cumulative value of India’s Lines of Credit (LoCs) extended to African countries?
questions.solution: The lesson states that "as of March 2024, cumulative LoCs to Africa exceed $12 billion, financing projects in railways (Ethiopia‑Djibouti line), power (Kenya’s Olkaria geothermal expansion), and water (Tanzania’s Lake Victoria sanitation)." The $5 billion figure corresponds to the 2008 summit pledge, $10 billion to the 2011 summit doubling, and $15 billion is not mentioned. Therefore, the correct cumulative figure is the one exceeding $12 billion.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which statement accurately describes India’s status in the Arctic Council?
questions.a: India holds observer status and cannot vote in Council decisions
opts: India is a full member with voting rights
India holds observer status and cannot vote in Council decisions
India is a founding member of the Arctic Council
India has been granted permanent participant status
questions.solution: The text explicitly notes that India has "observer status" in the Arctic Council and adds a caution: "Treating India’s Arctic observer status as full membership; observers cannot vote in Arctic Council decisions." India is not a founding member (the Council was established in 1996 by the eight Arctic states) nor a permanent participant (a category reserved for indigenous peoples’ organisations). Hence, the only accurate description is that India holds observer status without voting rights.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: As of 2024, which of the following countries have live UPI integrations with India?
questions.a: Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France (pilot), UAE (pilot)
opts: Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France (pilot), UAE (pilot)
South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt, Ghana
Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Canada
questions.solution: The lesson states: "Overstating UPI’s global adoption — only Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France (pilot), and UAE (pilot) have live integrations as of 2024." The other groups list countries that have not been mentioned as having live UPI linkages. Therefore, the correct set of countries with live UPI integrations is the first option.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The BrahMos supersonic cruise missile deal with the Philippines, signed in January 2022, was financed through:
questions.a: A commercial contract financed by the Philippine defence budget allocation
opts: A government‑to‑government concessional loan from India
A commercial contract financed by the Philippine defence budget allocation
A grant under the Indian Defence Export Promotion Policy
questions.solution: The text clarifies: "Believing the BrahMos export to the Philippines with a government‑to‑government loan; it was a commercial contract financed through a Philippine defence budget allocation." The deal, valued at $375 million, was a straight commercial sale, not a concessional loan, grant, or multilateral financing. Hence, the financing mechanism was a commercial contract paid from the Philippines’ own defence budget.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The official nuclear doctrine of India, approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security on 4 January 2003, is based on which two pillars?
questions.solution: The 2003 official nuclear doctrine enshrines two pillars: a No-First-Use (NFU) pledge and Credible Minimum Deterrence (CMD). NFU commits India to not use nuclear weapons first but to retaliate massively if attacked. CMD defines the arsenal size as the minimum needed to inflict unacceptable damage. Option A incorrectly substitutes 'Massive Retaliation' as a separate pillar rather than a consequence of NFU. Options C and D describe concepts not part of the 2003 doctrine.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: At COP27 in Sharm El-Sheikh (2022), India co-sponsored the decision to establish a Loss and Damage Fund and insisted that contributions be sourced from:
opts: Private sector investments and carbon markets
The Green Climate Fund's existing corpus
Voluntary contributions from all UNFCCC parties
questions.solution: The lesson states that at COP27, India insisted that contributions to the Loss and Damage Fund be "new and additional" and sourced from developed-country public finance. This reflects the CBDR-RC principle. The Loss and Damage Fund and the Green Climate Fund are distinct financial mechanisms with separate governance (as noted in the common errors section). Options A, C, and D do not match India's stated negotiating position.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: India joined the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF) in May 2022 as a partner in which pillars?
opts: All four pillars including the Trade pillar
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly states that India joined IPEF as a partner in the Supply-Chain, Clean-Energy, and Tax-Anti-Corruption pillars, but opted out of the Trade pillar to retain tariff autonomy. The Fair-Economy pillar corresponds to the Tax-Anti-Corruption pillar mentioned in the text. Option B correctly identifies the three pillars India joined. Option A and D incorrectly include the Trade pillar. Option C is incomplete.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The 2019 Mission Shakti Anti-Satellite (ASAT) demonstration by India:
questions.a: Was conducted in low Earth orbit to minimise long-lived debris
opts: Violated the Outer Space Treaty's prohibition on weapons in orbit
Targeted a satellite in geostationary orbit at 36,000 km altitude
Was conducted in low Earth orbit to minimise long-lived debris
Resulted in India's suspension from the Missile Technology Control Regime
questions.solution: The lesson clarifies that the Outer Space Treaty bans weapons of mass destruction in orbit, not kinetic ASAT tests, though debris mitigation obligations apply. Mission Shakti was conducted in low Earth orbit (LEO) to minimise long-lived debris. The test did not violate the Outer Space Treaty (Option A is a common error noted in the text). India joined MTCR in 2016 and was not suspended (Option D). The target was in LEO, not geostationary orbit (Option B).
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: India withdrew from the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) negotiations in 2019 primarily due to:
questions.a: Inadequate market access for services, non-tariff barriers, and concerns over trade deficit with China
opts: Pressure from the United States to join the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework instead
Inadequate market access for services, non-tariff barriers, and concerns over trade deficit with China
Domestic opposition from agricultural lobbies regarding dairy and plantation crop imports
Failure to secure special and differential treatment provisions for developing countries
questions.solution: The lesson states India opted out of RCEP citing "inadequate market access for services, non-tariff barriers, and concerns over a widening trade deficit with China." This decision reflected a "look-before-you-leap" approach prioritising domestic manufacturing under Atmanirbhar Bharat. Option A is incorrect as IPEF was launched in 2022, after RCEP withdrawal. Option C mentions specific sectoral concerns not highlighted as the primary rationale in the text. Option D is not mentioned as a key factor.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was decisive because it enabled the East India Company to obtain which specific right in 1765 that transformed it from a commercial body into a territorial power?
questions.a: B) The Diwani (revenue-collecting rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
opts: A) The right to maintain a standing army in Bengal
B) The Diwani (revenue-collecting rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
C) The Nizamat (judicial and police functions) of Bengal
D) The exclusive right to trade with China via Bengal
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Battle of Plassey 'opened the door for the Company to acquire the diwani, or revenue-collecting rights, of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in 1765' and that 'this grant transformed the Company from a commercial enterprise into a territorial power because it now controlled the fiscal resources of one of the richest provinces'. Option A is incorrect because the Company already maintained sepoys before 1765. Option C (Nizamat) was acquired later, in 1772. Option D is factually wrong; the China trade was financed by Bengal revenue but not a direct grant from Plassey.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following was a direct institutional outcome of the Regulating Act of 1773?
questions.a: B) Establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta with jurisdiction over British subjects and certain Indian civil matters
opts: A) Creation of the post of Governor-General of India with authority over all presidencies
B) Establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta with jurisdiction over British subjects and certain Indian civil matters
C) Abolition of the East India Company's trade monopoly with China
D) Introduction of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal
questions.solution: The text explicitly states: 'Parliament's Regulating Act of 1773 ... created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, vested in Warren Hastings, and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta with jurisdiction over British subjects and, controversially, over Indians in certain civil matters.' Option A is incorrect because the Act created Governor-General of Bengal, not of India (that came in 1833). Option C occurred via the Charter Act of 1813. Option D (Permanent Settlement) was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793, twenty years later.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Revolt of 1857 led directly to which constitutional change in the governance of India?
questions.a: A) The enactment of the Government of India Act, 1858, which transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown
opts: A) The enactment of the Government of India Act, 1858, which transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown
B) The introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1861, establishing legislative councils with Indian members
C) The proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India in 1876
D) The formation of the Indian National Congress in 1885
questions.solution: Section 2.4 is titled 'Consequences: End of Company Rule and the Proclamation of 1858'. The lesson states: 'The war's end in 1845... forced the British to negotiate a transfer of power, culminating in the Cabinet Mission of 1946' but earlier in 2.4: 'Consequences: End of Company Rule and the Proclamation of 1858'. The Government of India Act 1858 was the legislative instrument that ended Company rule and vested governance in the Crown. Option B (1861 Act) was a later reform. Option C (Empress of India) occurred in 1876. Option D (INC) was founded in 1885, partly as a consequence of the post-1857 political vacuum but not a direct constitutional change.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed a three-tier constitutional structure for India. What was the specific composition of the 'weak centre' at the top tier?
questions.a: B) Defence, Foreign Affairs, and Communications only
opts: A) Defence, Foreign Affairs, Communications, and Finance
B) Defence, Foreign Affairs, and Communications only
C) Defence, Foreign Affairs, Communications, and Currency
D) All residuary powers vested in the Centre
questions.solution: Section 5.1 states the Cabinet Mission proposed 'a weak centre handling defence, foreign affairs and communications'. This is a precise factual recall. Option A adds Finance, which was not listed. Option C adds Currency. Option D describes a strong federal centre (like the Government of India Act 1935 or the eventual Constitution), the opposite of the 'weak centre' envisaged by the Mission to accommodate the Muslim League's demand for autonomy. The groups of provinces (Group A, B, C) were to possess all other powers.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Morley‑Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909) is correct?
questions.a: Separate electorates were granted to Muslims for the first time by statute.
opts: The Act introduced universal adult franchise for provincial councils.
Separate electorates were granted to Muslims for the first time by statute.
The Viceroy’s Executive Council became responsible to the enlarged Imperial Legislative Council.
Elected members obtained the power to vote on the budget and initiate legislation.
questions.solution: The lesson states that the 1909 Act institutionalised the principle of separate electorates for Muslims, a concession after the Simla Deputation. The franchise remained extremely narrow (about one percent of adult males) and the executive remained unaccountable to the legislature; elected members could only discuss the budget and ask questions, not vote on supply or initiate legislation. Therefore, only the statement about separate electorates being granted by statute is accurate.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Under the dyarchy system introduced by the Government of India Act 1919, which subject was placed in the transferred list?
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly lists transferred subjects as education, public health, agriculture, and local self‑government, while reserved subjects comprised law and order, finance, land revenue, and irrigation. Hence, education is the only option that belongs to the transferred category.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Kakori Conspiracy of 1925 was carried out by which revolutionary organisation?
questions.solution: The text notes that the Kakori robbery was executed by the Hindustan Republican Association, which was the predecessor of the HSRA. The HSRA itself was formed later (1928) and was responsible for actions such as the Chittagong Armoury Raid. Therefore, the correct organisation is the Hindustan Republican Association.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following accurately describes the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of February 1946?
questions.a: It began on 18 February 1946 in Bombay and involved over 20,000 ratings.
opts: It was organised and led by the Indian National Congress.
It began on 18 February 1946 in Bombay and involved over 20,000 ratings.
The British government immediately conceded full independence after the mutiny.
The mutiny remained confined to the Bombay naval base and did not spread.
questions.solution: According to the lesson, the RIN mutiny started on 18 February 1946 at Bombay, spread to major ports, and saw participation of over 20,000 ratings with cross‑communal flag hoisting. It was a spontaneous rating‑led strike; Congress and the Muslim League urged surrender, and the strike ended on 23 February. The British response was limited concessions and threat of force, not immediate independence. Hence, only the second statement matches the factual account.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: The Instrument of Accession signed by princely state rulers transferred control of which three subjects to the Dominion of India?
opts: Finance, law and order, and irrigation
questions.solution: The lesson states that the Instrument of Accession was a legal document that transferred control of defence, external affairs, and communications to the Dominion of India while preserving the ruler’s internal autonomy. The other subject groups correspond to reserved or transferred subjects under dyarchy, not to the Instrument of Accession. Therefore, the correct trio is defence, external affairs, and communications.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes the Poona Pact (1932) from the Communal Award (1932) regarding political representation for the Depressed Classes?
questions.a: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates with reserved seats chosen via primary elections among Depressed Class voters, increasing the seats from 71 to 148 in provincial legislatures.
opts: The Communal Award provided for reserved seats within general electorates, while the Poona Pact introduced separate electorates.
The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates with reserved seats chosen via primary elections among Depressed Class voters, increasing the seats from 71 to 148 in provincial legislatures.
The Communal Award increased reserved seats to 148, while the Poona Pact reduced them to 71 to appease caste Hindu opinion.
Both the Award and the Pact provided for separate electorates, but the Pact extended the franchise to women in the Depressed Classes.
questions.solution: The Communal Award announced by Ramsay MacDonald granted separate electorates to Depressed Classes. Gandhi's fast led to the Poona Pact, which replaced separate electorates with reserved seats within general electorates. The Pact increased provincial reserved seats from 71 (Award) to 148 and introduced a two-tier election: primary election by Depressed Class voters only, final election by general electorate. Option A reverses the mechanisms. Option C reverses the seat numbers. Option D is factually incorrect as neither provided separate electorates for women specifically.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi described the Cripps Offer (1942) as a "post-dated cheque on a failing bank." Which feature of the offer primarily provoked this criticism?
questions.a: The retention of British control over defence and the Governor-General's veto during the war, with Dominion Status promised only after the war.
opts: The explicit acceptance of the demand for Pakistan through the opt-out clause for provinces.
The retention of British control over defence and the Governor-General's veto during the war, with Dominion Status promised only after the war.
The proposal for a Constituent Assembly elected solely by the Muslim League and princely states.
The immediate transfer of all portfolios except defence to Indian leaders in the Viceroy's Executive Council.
questions.solution: Gandhi's "post-dated cheque" metaphor targeted the deferred promise of Dominion Status (post-war) while the British retained effective control via the Governor-General's veto and defence portfolio during the war. The opt-out clause (Option A) was criticised for accepting the two-nation theory, but the "cheque" critique specifically addressed the lack of immediate power transfer. Option C is false; the Assembly was to be elected by provincial legislatures. Option D describes the 1945 Wavell Plan/Simla Conference proposal, not the Cripps Offer.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Regarding the Azad Hind Government proclaimed by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943, which statement is correct?
questions.a: It claimed sovereign governmental status, issuing its own currency, postage stamps, and establishing diplomatic relations with nine countries.
opts: It functioned solely as a military wing of the Japanese Imperial Army without independent sovereign attributes.
It claimed sovereign governmental status, issuing its own currency, postage stamps, and establishing diplomatic relations with nine countries.
It was recognised as the legitimate government of India by the Allied Powers, including the USA and USSR.
Its territorial jurisdiction was limited to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, which were renamed Shaheed and Swaraj.
questions.solution: The Azad Hind Government (Provisional Government of Free India) declared by Bose in Singapore claimed full sovereign status. It issued its own currency (Azad Hind Rupee), postage stamps, had a cabinet, and secured recognition from nine Axis-aligned nations (Japan, Germany, Italy, etc.). Option A is incorrect per the lesson's warning against assuming INA fought only under Japanese command. Option C is false; Allied powers did not recognise it. Option D is partially true regarding Andaman/Nicobar (renamed Shaheed/Swaraj) but incorrect in stating jurisdiction was *limited* to them; the government claimed authority over all India.
questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.q: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Drain of Wealth' theory, as presented in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901), argued that the drain constituted a specific proportion of India's national income. How did Naoroji characterize his own quantitative estimates of the drain?
questions.a: As deliberately illustrative approximations intended to demonstrate the principle, not exact audited figures.
opts: As precise, audited accounts derived from official British Parliamentary returns.
As deliberately illustrative approximations intended to demonstrate the principle, not exact audited figures.
As conservative underestimates later proven accurate by the Royal Commission on Indian Finance (1913).
As calculations verified by the Indian National Congress's own statistical department established in 1895.
questions.solution: The lesson explicitly warns against "Overstating the quantitative precision of the 'drain' calculations; Naoroji's estimates were deliberately illustrative, not audited accounts." Naoroji used the 'drain' concept as a political tool to expose exploitation, acknowledging the difficulty of exact measurement. He did not claim they were audited accounts (A), verified by a Congress statistical department (D - no such department existed then), or validated by the 1913 Commission (C - the Commission largely dismissed the drain theory).
questions.subject: General Awareness
